equip.cite: Accessory uses - setbacks (§ 13-610(b))
equip.text: "Setbacks. Accessory uses must comply with setback standards pertaining to the principal use unless specified in section 13-440."

equip.cite: All structures, including accessory (§ 13-440(b)(1))
equip.text: "The distances in Table 13-440A shall be the minimum setback for all above or below ground structures, including accessory structures, unless otherwise specifically provided in section 13-610. The setback providing the greatest distance from the road centerline shall be used."

equip.cite: Side/rear lot lines, all structures (§ 13-440(c)(1))
equip.text: "The setback distances in Tables 13-423A and 425A shall be the minimum setback distances from side and rear lot/parcel lines for all substantial above-ground structures, including accessory structures, and in or below ground structures."

equip.cite: Small accessory buildings in residential districts (§ 13-440(c)(2)a)
equip.text: "In residential zoning districts, accessory buildings of not more than 100 square feet shall be required to only observe a one-foot setback from lot lines, provided such building does not exceed ten feet in height. Accessory structures with reduced setbacks shall not be located within the front yard."

equip.cite: Underground storage tanks (§ 13-440(c)(2)c)
equip.text: "Underground storage tank setbacks shall be ten feet to any wall or surface of the tank, excluding piping. Front setback from a maintained road right-of-way may be administratively reduced by the development services director upon demonstration of good cause."

equip.cite: Swimming pools / spas and screen enclosures (§ 13-440(c)(2)b)
equip.text: "Setbacks shall be as for other above-ground structures, or five feet for the outermost structure, whichever is less, provided adjacent property is protected from damage due to excavation, etc."

equip.cite: Above-ground extensions of a building (§ 13-440(a)(3)b)
equip.text: "Measurement shall be to the nearest vertical wall or support of the building or structure, provided any above-ground extension of the building does not encroach into the required setback more than two feet, or onto adjoining property. Any above-ground encroachment of more than two feet into the required setback will require a compensating setback increase in the structure's wall or support."

equip.cite: On-site utilities as accessory use (§ 13-610(c)(1)e)
equip.text: "On-site utilities, including water and sewer facilities, serving only the project on which they are located" are specifically presumed to be accessory uses in all zoning districts.

equip.cite: Nonresidential lot abutting residential (§ 13-440(e)(2))
equip.text: "Whenever a lot in a nonresidential district has a common boundary line with a lot in a residential district, and the property line setback requirement applicable to the residential lot is greater than that applicable to the nonresidential lot, then the lot in the nonresidential district shall be required to observe the property line setback requirement applicable to the adjoining residential lot."

equip.cite: Permit exemption, accessory buildings with no HVAC (§ 13-312)
equip.text: Additions and accessory buildings meeting the setback requirements are exempt from a development permit only where they do "not contain electrical, plumbing or HVAC fixtures" and are not larger than 100 sq ft (R2M, R2C, R4M, R4C, R6M, R6C) or 200 sq ft (A10, A10C, RR5, RR5C, RR2.5, RR2.5C, RR1, RR1C).

equip.cite: searched — no such rule in this code
equip.text: The words generator, standby, emergency power, condenser, heat pump, LP-gas, 'mechanical equipment' and 'pool equipment' appear nowhere in this LDC as a placement or screening standard. 'Propane gas' appears only as a category in the Table 13-431A principal-use list. There is no generator-specific or A/C-specific encroachment, separation or screening section.

doral.source: Land Development Code (Subpart B), Chapter 53 Administration, Article II, Division 5, Sec. 53-127 'Zoning district development standards' - the two 'Development

gen.cite: Permanently installed stand-by generators - residential zones (Sec. 74-105 table, PDF p.958)
gen.text: "Permanently installed stand-by generators / Residential zones (A maximum of one generator may be permitted for a single-family residence, individual duplex unit or individual townhouse unit) (11) | Front - behind the front building line / Rear - Five feet / Interior side - 3 feet / Side Street - behind the side street building line".

gen.cite: Permanently installed stand-by generators - nonresidential zones (Sec. 74-105 table, PDF p.958)
gen.text: "Nonresidential zones | Permanent generator must comply with principal building setbacks, except that there shall be no spacing requirement from the principal building to the generator."

gen.cite: Generator note (11) to Sec. 74-105 (PDF p.959)
gen.text: "Permanently installed generators fueled by propane gas or natural gas not exceeding five feet in height from finished grade to the top of the generator shall be permitted as an accessory use in conjunction with a permitted residential use. Side street setback shall be behind the side street building line, unless completely screened from view by a wall or hedge. In no event shall a permanently installed generator be placed closer than ten feet to the side street property line. These requirements are in addition to all applicable county, state or federal requirements."

equip.cite: Air conditioning unit (Sec. 74-105 table)
equip.text: "Air conditioning unit | 3.5 feet into setback(1)" Note (1): "In no case shall the special setback exceed 50 percent of the minimum yard dimension."

equip.cite: Aboveground fuel storage tank (Sec. 74-105 table)
equip.text: "Fuel storage tank, aboveground(2)(7)(8) / Nonresidential zones | Ten feet from property line" Note (2): "Location within required yards permitted in rear and side yards only." Note (7): "Location within the required rear yard is prohibited on an atypical lot if structure is greater than four feet in height." Note (8): "Shall be screened properly from the right-of-way." The table prints no aboveground fuel storage tank setback for residential zones.

equip.cite: Purpose of the special setbacks (Sec. 74-104)
equip.text: "This section provides for specific accessory structures and architectural appurtenances and features to be located within required building setback areas. Recorded easements and required landscaped buffers shall supersede the minimum dimensions permitted by this section."

equip.cite: Storage building (Sec. 74-105 table)
equip.text: "Storage building(2)(7) / Residential uses (120 square feet or less) Five feet from property line / Residential uses (121 to 300 square feet) Seven and one-half feet from property line / Nonresidential uses (250 square feet or less) Ten feet from property line".

equip.cite: Renewable energy devices - ground installations (Sec. 74-66(13))
equip.text: "Ground installations shall comply with the site development criteria of the applicable zoning district except encroachment into side setback areas by up to 50 percent and rear setback to within five feet of the property line may be permitted if necessary upon approval of the planning and zoning director."

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment screening (Sec. 86-2(a), (b), PDF p.1151)
equip.text: "(a) Mechanical equipment shall be screened with either landscaping or wall. All wall mounted mechanic equipment must be painted to match the building and shall be placed on the side and/or rear of the building. Any mechanical equipment on the rooftop shall be screened from the right-of-way using architectural features such as parapets etc. Townhomes shall meet the provisions in this section. (b) All mechanical equipment for townhomes, surface and wall mounted, shall be placed on the side of the building which shall be screened with either landscaping or wall."

equip.cite: Rooftop mechanical equipment, Live Local Act qualifying developments (Sec. 68-994(1)(3))
equip.text: "Mechanical equipment. All rooftop mechanical equipment, including but not limited to heating, ventilating, air conditioning machinery, accessory communication equipment, public utility service fixtures, and elevator facilities shall be screened from the public view by a parapet wall or similar solid barrier as approved by the Planning and Zoning Director."

equip.cite: Ground equipment cabinets for antennas (Sec. 74 art. XI)
equip.text: "Self-standing, nonsheltered equipment cabinets used in conjunction with antenna support structures or antennas, if located on the ground shall be deemed mechanical equipment similar to air conditioning units and shall be limited to a height not to exceed eight feet and an area not to exceed 80 square feet. There shall be no minimum spacing between accessory wireless equipment buildings and the building located on the property."

equip.cite: Shading of A/C units (Chapter 71, landscaping, PDF p.931)
equip.text: "All exterior air conditioning units, except for air conditioning units placed on the roof, shall be shaded by trees and/or shrubs as referenced in the landscape manual."

equip.cite: Steady mechanical noise (Sec. 26-128(13))
equip.text: "Steady, mechanical noise. The use of an air conditioner, electric motor, pool pump, exhaust fan, filter, or similar noise-producing mechanical equipment which causes frequent, habitual or long continued noise which is plainly audible at a distance of 100 feet from the building, structure or property line in which the mechanical equipment is located." (a prohibited noise).

TND (house use).frontNote: Sec. 68-508(3)a: 'Buildings on house use lots shall be set back ten to 20 feet from the frontage line. Buildings at street intersections shall be set back ten feet from the frontage line and the side street frontage line.' This is a build-to band, not a single minimum.
TND (house use).sideNote: Sec. 68-508(3)d: 'Buildings on house use lots shall be set back from the side lot lines equivalent (in total) to no less than 20 percent of the width of the building lot. The entire setback may be allocated to one side. If buildings have a zero-foot setback on one side, a four-foot maintenance easement shall be provided on the adjacent lot.'
TND (house use).note: Traditional Neighborhood Development district, house use land-use category, Sec. 68-508. House use lots: minimum width 36 feet, maximum width 75 feet, minimum AVERAGE lot size 5,000 square feet (the code states an average, not a per-lot minimum). Maximum 30 percent of the gross area of the neighborhood proper. Outbuildings and front porches do not count in lot coverage.

TND (rowhouse use).frontNote: Sec. 68-507(3)d: 'Buildings on rowhouse use lots shall be set back from eight to 15 feet from the frontage line. Buildings at street intersections shall be set back eight feet from the frontage line and six feet from the side street line. Setback requirements shall apply to the enclosed portion of the buildings only.' A build-to band, not a single minimum.

lakeland.name: Lakeland
lakeland.source: Code of Ordinances of the City of Lakeland, Florida, Supplement No. 22 (April 2026), current through Ordinance No. 6121 enacted December 1, 2025. This document
lakeland.offsite: The zoning chapter is not in this jurisdiction's Municode document — the copy held here is a supplement or a stub. Nothing on this card is a setback for this jurisdiction; read the adopted code before siting anything.

equip.cite: No generator, A/C, condenser, pool equipment, LP-gas or mechanical-equipment placement rule exists in this document
equip.text: A full-text search of all 856 pages for generator, standby, emergency power, air conditioner/air conditioning, condenser, compressor, mechanical equipment, HVAC, heating and cooling, pool pump, pool equipment, propane, LP-gas, liquefied petroleum, fuel tank, aboveground storage tank and transformer returns no placement, setback, clearance or separation standard anywhere in the Code. The only hits are (a) the Chapter 18 business tax receipt fee schedule, which lists 'Mechanical contractor... Unlimited mechanical, air conditioning boilers, pressure vessels, lift station equipment, pressure and process piping, pneumatic control piping, gasoline tanks/pumps, chemical and fuel lines and related work... 127.50' and 'Class A air conditioning contractor... 127.50' and 'Class B air conditioning contractor... Limited to 25 tons cooling and 500,000 BTU heating... 127.50' (§ 18-67); (b) § 94-21's definition 'Gas includes natural gas, liquefied petroleum gas or manufactured gas', a utility-tax definition; (c) § 102-26's sewer definitions referring to 'air conditioners, refrigeration, cooling' as sources of non-contact cooling water and § 102-34(g)'s prohibition on connecting 'water-cooled air conditioning systems' to a building sewer; and (d) § 86-33(i) 'disposed of by the generator', where 'generator' means a waste producer, not a machine.

equip.cite: Noise Control exemptions (§ 70-48) — no standby-generator exemption
equip.text: 'The provisions of this article, except for those specific prohibitions set forth hereinabove, shall not apply to the following sounds: (1) The unamplified human voice; (2) Railway locomotives or cars; (3) Household or farming tools, appliances and equipment meeting manufacturer's specifications as to sound, if applicable; (4) Aircraft and airport activity conducted in accordance with federal laws and regulations; (5) Maintenance of public service facilities; (6) Law enforcement activities, including training; (7) Authorized target shooting; (8) Emergency signals during emergencies; (9) Emergency signal testing; (10) Motor vehicles operating on a public right-of-way subject to F.S. § 316.293; (11) Refuse collection and mosquito fogging; (12) Operation of any regulated utility; (13) Ordinary and customary construction activities exempt from or for which Lakeland has issued a development permit, provided such activity occurs between 7:00 a.m. and 9:00 p.m.; (14) Organized athletic contests; (15) Sounds relating to and originating within any area zoned for commercial use; (16) Sounds relating to and originating within any area zoned for industrial use; (17) Sounds relating to and originating from legal, pre-existing, nonconforming commercial and industrial activities; (18) Boats and boating activities; (19) Phosphate mining activity; (20) Emergency devices and vehicles used for the purpose of alerting persons of an emergency or the emission of sound in the performance of emergency work; (21) Lawful noncommercial public gatherings including, but not limited to, parades, festivals and school functions; (22) Reasonable operation of equipment associated with the following activities between one-half hour before sunrise and 10:00 p.m.: Lawn care; soil cultivation; maintenance of trees, hedges and gardens; the use of lawn mowers, saws and tractors; tree trimming and limb clipping. These exemptions do not apply to the specific prohibitions set forth in section 70-47, above.' (§ 70-48.) Unlike many Florida municipal noise ordinances, Lakeland's list does NOT name a standby or emergency electrical generator; the nearest categories are (3) household equipment meeting manufacturer's sound specifications and (20) emergency devices used in the performance of emergency work. Nothing here is a distance.

equip.cite: Vegetation clearance to electric wires (§ 38-57)
equip.text: 'Trees, etc., interfering with electric wires — Allowing to grow within five feet of electric wires.' This is the only clearance distance in the Code involving electrical equipment, and it governs vegetation, not generators or mechanical equipment.

equip.cite: Screening / buffering of a parked trailer (§ 66-7(f))
equip.text: Where the city commission permits a motor home, boat or trailer to be parked on a lot, it may impose conditions 'including without limitation a requirement for buffer fencing and noise mitigation measures.' No distance is printed.

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment - the governing rule
equip.text: Sec. 34-902, Yard restrictions - General, all districts, paragraph (3), quoted in full: 'Any mechanical equipment, excluding public utility fixtures, including telephone, telegraph, electric and water and sewer facilities, shall not be located in the front yard and shall be located a minimum of five feet from any side or rear property line. When a nonresidential or multifamily use is located adjacent to any residential use, then such mechanical equipment shall be located a minimum of ten feet from any property line. Notwithstanding the foregoing, fuel oil and propane tanks that are placed completely underground may be located in the front yard provided that they are in compliance with the most current Florida Building Code and National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) standards and requirements.' This is the clause that governs a standby generator pad, an A/C condenser and a pool pump: no front yard, 5 ft from any side or rear property line, 10 ft from any property line where a nonresidential or multifamily use adjoins a residential use, and an underground LP or fuel oil tank may sit in the front yard.

equip.cite: Where Sec. 34-902 does not apply
equip.text: Sec. 34-436 (HIST-S), Sec. 34-475 (HIST-Z) and Sec. 34-507 (HIST-B) each provide that 'Yard setback encroachments that may be authorized in sections 34-902 and 34-903 are expressly prohibited' in that historic preservation district. Whether that removes the mechanical-equipment allowance of Sec. 34-902(3) in those three districts, or only the projection allowances of Secs. 34-902(1), (2) and 34-903, is not settled on the page.

equip.cite: Restriction on use of required yards
equip.text: Sec. 34-901(a): 'Every part of a required front, side and rear yard must be open to the sky and unobstructed except for accessory buildings in a rear or side yard, garden walls and fences, as permitted, and except for the ordinary projection of open porches, balconies, steps, sills, belt courses, cornices. (See sections 34-902(1) and 34-903.)' Sec. 34-901(b): 'Metal storage accessory buildings shall be permitted only in the following zoning districts: CG commercial general, CO commercial office, UTL utility, RV Park recreational vehicle park, and MH manufactured home community. All metal storage buildings shall have skirting and landscaping around the entire base of the structure, except in the RV park and MH zoning districts, where only skirting shall be required if landscaping is not possible.'

equip.cite: Setback of accessory structures
equip.text: Sec. 34-873, in full: 'Accessory structures shall provide a minimum of ten feet from rear and side lot lines and shall be set back by the required front setback in the district which is applicable.' Note that this ten-foot figure is more restrictive than the five-foot mechanical-equipment figure of Sec. 34-902(3), and that several district tables print their own 'Minimum accessory structure setback' of 5 ft (RS, R-DUP, HIST-S, HIST-Z, HIST-B) with the footnote 'If accessory structure is in the front yard, the front yard setback shall apply.' The code does not say on the page which figure controls a generator enclosure, so both are recorded.

equip.cite: Swimming pools and pool equipment
equip.text: Sec. 34-871(a): 'Swimming pools shall be set back at least 15 feet from the front property line and five feet from the side and rear property lines measured to the water's edge. Swimming pools may be enclosed by screening in the side and rear yards, providing a minimum five-foot setback is provided from the side and rear property lines to the screen enclosure.' Sec. 34-871(b)(4), for zero lot line communities: 'Pools, fountains, hot tubs/whirlpools, etc., that have jets, blowers, waterfalls, mechanical equipment, or any other mechanisms that generate noise, must be completely sound-insulated from adjacent houses with a minimum two-inch thick urethane insulation or better against all surfaces within two feet of the zero line.' Sec. 34-871(c)(2), for individual townhouse lots: 'Pools, fountains, hot tubs/whirlpools, etc., that have jets, blowers, waterfalls, mechanical equipment, or any other mechanisms that generate noise, must be completely sound insulated from the adjacent property with a minimum two-inch thick urethane insulation or better around the noise generator within five feet of the property line.' Sec. 34-871(c)(3): 'A minimum five-foot-high wall or fence, consistent with the architecture of the building, shall be installed along the side property lines to screen the pool or hot tub/whirlpool from the adjacent properties.'

equip.cite: Fuel pumps and tanks at a fuel service station
equip.text: Sec. 34-869(g): 'All fuel pumps, tanks, vents, pump islands and pump island canopies shall conform to setback requirements for the district except that no such pumps, tanks, vents, pump islands or pump island canopies shall be located closer than 25 feet to any side property line.'

equip.cite: Private utility structures in the REC-PRIV district
equip.text: Sec. 34-752(b)(1): 'All private utility structures shall be required to be screened with landscaping or other appropriate material in order to be completely screened from view from all streets and adjacent properties. In addition, there shall be no noise, smell, or other nuisance generated from a private utility structure. All private utility structures, other than submersible wells which are no greater than 25 square feet in area and three feet in height, shall be located a minimum of 250 feet from the side and rear property lines, and a minimum 50 feet from the front property line.' Sec. 34-752(b)(2): 'Submersible wells no greater than 25 square feet in area and three feet in height shall be set back a minimum 15 feet from any property line.'

equip.cite: Air conditioning in the RV Park district
equip.text: Sec. 34-566 note (e): 'All accessory structures shall be freestanding structures, not permanently attached to the RV and must not protrude beyond the front corner of the RV walls; however, protrusion may occur between tip-outs. No plumbing, air conditioning unit or ducts are permitted within an accessory structure. Electricity, however, shall be permitted to serve an accessory structure. Accessory structures, other than storage buildings, are permitted only when an RV is located on the lot. When an RV is removed from a lot, all accessory structures, other than storage buildings and cooking/barbecue grill structures, must also be removed. A freestanding air conditioning unit shall be considered an accessory structure (see definition of accessory structure in section 34-4).' This is the one place in the code that says in terms that a free-standing mechanical unit is an accessory structure.

equip.cite: Generators in the general Code of Ordinances (not zoning)
equip.text: Sec. 12-118 (noise chapter), closing sentence: 'This article shall not prohibit the operation or periodic testing of emergency engines, generators and other equipment necessary to maintain or restore regulated public utilities service or other necessary public services.' Construction-site rule in the buildings chapter: 'The building official may issue a permit for the use of a portable generator for a period not to exceed four days provided the permit applicant provides proof that neither permanent nor temporary electrical power is available at the work location. The portable generator shall be operated only during the times for permissible construction activities as set forth in section 12-127 of this Code. No fee shall be required for the issuance of such a permit.' Neither is a setback.

lantana.source: Code of Ordinances Chapter 23 (Zoning), Article V District Regulations — Secs. 23-92 through 23-105. Each district carries its own '(e) Building requirements' b

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment in residential zoning districts (the governing rule)
equip.text: Sec. 23-81(k)(3), Projections into setback areas: '(3) Mechanical equipment in residential zoning districts. Mechanical equipment shall not be allowed within the required side setbacks for new construction in residential zoning districts, however existing mechanical equipment may be replaced in its existing location.'

equip.cite: Definition of 'mechanical equipment'
equip.text: Sec. 23-3 definitions: 'Mechanical equipment includes but is not limited to air conditioning compressors and condensers, heating-ventilation equipment, electrical transformers, and pool or spa equipment, ground-mounted, roof-mounted or on pads.' NOTE: the definition is open-ended ('includes but is not limited to') but does not name generators, standby power equipment, LP-gas tanks or propane tanks. I found no section of the Lantana code that sets a siting standard for a standby generator by name.

equip.cite: Accessory uses — location
equip.text: Sec. 23-81(c): 'Accessory uses in residential districts shall be constructed to conform with the building and site regulations in the district where the structure is to be located, provided, however, that all accessory uses shall be located only in the side or rear yard at least six (6) feet from the principal building.' Each district section also repeats, in its '(c) Accessory uses' subsection, 'Accessory uses shall not be located within any required yard setbacks' — except Sec. 23-100(c) (P district), which as printed reads 'Accessory uses shall be located within any required yard setbacks'.

equip.cite: Architectural features and chimneys — permitted projections
equip.text: Sec. 23-81(k)(1)-(2): '(1) Chimneys. Chimneys may project into side and rear yards a distance not to exceed 24 inches, provided that a clear space of not less than 96 inches is left between such projection and the Lot Line adjacent. (2) Architectural features. No main walls of any building shall encroach on the front, side or rear setback areas, but architectural features such as canopies, cantilever slab projections (open balconies), cornices and similar features may project into the front, side and rear setbacks not more than twenty-four (24) inches, and there shall be not less than seven feet of clear headroom under any such projection. Eaves may project into the setbacks not more than thirty-six (36) inches.'

equip.cite: Standby generator REQUIRED at service stations (C1 district)
equip.text: Sec. 23-96(d)(6), C1 commercial district special exceptions: '(6) Service stations, except in CC or OMX. All new service stations shall permanently install a standby electrical generator with sufficient capacity to power the entire service station facility, not including vehicle washing/cleaning equipment, such that the loss of commercially supplied electrical power shall not result in the loss of service. Additionally, if any existing service station facility is renovated, reconstructed or remodeled in any way, where the total combined cost exceeds fifty thousand dollars ($50,000.00) during any twelve-month period, such service station shall be required to install a permanent standby electrical generator, which satisfies the criteria listed hereinabove.' This is a requirement to install a generator, not a setback or siting standard.

equip.cite: Underground utility installation (R1A only)
equip.text: Sec. 23-81(m): 'Within the single-family residential zoning district of R1-A, at the time of construction of any new buildings or structures located on any privately-owned property, such buildings or structures shall have an entirely underground location for all utility service lines, electrical distribution systems, wires and cables, which connect to and service such buildings or structures. This section shall apply to all new utilities located within town or rights-of-way within the town, as well as in easements or on private properties, except for restoration of service under emergency conditions, e.g., following a hurricane or similar disaster that damages overhead utility facilities.'

equip.cite: Lot coverage — what counts
equip.text: Sec. 23-81(l): 'Lot coverage shall be calculated to include the footprint of all above-grade structures under roof, and all swimming pools excluding, patio areas unless a screen enclosure is provided.'

gen.cite: Generators, A/C and pool equipment — encroachment into a required setback (§ VII-1201(a)(7))
gen.text: "Window, wall-hung air-conditioning units and air-conditioning units installed at grade may project no more than three feet into any required setback in residential districts. Pool equipment and the screening wall for outdoor mechanical equipment, including, but not limited to, air-conditioning equipment and pool pumps required by subsection VI-102(u)(3) for single-family dwellings may project no more than 36 inches into any required sideyard setback. A generator at grade outside of Special Flood Hazard Areas or a generator elevated within Special Flood Hazard Areas may project no more than 36 inches into any required sideyard setback in residential districts."

gen.cite: Ground-mounted mechanical equipment, institutional uses in single-family and multiple family zones (§§ VI-204, VI-304)
gen.text: "Mechanical equipment. Mechanical equipment located on the ground, such as heating or cooling equipment, pumps, or generators shall be screened from the street and any abutting residentially zoned properties by walls, fences, or vegetation tall enough to screen the equipment. Mechanical equipment on roofs shall be screened from the ground level of any abutting residentially zoned properties." The same sections also provide: "Exterior storage. Exterior storage of materials and equipment is prohibited." (p.519).

gen.cite: Ground-mounted mechanical equipment, commercial, industrial, special purpose and mixed-use zones (§§ VI-503(i), VI-603(j), VI-703(i), VI-1005, VI-1103(g))
gen.text: "Mechanical equipment. Mechanical equipment, located on the ground, such as heating or cooling equipment, pumps, or generators must be screened from public streets and any adjacent properties. All rooftop mechanical equipment must be screened from the ground level of public streets and any adjacent properties by integrating it into building and roof design." (p.592, p.665, p.751).

equip.cite: General rule on required setbacks (§ VII-1201(a))
equip.text: "Encroachments into required setbacks. Every part of every required setback shall be open and unobstructed from the ground to the sky except as otherwise permitted by these regulations. Except for setbacks adjacent to the Gulf of Mexico, the following encroachments are permitted in all setbacks." The list that follows also allows: sills and belt courses 12 inches; movable awnings 3 ft (not more than half the setback where the setback is less than 5 ft wide); chimneys, bay windows or pilasters 2 ft; unroofed and unenclosed fire escapes and stairways 5 ft into a rear setback or 3 ft into a side setback of a multifamily dwelling, hotel or motel; hoods, canopies, roof overhangs or marquees 3 ft but no closer than one foot to the zoning lot line; cornices, eaves or gutters 3 ft (not more than half the setback where it is less than 6 ft wide); fences, walls, poles, posts and customary yard accessories in all yards except Gulf-front waterfront yards; and structures up to 30 inches above the general ground level in all yards except Gulf-front waterfront yards.

equip.cite: Outdoor mechanical equipment screening wall, single-family dwellings (§ VI-102(u)(3))
equip.text: "Outdoor mechanical equipment. Screening wall in the absence of perimeter fencing or mechanical equipment elevated above grade. Prior to the issuance of a building permit which includes the installation of new exterior mechanical equipment or the relocation of existing mechanical equipment in a side yard in the absence of perimeter fencing or when outdoor mechanical equipment is elected above grade, the applicant shall submit documentation demonstrating that a screening wall, or screening fence has been provided... showing all air conditioning equipment, pool pumps and similar electrical-mechanical equipment, proposed to be placed outside the main structure in a side yard to be screened from adjoining properties with a screening wall. This screening wall shall be required regardless of the distance from the side property line to the mechanical equipment. Wall- or window-mounted outdoor mechanical equipment shall be exempt from the screening wall requirement.... (i.e., the replacement of existing mechanical equipment shall not require a screening wall). The screening wall shall be located in the side yard between the mechanical equipment and the closest property line. The screening wall shall be 18 inches higher than the equipment being shielded and at least as wide as the equipment being shielded. See section VII-1201 for allowable encroachment of the wall into the required setback."

equip.cite: Accessory buildings and structures (Table VI-203 notes; § VII-903)
equip.text: Table VI-203 note (4): "Minimum side and rear yard for accessory buildings shall be three feet." Note (6): "Minimum rear yard setback for accessory dwelling shall be ten feet." § VII-903: "Accessory buildings shall not exceed the maximum height requirement for the particular district in which it is located"; on waterfront lots "Accessory buildings shall not be allowed in front setbacks, shall not exceed ten feet in height, and shall not cover more than 50 percent of the yard in which they are located"; "Accessory structures shall not be located in any required waterfront setback" except uncaged swimming pools meeting stated conditions; "No accessory building shall be constructed, erected, or otherwise placed on a zoning lot that is not occupied by a principal building." (p.976-978).

equip.cite: Manufactured home lots (§ VII-602)
equip.text: "Development standards for manufactured home lots. All home lots in manufactured home parks shall conform to the following standards: a. Minimum lot size. 3,500 square feet. b. Minimum lot width. 50 feet. c. Setbacks. No manufactured home, carport or other structure shall be placed or erected closer to the back of the gutter line on any internal roadway than ten feet if a utility easement is provided, or 15 feet if a utility easement is not provided. No manufactured home shall be placed or erected closer than five feet to any side or rear manufactured home lot line, provided that roof projections, overhangs, rain gutters and air conditioners may project 18 inches into any required yard areas."

equip.cite: Exterior storage of equipment, production intensive commercial zones (§ VI-603(l)(4))
equip.text: "Exterior storage is allowed if the storage area complies with the standards of this section. Exterior storage is limited to 50 percent of the zoning lot area for all uses in the CI and ICD zones; however, there is no limit for such uses in the ILW, I, IGD and IHD zones. All exterior storage areas: shall meet all setback requirements applicable to the primary use; shall meet all applicable environmental performance standards of article VII, division 10 of this Code; shall be screened in accordance with article VII, division 3 of this Code; and shall be screened from public view along all street frontages. Except for an approved waste related use, storage of refuse, waste, junk or inoperative motor vehicles or the accumulation of inoperative equipment shall be prohibited."

FAR none. Maximum front: none. ADDITIONAL: minimum Gulf front setback 150 ft measured from the mean high water line. Minimum dwelling unit size none.

G.note: Governmental district. Every cell of the G column in Table VI-703 is blank. Note (1): "All development within the G district shall be carried out in accordance with the development standards of the most restrictive zone district adjacent to the G zoned zoning lot.

CRT.frontNote: "10 ft. (8)"; note (8): "The minimum front setback for single- and two-family is 20 feet." Maximum front: none.
CRT.sideNote: "10 ft. (8)"; note (8): "The minimum side setback for single and two family is five feet but 15 feet combined."
CRT.heightNote: "65 ft. (7)"; note (7): "Maximum height for single- and two-family is 35 feet. Maximum height for mixed use where less than 50 percent of floor area devoted to residential is 45 feet. Maximum height for hotels/motels is 45 feet, however, no portion of any structure located within 100 feet of any residential zone district shall exceed the height permitted in such residential zone district."
CRT.note: Commercial Residential Transition — a non-implementing district. Densities: single and two family 8.7, multiple family 35, assisted living 35, community residential home 35, group home facility 8.7, nursing home 35, mixed use development 35, live/work 35 du/ac; hotel/motel 70 guest units. FAR none. Minimum lot sizes by use: single family 5,000 sq ft / 50 ft; two family 10,000 / 80; multiple family 20,000 / 100.

POS.frontNote: Table VI-803 prints, for all building setbacks: "All buildings must be set back from all property lines one foot for each foot of building height." A ratio, not a distance.
POS.sideNote: Same one-foot-per-foot-of-height rule. Additionally: "All outdoor activity facilities, such as playgrounds, swimming pools, basketball courts, tennis courts, or baseball fields must be set back 50 feet from any residentially zoned property."
POS.note: Park and Open Space. Maximum density none, note (2): "One caretaker dwelling unit per zoning lot is permitted." Maximum FAR 0.1. Minimum zoning lot size none. Maximum building coverage none. Table VI-803 note (1): "These standards may be superseded by the regulations of an overlay zone district."

MP.heightNote: "Applicable only to dock height (See section VII-1302)." No building height figure is printed.
MP.note: Marine Park. Maximum density none, FAR none, both with note (3) allowing additional density and FAR for submerged land. Minimum zoning lot size none; maximum building coverage none. Special standards of Sec. VI-804 apply (boat ramps and associated parking areas are conditional uses).

DTN.frontNote: Minimum front 10 ft, MAXIMUM front 20 ft — a build-to band. On secondary streets (map VI-1001) buildings are exempt from the maximum setback limitation; on primary streets the maximum front setback applies only to portions of a building meeting the minimum facade requirement. Porches may encroach up to 50% of the depth of the setback.
DTN.sideNote: "0 ft./10 ft. combined". The minimum side yard setback for structures on the south side of 4th Street is zero.
DTN.rearNote: "15 ft. primary building; 3 ft. accessory building; 4 ft. all accessory buildings, pools, and fences abutting alleys."
DTN.heightNote: Table VI-1003 gives height only in storeys: maximum 3 storeys for a primary building and 2 storeys for an accessory building; minimum not applicable. No figure in feet is printed.
DTN.note: Downtown Neighborhood District. Maximum density 12 units/acre, or 35 units/acre in the Missing Middle overlay district (MMOD, Sec. VI-906). Maximum FAR 0.5. Minimum zoning lot size 3,630 sq ft. Encroachments allowed consistent with Sec. VII-1201.

DTNE.frontNote: Minimum front 5 ft, MAXIMUM front 15 ft — a build-to band. On primary street intersections the maximum setback for chamfered corners is 20 ft from the lot corner to the center of the building facade that faces the lot corner.
DTNE.sideNote: "0 ft." but "10 ft. (where DTNE abuts DTN or RSF)".
DTNE.heightNote: Maximum 3 storeys; minimum 2 storeys on primary streets (map VI-1001). Projects using the historic preservation TDR program may be eligible for additional building height — see Sec. VI-914. No figure in feet is printed.
DTNE.note: Downtown Neighborhood Edge District. Maximum density 18 units/acre, up to 72 units/acre under Sec. VI-1005(b)(3) and VI-914. Maximum FAR: not applicable. Minimum zoning lot size 2,500 sq ft.

DTE.frontNote: Minimum front 0 ft, MAXIMUM front 10 ft — a build-to band.
DTE.heightNote: Maximum 5 storeys, or 7 storeys in the Rosemary residential overlay district (RROD, Sec. VI-912) only when provided with urban open space or transfer of development rights; minimum 2 storeys on primary streets. No figure in feet is printed.
DTE.note: Downtown Edge District. Maximum density 25 units/acre, up to 100 units/acre under Sec. VI-1005(b)(3), or up to 100 units/acre in the Rosemary residential overlay district (Sec. VI-912). Maximum FAR: not applicable. Minimum zoning lot size 1,800 sq ft.

DTC.frontNote: Minimum front 0 ft, MAXIMUM front 10 ft — a build-to band.
DTC.heightNote: Maximum 10 storeys; minimum 2 storeys on primary streets. Projects using the historic preservation TDR program may be eligible for additional building height — see Sec. VI-914. No figure in feet is printed.
DTC.note: Downtown Core District. Maximum density 50 units/acre up to 200 units/acre — see Secs. VI-1005(b)(3) and VI-914. Maximum FAR: not applicable. Minimum zoning lot size 1,800 sq ft.

DTB.frontNote: Minimum front 0 ft, MAXIMUM front 10 ft — a build-to band.
DTB.heightNote: Maximum 18 storeys; minimum 2 storeys on primary streets. No figure in feet is printed.
DTB.note: Downtown Bayfront District. Table VI-1003 prints DTC and DTB in one column; every standard is the same as DTC except the maximum storey count. Maximum density 50 units/acre up to 200 units/acre. Minimum zoning lot size 1,800 sq ft; building coverage 100%.

MU-1.sideNote: "10/15 (1,2)"; note (1): "Attached developments may reduce the interior side-setback to zero." Note (2): "The larger setback is required for zoning lots abutting residentially zoned property."
MU-1.heightNote: Table VI-1103 gives height only in storeys: maximum 3 storeys, up to 5 storeys under note (3), which adds "The maximum height shall not exceed 70 feet." Minimum: not applicable.
MU-1.note: Urban Mixed-Use 1. Maximum density 13 units/acre, up to 75 units/acre under Sec. VI-1103(b)(3). FAR not applicable; minimum zoning lot size none; maximum front none. Daylight plane requirement: where a side or rear yard abuts single-family or RMF-1, 2 or 3 zoned property, the building is limited to two storeys at the required setback line and may then extend upward at a 45-degree angle.

MU-2.sideNote: "10/15 (1,2)" — interior side may be zero for attached developments; the larger figure applies where the zoning lot abuts residentially zoned property.
MU-2.heightNote: Maximum 4 storeys, up to 5 storeys under note (3) ("The maximum height shall not exceed 70 feet"). Minimum: not applicable.
MU-2.note: Urban Mixed-Use 2. Maximum density 25 units/acre, up to 75 units/acre under Sec. VI-1103(b)(3). FAR not applicable; no minimum lot size; maximum front none. Same daylight plane, building length and outdoor area standards as MU-1.

MU-3.heightNote: Maximum 4 storeys, up to 5 storeys under note (3) ("The maximum height shall not exceed 70 feet"). Minimum: not applicable.
MU-3.note: Urban Mixed-Use 3 (North Trail only). Maximum density 35 units/acre, up to 105 units/acre under Sec. VI-1103(b)(3). FAR not applicable; no minimum lot size; maximum front none.

royal_palm_beach.name: Royal Palm Beach
royal_palm_beach.source: Code of Ordinances Chapter 26 (Zoning), Article V Zoning Districts, Secs. 26-77 through 26-95 - each district carries its own '(4) Site development standards' b

equip.cite: Permanent and portable emergency power generators - Sec. 26-101(b)(4), Table 1, Note 1
equip.text: Table 1 ('Maximum Permissible Sound Levels for Inhabited Residential and Commercial Receiving Land') sets, for inhabited residential land: 'Fixed mechanical equipment (excluding permanent emergency power generators) - Anytime - 60 dBA' and 'Permanent and portable emergency power generators - See Note 1 below - 85 dBA'. Note 1 reads: '1. Permanent and portable emergency power generators may be allowed, subject to the following restrictions: A. The property owner must obtain a building permit from the village for the installation of the permanent emergency unit. The building department shall review all such permit applications to ensure that such installation minimizes the visual and acoustic impact on adjacent properties. Additionally, special attention shall be paid to the placement of the generator, the use of sound attenuating materials and the reasonable containment of sounds which will be created by the operation of any emergency use generator. B. The permanent and portable generator's maintenance cycle run shall only be permitted between the hours of 10:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday only, and shall continue for no more than 30 minutes per cycle. C. Permanent and portable generators being utilized to allow normal residential and business functions to continue during a power outage may only be operated for nonmaintenance purposes when a state of emergency has been declared by the village or whenever there is a power outage.'

equip.cite: Definition of fixed mechanical equipment - Sec. 26-101(b)(3)h
equip.text: 'Fixed mechanical equipment shall mean mechanical equipment, such as an air-conditioning unit, water-cooling tower, swimming pool pump, fan, power generator or other similar power-source equipment permanently affixed to real property as distinguished from temporary, portable, nonfixed mechanical equipment.'

equip.cite: Accessory uses, buildings and structures - Sec. 26-57(b)(1)a
equip.text: 'Permanent. All permanent accessory uses, buildings and structures, including sheds, shall be located on the same lot as the primary structure or principal or main use and not within any required yard setbacks, except for play structures and sheds which must meet the side yard setback requirements for the zoning district in which they are located but which may be located ten (10) feet from the rear property line providing that no portion of the play structure or shed exceeds eight (8) feet in height. For sheds and play structures exceeding eight (8) feet in height, any design element of a shed or play structure exceeding eight (8) feet in height must be set back an additional one (1) foot in both the rear and side yards for every one (1) foot, or portion thereof, which exceeds eight (8) feet. All accessory structures over one hundred fifty (150) square feet shall match the architectural style of the principal/primary structure...' Sec. 26-57(b)(2): 'Height. No accessory use, building or structure shall exceed the height permitted in the district in which the principal use is located.'

equip.cite: Generators treated as accessory structures for site plan purposes - Sec. 26-40 (minor amendments)
equip.text: A minor amendment to a previously approved site plan includes: '(7) Addition of or modification to small accessory structures or other site improvements/features such as generators, sheds, traffic bollards (must be ornamental in nature), propane tank storage cages, air compressor service stations, ice merchandisers, or mail kiosks; relocation of loading spaces; and repurposing of recreational courts.'

equip.cite: Propane storage - Sec. 11-23 (Fire prevention)
equip.text: 'Except for where warranted on village-owned property, all propane storage tanks in excess of one hundred twenty-five (125) gallons capacity shall be installed underground. A maximum of two (2) above ground tanks of lesser capacity, not to exceed fifty-six (56) gallons each, can be installed aboveground on any one (1) lot. All propane storage tanks shall be installed in accordance with NFPA 58, as amended.'

equip.cite: Emergency generators required for automotive service stations - Sec. 26-101(m)
equip.text: 'All newly constructed automotive service stations which sell gasoline or other petroleum products shall have a permanently installed emergency generator. Existing automotive service stations which sell gasoline or other petroleum products shall be required to install permanent emergency generators whenever such service station is rebuilt after being destroyed to an extent of more than fifty (50) percent of its assessed value or whenever a revised site plan for such service station is submitted for approval which enlarges upon or alters in any way the original site plan for that service station... (2) The permanent emergency generators installed at service stations are also subject to the noise standards and restrictions set forth in subsection (b) at table 1 hereinabove.'

equip.cite: Emergency generator required for ALF/MCF/CCF - Sec. 26-60(13)
equip.text: 'Emergency generator. A sufficient emergency generator must be provided for ALF, MCF, and CCF. An emergency generator shall be sufficient to provide the necessary power to allow for (i) a climate controlled area of refuge within a common area that is large enough to accommodate all facility residents; (ii) an element of refrigeration in th[e]...'

equip.cite: Performance standards, general - Sec. 26-101(a)
equip.text: 'All uses and activities permitted as of right, special exceptions, or special permit in any district shall conform to the standards of performance described below and shall be constructed, maintained, and operated so as not to be injurious or offensive to the occupants of adjacent premises by reason of the emission or creation of noise, vibration, smoke, dust or other particulate matter, toxic or noxious waste materials, odors, fire and explosive hazard, or glare; so as not to allow any non-permitted use to occur on the property; and/or so as to be operated in such a manner as will allow for the continuation of essential services during times of emergencies due to events such as hurricanes or other natural disasters.'

equip.cite: Screening of service function areas / mechanical equipment - Sec. 26-73 (large scale commercial/industrial)
equip.text: '(2) Service Function Areas (SFA's) including but not limited to loading, storage, mechanical equipment, and solid waste disposal. a. Buffering and screening standards. Loading areas or docks, trash collection, mechanical equipment, trash compaction, vehicular storage, (excluding new and used cars) recycling, roof top equipment and other service function areas shall be fully screened from view of adjace[nt]...'. The MXS district repeats this at Sec. 26-95(9)(j).

equip.cite: Machinery noise hours - Sec. 26-101(b)(5)e
equip.text: 'Machinery construction work. The operation of any machinery, demolition equipment, construction equipment, power tools, equipment of semimechanical devices or undertaking construction work which emits a sound plainly audible across the property line of an inhabited residential property between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. However, this subsection shall not prohibit the use of temporary pumps or machinery which, because of its very nature and purpose, is required to be operated twenty-four (24) hours a day.'

CON.note: Conservation District (Sec. 26-77). The section has no '(4) Site development standards' subsection at all - it lists purpose and intent, environmentally significant lands, uses permitted, activities requiring a special events permit, and prohibited activities only. No lot, setback or height standard is printed.

RS-1.heightNote: Sec. 26-78(4)(c) reads only 'Reserved.' - no maximum building height is printed for RS-1.
RS-1.note: Single-Family Residential (Sec. 26-78). Side (interior) 10; Side (corner) 15; Rear, for screened enclosure 10. Minimum floor area 1,700 sq ft per unit (reducible by the village council under a F.S. 163.3220-163.3243 development agreement). Minimum pervious area 50 percent of total lot area. Maximum density 5 units per gross acre. Special exception uses note: 'Public utilities.

RS-2.note: Single-Family Residential (Sec. 26-79). Height printed '30 feet and not more than 2 stories'. Side (interior) 10*; Side (corner) 15; Rear 20*; Rear, for screened enclosure 10.

RS-3.note: Single-Family Residential (Sec. 26-80). Height printed '30 feet and not more than two (2) stories'. Minimum lot depth 100 feet. Side (interior) 7.5; Side (corner) 15; Rear, for screened enclosure 10. Minimum floor area 1,500 sq ft. Minimum pervious area 20 percent. Maximum density 5 units per gross acre.

RMU.frontNote: Sec. 26-81(4)(c) prints a separation matrix, not a single front setback: 'The following required minimum distances shall be measured from each structure to nearest adjacent structure, street, parking space, water body or perimeter, whichever occurs first' - Front to Front of structure 50; Front to Side of structure 40; Front to Street, water body or perimeter 15; Front to right-of-way line 25.
RMU.sideNote: Same matrix: Side to Side of structure when not a zero lot line development 30; Duplex 10; Side to Street, water body or perimeter 15; Side to Parking space 5; Side to Zero lot line or attached structure 0.
RMU.rearNote: Same matrix: Rear to Rear of structure 40; Rear to Side of structure 35; Rear to Street, parking space, water body or perimeter 20.
RMU.note: Residential Mixed Use District (Sec. 26-81). Minimum parcel size 3 acres (3 x 43,560 = 130,680 sq ft). Maximum building height 'Thirty-two (32) feet. Lofts, mezzanines or other elevated floor areas are permitted but cannot be included as livable area.' Minimum parcel perimeter landscape setback width: adjacent to public rights-of-way 25 feet; adjacent to interior lot lines 10 feet.

RV-6.frontNote: Sec. 26-82(4)(c) prints a separation matrix, not a single front setback: Front to Front of structure 50; Front to Side of structure 40; Front to Street, water body or perimeter 15; Front to right-of-way line 25; Front to Parking space 5.
RV-6.sideNote: Same matrix: Side to Side of structure when not a zero lot line development 30; Duplex 10; Side to Street, water body or perimeter 15; Side to Parking space 5; Side to Zero lot line or attached structure 0.
RV-6.rearNote: Same matrix: Rear to Rear of structure 40; Rear to Side of structure 35; Rear to Street, parking space, water body or perimeter 20.
RV-6.note: Villa Residential District (Sec. 26-82). Minimum parcel size three (3) acres, 'except Tract 205 which is already platted' (3 x 43,560 = 130,680 sq ft). Maximum building height 'Twenty (20) feet; all required livable space shall be at ground floor level.' Minimum parcel setback width to perimeter landscape buffer: adjacent interior property lines 10 feet unless the yard is 10 feet or greater.

RT-8.frontNote: Sec. 26-83(4)(c) prints a separation matrix, not a single front setback: Front to Front of structure 50; Front to Side of structure 40; Front to Street, water body or perimeter 15; Front to right-of-way line 25; Front to Parking space 5.
RT-8.sideNote: Same matrix: Side to Street, water body or perimeter 15; Side to Zero lot line or attached structure 0; Side to Parking space 5; Side to right-of-way line 20; Side to Side of structure 30; Duplex 10.
RT-8.rearNote: Same matrix: Rear to Rear of structure 40; Rear to Side of structure 35; Rear to Street, parking space, water body or perimeter 20.
RT-8.note: Townhouse Residential District (Sec. 26-83). Minimum parcel size 3 acres (130,680 sq ft), 'except for parcels platted within Tracts 107 and 204 prior to the adoption of this chapter, which shall be permitted at their platted size'. Height printed '30 feet and not more than 2 stories'.

RM-9.note: Multifamily Residential District (Sec. 26-84). Minimum parcel size two and one-half (2.5) acres (2.5 x 43,560 = 108,900 sq ft), except child care centers which require one (1) acre, and except for parcels platted prior to the adoption of this chapter. Minimum parcel width 200 feet.

RM-12.note: Multifamily Residential District (medium density) (Sec. 26-85). Minimum parcel size 3 acres (130,680 sq ft), except child-care centers which require one (1) acre, and except parcels platted prior to adoption. Minimum parcel width 200 feet. Maximum building height '3 stories or 32 feet'. Side (interior) 20; Side (corner or between structures; does not include accessory structures) 40; Side (child-care center) 50.

RM-14.note: Multifamily Residential District (high density) (Sec. 26-86). Minimum parcel size 3 acres (130,680 sq ft) except child-care centers of one (1) or more acres. Minimum parcel width 200 feet. Height printed '32 feet and not more than 3 stories'. Side (interior) 20; Side (corner or between structures) 40; Side (child-care center) 50; Rear (child-care center) 50. Maximum building coverage 25 percent.

CO.note: Office Commercial District (Sec. 26-87). Height printed '32 feet and not more than three (3) stories'. Setbacks apply 'to all three-story structures or less': Front 50; Rear 30; Side (interior) 20; Side (corner) 50.

CN.note: Neighborhood Commercial District (Sec. 26-88). Height printed '32 feet and not more than 2 stories'. Side (interior) 15; Side (corner) 30. these are unusually large but they are what the code prints. Minimum pervious area 20 percent of total lot area.

CG.note: General Commercial District (Sec. 26-89). Height printed 'Thirty-two (32) feet and not more than two (2) stories'. Side (interior) 0; Side (corner) 50. No maximum lot coverage is printed.

PR.note: Private Recreation District (Sec. 26-90). Minimum parcel size five (5) acres (5 x 43,560 = 217,800 sq ft). Minimum parcel width 200 feet. Height printed 'Thirty-two (32) feet and not more than two (2) stories'. Side (interior) 100; Side (corner) 100. Minimum pervious area 20 percent of total site area. 'Lighting shall be designed so as not to illuminate adjacent properties.

PO.note: Public Ownership District (Sec. 26-91). Subsection (4) reads in full: 'Site development standards. To be determined by village council upon recommendations by staff and the planning and zoning commission.' No dimensional standard of any kind is printed.

IL.note: Industrial Limited District (Sec. 26-92). Minimum parcel size 2 acres (2 x 43,560 = 87,120 sq ft); minimum parcel width 150 feet.

IG.note: Industrial General District (Sec. 26-93). Minimum parcel size 3 acres (130,680 sq ft); minimum parcel width 200 feet; both carry the same unity-of-control asterisk as IL. Side (interior) 25; Side (corner) 40. 'Required yards abutting public rights-of-way shall be landscaped to provide a park-like appearance.' Height printed '32 feet and not more than 2 stories except as otherwise set forth in this section'.

MXD.frontNote: Sec. 26-94(4)(c): 'Setbacks for individual uses within the MXD shall be as follows: (1) Single-family detached dwellings, subject to subsection 26-79(4)(d). (2) Patio homes/zero lot line homes, subject to section 26-63. (3) Villa dwellings, subject to subsection 26-82(4)(d). (4) Townhouse dwellings, subject to subsection 26-83(4)(d). (5) Multifamily dwellings, subject to subsection 26-84(4)(e).
MXD.heightNote: Sec. 26-94(4)(b): 'Maximum building height shall be determined by the location of that individual building as shown below.

Minimum parcel perimeter landscape setback width: public rights-of-way 25 feet; private interior lot line 10 feet; public open space 10 feet. Minimum common open space 40 percent of the total site of the entire project.

MXS.frontNote: Sec. 26-95(4)(c): 'Setbacks within the MXS zoning district shall comply with the MXS layers regulating plans set forth in figures 3 and 4 below.

'Minimum MXS project size shall be forty (40) acres' (Sec. 26-95(7); 40 x 43,560 = 1,742,400 sq ft).

PUD.frontNote: Sec. 26-74(c)(2): 'Uses and dwelling types permitted in this district shall be generally reviewed according to the site development standards of those zoning districts under which the uses and dwelling types are set forth as "Permitted Uses"...
PUD.note: Planned Unit Development (Sec. 26-74) - a special-exception overlay on an underlying district, not a mapped base district. Height: 'The maximum building height shall be thirty-two (32) feet and not more than three (3) stories.

PID.frontNote: Sec. 26-75(c)(2): 'Outparcels within the PID may be permitted at less than the minimum parcel size required in the underlying IG or IL zoning district and the site development standards applicable to these zoning districts may be modified as approved by village council through the PID approval process.' No PID-specific yard setback is printed; the underlying IL or IG setbacks apply.
PID.note: Planned Industrial Development (Sec. 26-75) - a special-exception overlay on the underlying IL or IG district. 'Minimum parcel size for an entire PID shall be three (3) acres' (130,680 sq ft). 'The maximum building height shall be thirty-two (32) feet and not more than two (2) stories.'

jefferson_county.name: Jefferson County
jefferson_county.source: Land Development Code, ch. 50. Jefferson has no zoning districts in the usual sense and no per-district dimensional table: land use districts are the FLUM categ

equip.cite: Countywide building setback (Sec. 50-5.1.3(a), PDF p.513)
equip.text: "For all properties in the county, building placement shall adhere to the following standards: (a) Perimeter property setbacks. (1) The outermost wall of all buildings shall be constructed a minimum of ten feet from any side or rear perimeter boundary line and 25 feet from any public or private road easement line or right of way line. If there is no defined right-of-way or easement, the building construction setback shall be 55 feet from the centerline of the road driving surface. (2) All parking lot construction shall be a minimum of ten feet from any perimeter property line and shall provide landscaping as required herein." The rule is written for BUILDINGS; the code prints no accessory-structure or equipment-pad variant and no permitted encroachment into these setbacks.

equip.cite: Table 5.1.3 Building Placement Standards (PDF p.514)
equip.text: Multi-Family Residential and Non-Residential Site Plans - Perimeter Building Setbacks: Front 25 feet, Side-Corner 25 feet, Side-Interior 10 feet, Rear 10 feet. Interior Building Setbacks (Between Buildings): Front 50 feet, Side 20 feet, Rear 30 feet. Non-residential developments: minimum side separation of 20 feet, minimum front and rear separation of 30 feet.

equip.cite: Screening of equipment and machinery, Lloyd Historic Overlay (Sec. 50-2.8.0(e)(3)b.4, PDF p.479)
equip.text: "Dumpsters, sheds, equipment or machinery in support of a structure shall be shielded by appropriate fencing or buffering high enough to prohibit view from the street." This is the ONLY provision in the Jefferson code that addresses the screening or placement of equipment or machinery accessory to a building, and it applies only inside the Lloyd Historic Overlay District.

equip.cite: Rooftop equipment counts toward height (definition of height, PDF p.443)
equip.text: "When applied to a building, height shall be measured to the highest point of the coping of a flat roof or to the average height level between eaves and ridge for gable, hip, or gambrel roofs. Rooftop equipment shall be added to the measurement of the height of a building, as determined above, if the equipment extends more than four feet above the highest portion of the roof."

equip.cite: LP gas facilities (Sec. 50-2.1.x and Sec. 50-2.9.2(a)(3), PDF p.458, 461, 481)
equip.text: "LP gas storage and/or distribution facilities for 10,000 gallons or less" is listed as a general commercial use; facilities "including one or more storage tanks for liquids including chemicals, petroleum, or LP gas storage and/or distribution facilities exceeding 10,000 gallons" fall in the heavy industrial use group; and Sec. 50-2.9.2(a)(3) makes "LP storage and/or distribution facility in excess of 1,000 gallons" a special exception use in all land use districts. No separation distance or setback is printed for any of these.

equip.cite: Utility plants and electric power plants (Sec. 50-2.2.5(b), Sec. 50-2.9.2(a)(7))
equip.text: Utility plants are a special exception use in the industrial district; electric power plants are a special exception use in all land use districts under the transportation/utility overlay. Review criteria include "compatibility of the proposed district with adjacent and overlaid districts, and proposed means and methods of mitigating and potential incompatibilities due to nuisance, noise, glare, scale of facility, and appearance" - no distances are printed.

equip.cite: Noise limits by district (ch. 14, Table 1 and Table 2, PDF p.202)
equip.text: Sound level limits are set for the IB and IND land use districts (Table 1: 7:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. not regulated) and separately for any area of the county not in IB or IND (Table 2). "Residential property" for this purpose means property with habitually and lawfully occupied sleeping quarters located in CON, AG-20, AG-5, AG-3, MUBR, MUSR, R-1 or R-2.

AG-20.frontNote: Sec. 50-5.1.3(a)(1): "The outermost wall of all buildings shall be constructed a minimum of ten feet from any side or rear perimeter boundary line and 25 feet from any public or private road easement line or right of way line. If there is no defined right-of-way or easement, the building construction setback shall be 55 feet from the centerline of the road driving surface."
AG-20.heightNote: No maximum building height is printed for this or any other land use district. The only height limit in the code is 38 ft inside the Lloyd Historic Overlay District (Sec. 50-2.8.0(e)(3)a).
AG-20.coverageNote: The Sec. 50-2.6.0 table prints "N/A" in the Max Area of Impervious column for Ag. 20. Sec. 50-2.3.1(b) prints a conditional figure instead: "For institutional and public service uses, intensity of development by impervious surface coverage should not exceed 35 percent." The table's separate "Non-Residential Use Area" column prints 5%.

equip.cite: Accessory structures, including a generator — LDC § 4.2.6.C
equip.text: Marion County prints no dedicated generator ordinance and no special yard-encroachment allowance for mechanical equipment. A permanently installed generator is an accessory structure: it must sit in a rear or side yard — never in a required front yard — at the district's General Accessory setback, and on lots of one acre or less a minimum of 8 ft from the rear and side lot lines (§ 4.2.6.C.8). Only eaves, roof overhangs, pilasters, chimneys and fireplaces may protrude 2 ft into a required setback (§ 4.2.6.C.4), and that allowance does not extend to a generator. No structure may be placed over an easement without the easement holder's written approval (§ 4.2.6.C.3). Above-ground LP tanks follow the same accessory-structure setbacks plus Fire Code separation distances. Confirm placement with Marion County Growth Services (352-438-2600) before siting.

equip.cite: Accessory uses and structures (Sec. 3.12) - the general placement rule
equip.text: "(a) In residential districts all accessory buildings and uses shall be located only in the rear yard except that parking may be located in a side yard. (b) In residential districts all accessory buildings and uses in a rear yard shall be located at least eight feet from any lot line, meet required setback from any street, and at least five feet from any main building. Accessory buildings and structures shall not exceed two stories or 24 feet in height. In case of rear alleys, private garages not over one story in height may be located on the rear alley line."

equip.cite: Yard encroachments (Sec. 3.10)
equip.text: "Every part of every required yard shall be open and unobstructed from the ground to the sky except as hereinafter provided or as otherwise permitted in the zoning code. (a) Sills or belt courses may project not over 12 inches into a required yard. (b) Movable awnings may project not over three feet into a required yard... (c) Chimneys, fireplaces or pilasters may project not over two feet into a required yard. (d) Fire escapes, stairways and balconies which are unroofed and unenclosed may project not over five feet into a required rear yard, or not over three feet eight inches into a required side yard, of a multiple dwelling, hotel or motel. (e) Hoods, canopies or marquees may project not over three feet into a required yard, but shall not exceed closer than one foot to any lot line... (g) Accessory uses and structures may be located in required yards as specified in section 3.12 of this article... (i) Accessory parking may be located in a required rear or side yard. (j) Flagpoles, clotheslines, birdhouses and other yard accessories are permitted in any yard if they do not constitute substantial impediments to vision or free flow of light and air across the yard." NOTE: this list does not name generators, A/C condensers, pool equipment or LP tanks. In Dunnellon a ground-mounted generator in a residential district falls under Sec. 3.12 - rear yard only, at least 8 ft from any lot line and 5 ft from the main building.

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment screening, commercial development (Sec. 9.3-1(a)(3))
equip.text: "Mechanical equipment, electrical meter and service components, and similar utility devices, whether ground level, wall mounted, or roof mounted, shall be screened from view from public rights-of-way through one of the following methods: a. Landscaping. b. Uses of brick, wood, masonry, or PVC materials for screening. Such materials are to be compatible with the predominant materials and colors used for the principal building on the site."

equip.cite: Accessory structures and uses, commercial (Sec. 9.3-1(b))
equip.text: "Accessory uses and structures shall be integrated into the overall design of the site to ensure that visual and other impacts of these uses are fully contained or enclosed and out of view from adjacent properties and public streets. (1) Accessory uses and structures are loading docks, truck parking, outdoor storage, outdoor shopping cart storage areas, utility meters or cabinets, lift stations, HVAC equipment, dumpster, and other similar service facilities and functions. (2) Accessory uses and structures shall be designed to blend with the principal building through the use of color, building materials, and architectural features... (3) Loading docks and outside storage and displays shall be setback a minimum of 100 feet from any lots zoned for residential use... (5) Accessory uses shall not exceed the height of the principal building."

equip.cite: Height exclusions (Sec. 3.13)
equip.text: "Scenery lofts, towers, cupolas, steeples, domes, flagpoles, airplane beacons, broadcasting towers, antennas, chimneys, stacks, tanks and roof structures used only for ornamental or mechanical purposes may exceed the permissible height limit in any district."

equip.cite: District boundary line lots (Sec. 3.19)
equip.text: "(a) Where a business district is separated by a street from a residential district, then any lot in such non-residential district adjacent to the separating street shall be provided with a yard at least 25 feet in depth along such separating street. (b) Where a business district directly abuts on a residential district without any separator between them such as a street, alley, or other public open space, then any lot in such non-residential district shall be provided with a yard at least ten feet in depth adjacent to the residentially zoned property. (c) Where a warehouse use in a business district directly abuts on a residential district... at least 20 feet in depth. (d) Where a yard is required in this section, such yard may be used for walkways, driveways and landscaping, but not for any other use or purpose."
