equip.cite: Accessory structures — setback (§ 2.21.05.2 and .3, PDF p.1101)
equip.text: "2. Accessory uses or structures located in side or rear yards shall be no closer than five feet to any property line, except as otherwise specified herein. 3. Accessory uses and structures located in front yards must conform to the front minimum building setback requirement for the zoning district in which it is located, except as otherwise specified herein." This is the operative rule for a ground-mounted generator, condenser or pool pump in Okaloosa: five feet from any property line in a side or rear yard, or the full district front setback if it is in the front yard.

equip.cite: Accessory structures — sight and access (§ 2.21.05.1, PDF p.1101)
equip.text: "No accessory use or structure shall be installed, constructed, or placed so as to prevent the safe use of any driveway, or to cause a vision obstruction in any intersection vision triangle, or otherwise create a hazard by obstructing the view of pedestrians, cyclists, or motorists."

equip.cite: What counts as a residential accessory structure (§ 2.21.02, PDF p.1099–1100)
equip.text: The list permitted on lots in R-1, R-2, R-3, SR and MU is: "a. Private, freestanding garage or carport; b. Fence...; c. Storage shed; d. Freestanding deck, patio; e. Dock or pier; f. Swimming pool and enclosure, pool house; g. Gazebo, cabana; h. Vegetable or ornamental garden; i. Playhouse; j. Television or radio antennae; k. Keeping of domesticated animals as pets; l. Guest house; m. Garage apartment. n. Home occupation/office; o. Home or kitchen garden; p. Other similar uses and structures." A generator, A/C condenser or pool pump is not named; it would have to come in under "p. Other similar uses and structures" and under the § 2.21.01 test that the use "is so necessary or commonly to be expected that it cannot be supposed that the zoning regulations were intended to prevent it."

equip.cite: Projections into side and rear setbacks (§ 2.19.00 footnote 4, PDF p.1080)
equip.text: "Two or more structures located on the same lot shall be a minimum ten feet apart for one- or two-story buildings. Fireplaces, chimneys, and bay windows will be allowed to extend into rear and side yard setbacks provided they do not exceed 30 inches in depth and six feet in width and provided the furthest extension is at least the greater of seven and one-half feet from the adjacent dwelling unit or the minimum required by the building and life safety codes as determined by type of construction." Only fireplaces, chimneys and bay windows — not mechanical equipment.

equip.cite: Setback from water (§ 2.19.00 footnotes 1 and 2, PDF p.1079)
equip.text: "In all zoning districts, the setback requirements from the mean high-water line (MHWL) do not apply to boat docks, piers, bulkheads (seawalls) or boathouses. For principal structure on tidal waterfront lots, the setback from the mean high-water line (MHWL) is 50 feet." "The setback from any natural non-tidal waters shall be 25 feet from the ordinary high-water line. A vegetative buffer shall be retained as required by chapter 6 of this ordinance."

equip.cite: Outdoor equipment for towers and telecommunication facilities (§ 2.20.xx, PDF p.1094)
equip.text: "All new tower bases, guy anchors, outdoor equipment, accessory buildings and accessory structures erected for use in connection with towers and telecommunication facilities shall be required to meet the minimum setback requirements established for the district in which they are located, and be visually screened to a height of at least eight feet by trees, large shrubs, solid walls and/or fences..." This is the only place the code screens ground equipment, and it is limited to tower sites.

equip.cite: Zero-lot-line, Z-lot and zipper-lot side yards (§ 2.18.04–2.18.06, PDF p.1078–1079)
equip.text: Zero-lot-line development in R-1, R-2, R-3 and MU: minimum lot 5,500 sq ft, "Yard setbacks shall be: Front — 20 feet; Sides — 0 feet, 10 feet; Rear — 10 feet [no portion of a building may extend across a property line]", frontage 50 ft (20 ft irregular or cul-de-sac), max height 45 feet. Zipper lots: minimum lot 5,500 sq ft, "Front — 20 feet; Sides — 7.5 feet; Rear — 0 feet", max height 35 feet. Cluster subdivisions in R-1, R-2, R-3 and mixed use: "setbacks may be reduced to a minimum 20 feet front, ten feet rear, and five-foot sides to accommodate smaller lots" with lots no smaller than 5,000 square feet. On a zero-lot-line or zipper lot the usable side or rear yard collapses to zero on one side, which is where a generator pad would most often conflict.

gen.cite: Mechanical equipment in the Siesta Key Overlay District (§ 124-102(b)(4)j.5., PDF p.2250)
gen.text: "In SKOD, new at-grade or elevated mechanical equipment (such as air conditioning units, pool equipment, generators) shall comply with minimum side yard setback for the underlying zoning district. Mechanical equipment on nonconforming lots in the RE-2/SKOD and any RSF/SKOD Districts shall comply with the minimum side yard setback required in subsection p., below. The replacement of existing mechanical equipment is exempt from the minimum side yard setback provided that existing encroachment is not increased by the new mechanical equipment. However, all mechanical equipment shall be screened with lattice fencing or a similar type of screening material that provides a partial screening of the view of the equipment from the neighboring property, the public right-of-way or private roadways."

gen.cite: Rooftop and ground-level mechanical screening in the Myakka River / temporary telecom context (§ 118-38(e), PDF p.1835)
gen.text: "Equipment such as air conditioners and generators used in connection with a temporary [telecommunications] facility shall not generate noise above decibel level consistent with County noise ordinance. Air conditioner units should not be louder than ordinary residential units and generation shall be equipped with a functioning residential muffler."

equip.cite: Air-conditioning, mechanical, electrical and plumbing equipment — exemption from side and rear yards (§ 124-72(e)(4)f., PDF p.2054)
equip.text: "Air-conditioning, mechanical, electrical and plumbing equipment located at above ground level or elevated due to FEMA elevation requirements is exempt from side and rear yard setback requirements. In no case shall such equipment be located closer than three feet from the property line or in any easement. In the case of a PUD where there are not required setbacks, such equipment shall not be placed in any easement. See Section 124-102(b)(4)j.5. for equipment placement requirements in the SKOD."

equip.cite: Required yards must be unobstructed (§ 124-72(e)(1), PDF p.2052)
equip.text: "Every part of every required yard shall be open and unobstructed from 30 inches above the general ground level of the graded lot upward to the sky except as hereinafter provided or as otherwise permitted in this UDC."

equip.cite: Accessory buildings and structures (§ 124-73(a)(5), PDF p.2055)
equip.text: "No accessory building or structure shall be erected in any required setback area, except as expressly set forth in Article 6."

equip.cite: Air conditioners in manufactured home parks (§ 124-76(b)(4)i.3., RMH rear yard, PDF p.2133)
equip.text: "Provided, however, roof projections, overhangs, rain gutters and air conditioners may project into any required setback areas."

equip.cite: Side-yard equipment where building separation is reduced (§ 124-133(a)3., PDF p.2371)
equip.text: Where the 12-foot minimum separation between residential buildings is reduced to as little as 8 feet: "Improvements in the side yards are prohibited, except for HVAC, mechanical, pool, and other equipment that is either to the rear of the building or staggered so that equipment on adjacent lots is 10 feet apart. These limitations shall be included in the applicable declaration of restrictions."

equip.cite: Commercial redevelopment adjoining residential (§ 124-129(d), PDF p.2347)
equip.text: "In addition to the requirements of Section 124-73, for lots with an average lot depth of 500 feet or greater, the following accessory uses or structures shall not be located in the minimum required side or rear yard when those yards abut a residential zoning district or a residential Future Land Use Map designation: (1) Solid waste storage and collection areas. (2) Air conditioning compressors and any other mechanical equipment that generates noise that is incompatible with an abutting residential use. (3) All delivery and loading and unloading areas and activities. (4) Drive-through lanes and windows."

equip.cite: Height exemption for HVAC equipment (§ 124-72(a)(6)d.1. and f., PDF p.2049-2051)
equip.text: Height limitations do not apply to "flagpoles; antennas and transmission towers...; water tanks or fire towers; heating, ventilation or air conditioning equipment, elevator shafts, chimneys and unenclosed roof-top stairways/ladders (when and specifically as required by the Building Code) on buildings with four or more stories." On the Barrier Islands in residential districts, where building height is measured from an established minimum floor elevation, "the only exclusions from height and Conservation District two-story limits shall be for unenclosed heating, ventilation, and air conditioning equipment and antennas in conformance with Chapter 118, Article II, of the County Code."

equip.cite: Accessory uses and structures - setbacks (Sec. 9-2.f)
equip.text: "Setbacks. This section provides for accessory structures to be located per required building setback areas according to the zoning district in which the principal use is located. Recorded easements and required landscape buffers may supersede the minimum dimensions permitted. However, in residential zoning districts where accessory structures are less than two hundred (200) square feet, setbacks shall be set a minimum of ten (10) feet two-tenths (.2)." [Quoted verbatim, including the trailing "two-tenths (.2)", which is how the printed page reads - confirmed against the page image at. It is not resolvable from the document what the ".2" modifies.]

equip.cite: Accessory uses and structures - principal use required (Sec. 9-2.b, 9-2.d.3)
equip.text: "No accessory structure or use shall be permitted on any lot without an established principal use on the same lot within the applicable zoning district." And: "Any specific accessory use or structure which is not addressed within this chapter shall not be located on any lot."

equip.cite: Accessory structure size (Sec. 9-2.e)
equip.text: "Size limitations. No enclosed, unattached accessory buildings, including accessory structures and guest quarters, shall cause the impervious coverage to exceed the maximum allowed for the specific district per the Zoning chapter."

equip.cite: Impervious surfaces in setbacks and easements (Sec. 9-1.a)
equip.text: "Impervious surfaces are allowed within building setbacks and easements. The impervious surface may abut the adjoining property line only if the lot size is equal to or less than six thousand nine hundred (6,900) square feet provided that a curb (three (3) inches high, six (6) inches wide) is constructed along the adjacent property line to direct water from adjacent property." Sec. 9-1.b adds that a covenant of removal is required before permit application if impervious surface is placed within a utility easement.

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment - commercial and multi-family (Sec. 20-3C.11, Service Areas)
equip.text: "B Mechanical equipment should be integrated into the overall mass of a building by screening it behind parapets or by recessing equipment into hips, gables, parapets or similar features. Plain boxes are not acceptable. C Loading areas or docks, outdoor storage, waste disposal, mechanical equipment, satellite dishes, truck parking, and other service support equipment shall be located behind the building line and shall be fully screened from the view of adjacent properties both at ground and roof top levels.... E Where storage/utilities/loading facilities are located adjacent to residential lots, they shall include a visual and solid acoustic buffer.... J Utilities for all new commercial developments shall be located underground. K Utility boxes must be totally screened from view of principal streets, as well as pedestrian walkways and areas." Applies to all commercial and multi-family development in the Town regardless of location (Sec. 20-2B).

equip.cite: Outside storage - residential (Sec. 9-2.h.1)
equip.text: "Residential uses. Outside storage of materials and equipment shall be restricted to the rear yard, screened and not visible from any public right-of-way or adjoining lot. This provision shall not apply to the regular parking or storage of licensed and operable motor vehicles, boats, recreational vehicles and other such vehicles which are regulated by other Town codes. Specifically prohibited is the outside storage of appliances, unlicensed or inoperable motor vehicles, motor vehicle parts, and equipment and materials used as part of a business conducted off-site."

equip.cite: Structure height for accessory structures (Sec. 9-2.g.2)
equip.text: Carports, freestanding: 15 feet. Storage buildings - residential uses: "Shall not exceed principal structure"; non-residential uses: 15 feet.

equip.cite: Administrative variance (Sec. 3-13.b)
equip.text: "1 Principal building setbacks. Up to twenty (20) percent of the setback requirement. In no case shall the side yard setback be less than five (5) feet for conventional one (1) and two (2) family developments. No modification of the required setback from a natural surface waterbody or preserved wetland shall be permitted. 2) Accessory building location standards. Up to ten (10) percent of the setback requirement." A modification of less than one foot is deemed non-substantial (Sec. 3-13.c.

equip.cite: Heating/air conditioning units on wells (Sec. 18-85)
equip.text: "a No person shall attach any heating/air conditioning unit to an existing well, or drill any well for use with a heating/air conditioning unit, unless a second well of equal size and depth is drilled to return to the same aquifer the water withdrawn. b All water taken from any such well and used with the heating/air conditioning unit must be returned to such second well, unless written permission is given by the Town for the use of such water or any part thereof for irrigation purposes." This is a groundwater-protection rule, not a setback.

equip.cite: Standby generators - the only generator sections in the code (Sec. 14-8.b.5, 14-8.b.6)
equip.text: The only 'generator' provisions in this Land Development Code govern municipal sewage pumping stations, not private property: "Sewage pumping stations shall be equipped with stationary stand-by power generator connections to provide for emergency auxiliary pumping. The emergency generator receptacle shall be a model AR2042-S22 unless otherwise approved by the Town." And Sec. 14-8.b.6.F: "An on-site standby emergency generator shall be required to be installed at lift stations with seven hundred (700) GPM flow or an eight (8) inch force main, and/or as required by the Department of Environmental Protection, and/or under special circumstances due to remoteness of site for lift stations smaller than the above cited standards." No clearance or setback distance is given.

gen.cite: Mechanical Equipment (UDC Subsection 9.3.R, PDF p.832)
gen.text: 'Mechanical Equipment. Mechanical equipment includes heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) equipment, electrical generators, and similar equipment. Equipment that serves Manufactured Homes, including electric, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning equipment and other service facilities, shall comply with the requirements of the Florida Building Code, Residential Section R322. (1) Ground-Mounted Equipment. a. Mechanical equipment is prohibited in the front yard. If mechanical equipment is located in the front yard as of the effective date of this Code, the equipment may remain and may be repaired and maintained unless it is replaced in its entirety or the principal structure is demolished. b. Mechanical equipment is permitted only in the interior side, or rear yard and shall be screened. (2) Roof-Mounted Equipment. a. For structures four or more stories in height, all roof equipment must be set back from the edge of the roof a minimum distance of one foot for every two feet by which the equipment extends above the roof. b. For structures less than four stories in height and for any building where roof equipment cannot meet the setback requirement of item a. above, there must be either a parapet wall to screen the equipment or the equipment must be housed in solid building material that is architecturally integrated with the structure.' This section names electrical generators explicitly. It fixes location (interior side or rear yard only, never the front yard) and a screening duty, but states NO clearance distance to a property line for ground-mounted equipment.

gen.cite: Mobile vendor generators (Code of Ordinances Chapter on mobile vending, PDF p.356)
gen.text: Mobile vendors may not use a device 'to attract public attention or as to constitute a nuisance in violation of the city's noise regulations. Generators exceeding the city's noise requirements must have proper sound attenuation to mitigate noise in excess of the requirements as set forth in article 9 of the city's Unified Development Code.' This governs mobile vending units, not a fixed standby generator.

gen.cite: Telecommunications facility definition (PDF p.769)
gen.text: 'Facility. A structure used to house and protect the equipment necessary for processing telecommunications signals, which may include air conditioning equipment and emergency generators.' This is a definition, not a setback.

equip.cite: General Regulations for Accessory Structures (UDC Subsection 9.3.A, PDF p.819-820)
equip.text: '(1) No accessory structure may be constructed prior to construction of the principal building to which it is accessory.... (3) Certain accessory structures may be prohibited in certain yards. The use of the term "yard" refers to the area between the applicable building line and lot line. The distinction is made because certain principal buildings may not be built at required district setback lines, thereby creating a yard larger than the minimum setback dimension. If a structure is permitted within a yard, it may be permitted within the required setback subject to additional limitations. (4) The maximum height of any detached accessory structure shall not exceed the height of the primary structure, unless otherwise permitted or restricted by this Code. (5) Accessory structures are included and must comply with all maximum impervious surface coverage. (6) Accessory structures are limited to 25% coverage of any [yard]... (8) Any accessory structure located closer that ten (10) feet to the primary structure shall be construed as part of the primary structure and shall observe all setback requirements for said primary structure. (9) Accessory structures must be at least five (5) feet from any lot line, unless otherwise permitted or restricted by this Code. (10) No accessory building shall be erected in any required front or side yard. Accessory buildings may be constructed in the rear yard provided such building meets the above and any other applicable standards.'

equip.cite: Permitted Intrusions into required setbacks (UDC Subsection 6.2(B)(2), PDF p.722-723)
equip.text: 'Intrusions into required building setbacks shall apply with the following additions. The following intrusions are permitted in any required building setback unless otherwise noted. a. Required driveways are permitted in the minimum setback. b. Awnings or overhanging eaves may be permitted to project into minimum setbacks provided the following conditions are met... d. Awnings or overhanging eaves shall provide a minimum of nine feet clearance above grade and comply with building code requirements. e. Balconies above the first floor may be permitted to project into minimum setbacks up to four feet... f. Bay windows above the first floor may be permitted to project into minimum setbacks... may not project more than three feet into minimum setbacks. g. Suspended planter or flower boxes above the first floor level may project up to 30 inches into minimum setbacks. h. Stoops, stairs, and porches may project into the minimum front yard setback up to five feet when applicable. i. Five feet of clear space shall be required between any projection of a structure and an adjacent property line and 10 feet of clear space between any projections of a structure from any projection of an adjacent structure.' Mechanical equipment is not on this list of permitted intrusions.

equip.cite: Yard Area (UDC Subsection 6.2(B)(5), PDF p.724)
equip.text: 'Every part of a required yard shall be open from its lowest point to the sky unobstructed; except for the ordinary projection of sills, belt courses, cornices, buttresses, and ornamental features; provided, however, none of the projections indicated in Subsection 2.2, shall project into a minimum side yard more than 24 inches. Open or enclosed fire escapes, fireproof outside stairways and balconies projecting into a minimum yard or court no more than three and one-half feet, in addition to the ordinary projections of chimneys and flues may be permitted where the same are so placed as not to obstruct light and ventilation and shall not be considered as an increase to the floor area of the building.'

equip.cite: Shed (UDC Subsection 9.3.W, PDF p.834)
equip.text: 'f. Sheds may only be placed within the rear yard or interior side yard but must not be visible to the general public from the right-of-way. Screening techniques such as fencing and landscaping may be used to ensure the shed is not visible from the right-of-way. g. Sheds must be set back no less than 10 feet from all property lines.'

equip.cite: Swimming Pools and Hot Tubs (UDC Subsection 9.3.Y, PDF p.835)
equip.text: '(1) No private swimming pool or hot tub, or portion thereof, including, but not limited to, aprons, walks, and mechanical equipment, integral to the pool, may be located within a front yard. (2) The outside edge of swimming and wading pools shall not be located closer than five feet from the rear or side lot lines. Swimming pools are not limited to the 25% coverage of any yard area requirement. (3) Such swimming or wading pools shall be enclosed by a security fence at least four feet in height. A screened fence may be substituted for such security fence. However, no screened enclosure shall be located within any required front yard, nor nearer than five feet from any side or rear property line.' This is the one place Milton gives a distance for pool mechanical equipment: it is bound by the pool's own five-foot side/rear limit and is barred from the front yard.

equip.cite: Carport (UDC Subsection 9.3.G, PDF p.823)
equip.text: '(2) A carport is permitted only in the interior side yard, side yard, or rear yard. (3) The total length of a carport is limited to 20 feet. The height of a carport is limited to 20 feet.... (7) Carports are allowed in front yards but shall not encroach into any front setback and must remain under 20 feet in height. (8) Carports are allowed in interior side yards up to the property line, regardless of distance to the principal structure, provided there is a minimum of 10 feet to any adjacent principal structures.'

equip.cite: Accessory buildings in yards — general rule (Appendix A, Art. II, § 3.C(2), PDF p.2050)
equip.text: "Accessory buildings are permitted in side, rear, and secondary front yards only. Accessory structures in the secondary front yard shall meet the front yard requirements of the district for the principal building."

equip.cite: Accessory structures in every residential district and in residential PDPs (Art. IV, § 2, subsection (j) of each district; Art. VIII § 1.K, PDF p.2205)
equip.text: "i. Accessory buildings are permitted in the side, rear and secondary front yards. Such accessory buildings shall be at least five (5) feet from side and rear lot lines. Accessory structures in the secondary front yard shall meet the front yard requirements of the district for the principal building.... v. Detached accessory structures which have impervious roof coverings shall be permitted in the side and rear yard and must be at least five (5) feet from the side and rear property lines. Detached accessory structures in the secondary front yard shall meet the front yard requirements of the district for the principal building." (This is the only setback the Hernando zoning code prints that a ground-mounted standby generator, A/C condenser or pool-equipment pad on a residential lot would fall under — 5 feet from side and rear lot lines. The code contains no separate mechanical-equipment projection or encroachment provision for residential districts.)

equip.cite: Small accessory structures exempt from a zoning permit (Art. IV, § 6.A(7)(d)v., § 6.B(5)v., § 13.A(5)(e))
equip.text: "Accessory buildings or structures five (5) feet or less in height, and smaller than forty (40) square feet in size shall not be required to obtain a zoning permit. Such buildings or structures must meet the minimum yard requirements for accessory buildings in the district." (Printed for the AG, Country 2.5 and A/R districts.) The same subsections add: "There are no minimum yard standards for wellhouses as defined in this ordinance."

equip.cite: Accessory buildings in the AG, Country 2.5, A/R, A/R-1, A/R-2 and CV districts
equip.text: AG and Country 2.5 (Art. IV § 6): accessory buildings and structures associated with the principal agricultural use — maximum height 45 feet; minimum front yard 75 feet (125 feet along U.S. 19, S.R. 50, U.S. 41, U.S. 98, U.S. 301, C.R. 578, C.R. 485 and C.R. 50); "All other yards shall be a minimum of thirty-five (35) feet"; no accessory building closer to the front property line than the district front yard requirement, and "If a single-family dwelling is on or will be on the premises, the accessory building shall be no nearer than fifteen (15) feet to such dwelling." A/R districts (Art. IV § 13.A(5)(c)) and CV (Art. IV § 10.E(1)): "All accessory buildings shall be located at least ten (10) feet from the side or rear property lines, or no closer to the front property line than the front yard requirement for the district. If a single-family dwelling is on, or will be on the premises in the future, the accessory building shall be no nearer than fifteen (15) feet to such dwelling."

equip.cite: Air conditioning and other operational equipment — commercial districts (Art. IV, § 3.E(6), PDF p.2134)
equip.text: "Air conditioning and/or other operational equipment must be oriented away from single family residentially zoned property, or screened to minimize noise impacts and reduce visual incompatibility to the single family residentially zoned property. Screening may include landscape plantings, berms, fences or walls."

equip.cite: Air conditioning and other operational equipment — industrial districts (Art. IV, § 4(7)(f), PDF p.2138)
equip.text: "Air conditioning and/or other operational equipment must be oriented away from single family residentially zoned property, or screened to minimize noise impacts and reduce visual incompatibility to the single family residentially zoned property. Screening may include landscape plantings, berms, fences or walls."

equip.cite: Air conditioning and other operational equipment — planned development projects (Art. VIII, § 6, PDF p.2216)
equip.text: "Air conditioning and/or other operational equipment must be oriented away from single family residentially zoned property, or screened to minimize noise impacts and reduce visual incompatibility to the single family residentially zoned property. Screening may include landscape plantings, berms, fences or walls."

equip.cite: Rooftop HVAC screening (Art. III, § 3.E, PDF p.2073 and p.2079)
equip.text: "Flat roof lengths, longer than one hundred (100) feet in length shall be concealed or addressed utilizing at least one of the following options. (1) Effective concealment of flat roof lines, rooftop equipment and heating, ventilating, and air conditioning (HVAC) units from any facade view by adjacent land uses of lesser intensity, and public rights-of-way by constructing a parapet. The parapet design shall be a minimum of three (3) feet in height..." and "Decorative parapets that are a minimum of three (3) feet in height above the finished roof or that are high enough to block the view of any mechanical equipment."

equip.cite: Ground-level mechanical/HVAC setback for large commercial PDPs (Art. VIII, § 6.B(1), PDF p.2216)
equip.text: Applies only to commercial development with a single building, or a single-site development of multiple buildings with the same use under one owner/manager, greater than 65,000 square feet of gross floor area, which is allowable only through approval as a Planned Development Project: "Mechanical/operational equipment including HVAC located at ground level shall be set back at least one hundred (100) feet from any property line external to the development site and shall be visually shielded through enhanced screening or shall be located [interior to the site]."

equip.cite: Sound and loading separations from single-family residential (Art. IV § 3.E and § 4(7), PDF p.2134 and p.2138)
equip.text: "There shall be no speakers or other sound equipment located within 100 feet of any single family residential district property line... No building within 100 feet of any single family residential district property line shall be more than 20 feet in height. All loading bays and loading docks must be a minimum of 100' from any residential district property line."

equip.cite: Communication towers and their accessory equipment (Art. III, PDF p.2042-2044)
equip.text: "Accessory structures shall meet the required principal structure setbacks of the [district]" and "all accessory equipment and structures shall" meet the tower setback provisions of Art. III § 1.7.

A/R-2.note: Agricultural/Residential-2 District (single-family dwellings and mobile homes). Shares one dimension and area table with A/R and A/R-1.

C-1.frontNote: No single front yard number is printed. The front yard requirement along U.S. 19, S.R. 50, U.S. 41, U.S. 98, U.S. 301, C.R. 578, C.R. 485 shall be 125 feet; along all other functionally classified roads identified on the Existing Functional Classification Map the front setback shall be 75 feet; along all roadways not identified on that map the minimum front yard requirement is 35 feet.
C-1.rearNote: 35 feet. The board may, upon request, reduce the required rear yard where such rear yards would be adjacent to railroad sidings if the reduction would not be detrimental to surrounding areas.
C-1.heightNote: 60 feet. The maximum height permitted (except in C-3) may be increased provided one additional foot is added to each of the required yards for each additional foot of building height over the maximum; in such cases the minimum side yard shall be 35 feet plus one additional foot for each additional foot of height.
C-1.coverageNote: No lot coverage percentage is printed. Maximum building area for a single building, or a single-site development of multiple buildings with the same use under one owner/manager, is limited to 65,000 square feet in all commercial districts; anything larger must apply through the planned development project process.
C-1.note: General Commercial District. Commercial uses on lots adjacent to a residential district shall maintain a minimum setback for all structures of 35 feet in the side or rear yard adjacent to the residential district, the outermost 5 feet of which is a landscaped separation strip with screening 5 to 8 feet high.

C-2.frontNote: 125 feet along U.S. 19, S.R. 50, U.S. 41, U.S. 98, U.S. 301, C.R. 578, C.R. 485; 75 feet along other functionally classified roads on the Existing Functional Classification Map; 35 feet along roadways not on that map.
C-2.rearNote: 35 feet, reducible by the board adjacent to railroad sidings.
C-2.heightNote: 60 feet, increasable one foot per additional foot added to each required yard; side yard then 35 feet plus one foot per additional foot of height.
C-2.coverageNote: No lot coverage printed; 65,000 sq ft maximum building area for a single building or single-site development.
C-2.note: Highway Commercial District. Same 35-foot side/rear setback and screening where adjacent to a residential district.

C-3.frontNote: 125 feet along U.S. 19, S.R. 50, U.S. 41, U.S. 98, U.S. 301, C.R. 578, C.R. 485; 75 feet along other functionally classified roads; 35 feet along roadways not on the Existing Functional Classification Map.
C-3.rearNote: 35 feet, reducible by the board adjacent to railroad sidings.
C-3.heightNote: 35 feet. The height-increase-with-added-yards provision expressly does NOT apply within the C-3 Commercial District.
C-3.coverageNote: No lot coverage printed; 65,000 sq ft maximum building area for a single building or single-site development.
C-3.note: Neighborhood Commercial District. Required land area: C-3 Commercial Districts shall consist of no more than three (3) acres of land area (a maximum, not a minimum lot size). Same 35-foot side/rear setback where adjacent to a residential district.

C-4.frontNote: 125 feet along U.S. 19, S.R. 50, U.S. 41, U.S. 98, U.S. 301, C.R. 578, C.R. 485; 75 feet along other functionally classified roads; 35 feet along roadways not on the map.
C-4.rearNote: 35 feet, reducible by the board adjacent to railroad sidings.
C-4.heightNote: 60 feet, increasable one foot per additional foot added to each required yard; side yard then 35 feet plus one foot per additional foot of height.
C-4.coverageNote: No lot coverage printed; 65,000 sq ft maximum building area.
C-4.note: Heavy Highway Commercial District. Communication tower setbacks: a monopole tower shall meet the setbacks of the C-4 District; a monopole 100 feet or taller shall not be located within 125 percent of its height of any residentially zoned property, and one under 100 feet not within 100 percent of its height, unless that property is used or designated for a nonresidential use.

A-C.frontNote: 125 feet along U.S. 19, S.R. 50, U.S. 41, U.S. 98, U.S. 301, C.R. 578, C.R. 485; 75 feet along other functionally classified roads; 35 feet along roadways not on the map.
A-C.rearNote: 35 feet, reducible by the board adjacent to railroad sidings.

escambia_county.name: Escambia County
escambia_county.source: Land Development Code, Chapter 3 (Zoning Regulations). There is no consolidated dimensional table: each district's numbers sit in its own "(d) Site and building

equip.cite: Accessory structures — setback (§ 3-1.5(g)(3), PDF p.1722)
equip.text: "Accessory structures shall be limited to side and rear yards and be at least five feet from any interior side or rear lot line except where specifically allowed as encroachments. Accessory dwellings shall be limited to the setbacks required for the principal dwelling."

equip.cite: Accessory structures — location (§ 4-7.3(b)(4), PDF p.1891)
equip.text: "An accessory use or structure shall be located on the same lot as the principal use or structure. Accessory structures are limited to locations within side and rear yards, except as specifically allowed by LDC provisions, including the following: a. Large residential lots. Accessory structures, including an accessory dwelling unit, on a lot ten acres in size or larger may be located within the front yard of the principal dwelling if the structures are at least 60 feet from the front lot line. b. Waterfront lots. Accessory structures may be located in the front yard of a waterfront lot if the structures are at least 60 feet from the front lot line and granted conditional use approval by the board of adjustment (BOA).... e. Sewage systems. The underground components of an on-site sewage treatment and disposal system (e.g., septic tank and drain field) may be located within a front yard as necessary to obtain sufficient open space if the components are at least five feet from any lot line."

equip.cite: Encroachments by building features into a required yard (§ 3-1.5(g)(5), PDF p.1722)
equip.text: "Every part of a required yard shall be open from its lowest point to the sky, unobstructed except for the ordinary projection of sills, belt courses, cornices, buttresses, awnings, eaves and similar building features. No such projection shall extend more than 24 inches into any yard, except roof overhangs, awnings, outside stairways, and balconies which may extend up to 48 inches into any yard provided the building setback is otherwise at least ten feet." This list does not name generators, condensers or pool equipment.

equip.cite: Rooftop mechanical equipment and the height limit (§ 3-1.5(h)(2), PDF p.1722)
equip.text: "The district height limits do not apply to belfries, chimneys, church spires, cooling towers, elevator bulkheads, flag poles, television reception antennae, roof-mounted tanks, mechanical equipment rooms, or similar rooftop structures that comply with all of the following conditions: a. They do not separately or in combination with other rooftop structures exceed ten percent of the horizontal roof area. b. They do not exceed applicable airport or airfield height restrictions. c. They do not exceed otherwise applicable height limitations by more than 15 feet or ten percent of actual building height, whichever is greater."

equip.cite: Air conditioning units on a zero lot line wall (§ 4-7.14, PDF p.1919)
equip.text: "Openings on zero lot line side. The wall of the dwelling located on the lot line shall have no windows, doors, air conditioning units or any other type of openings." Same section: "Corner lots. Minimum side yards for corner lots shall not be less than ten feet from the lot line or the street right-of-way line, whichever is greater."

equip.cite: Manufactured-home utility equipment in a flood hazard area (§ 4-2.14(f), PDF p.1844)
equip.text: "Utility equipment that serves manufactured homes, including electric, heating, ventilation, plumbing, and air conditioning equipment and other service facilities, shall comply with the requirements of the Florida Building Code, Residential Section R322, as applicable to the flood hazard area."

equip.cite: Pensacola Beach accessory structures (§ 4-7.3, PDF p.1897)
equip.text: For SRIA leasehold land, accessory structures such as "playhouses, swimming pools outside of structure setbacks, cabanas, gazebos, detached elevated decks, and screened enclosures" are approved "entirely at the discretion of the SRIA", and must meet compatible design, waterfront-location, no-variance and structure-separation conditions: "No wall of the accessory structure is closer than six feet to any wall of the principal structure, and no part of the accessory structure is closer than four feet to any part of the principal structure."

Agr.sideNote: Sides: "On each side, five feet or ten percent of the lot width at the street right-of-way, whichever is greater, but not required to exceed 15 feet."
Agr.heightNote: (3) Structure height: "No maximum structure height unless prescribed by use."
Agr.minLotNote: § 3-2 (4) Lot area: "No minimum lot area unless prescribed by use." The code prints no square-foot minimum for this district.
Agr.note: § 3-2.2. Max density 1 du/20 ac; max FAR 0.25. § 3-1.5(g)(3): "Accessory structures shall be limited to side and rear yards and be at least five feet from any interior side or rear lot line except where specifically allowed as encroachments."

Lot coverage: minimum pervious 30 percent (70 percent maximum semi-impervious and impervious). Max density 1 du/4 ac; max FAR 0.25.

RMU.sideNote: Sides: "On each side, five feet or ten percent of the lot width at the street right-of-way, whichever is greater, but not required to exceed 15 feet."
RMU.heightNote: (3) Structure height: "No maximum structure height unless prescribed by use."
RMU.minLotNote: § 3-2 (4) Lot area: "No minimum lot area unless prescribed by use." The code prints no square-foot minimum for this district.
RMU.lotWidthNote: Same curve exception as RR; 100 feet at the right-of-way for all other new lots.
RMU.note: § 3-2.4. Front and rear: "Forty feet in the front and rear." Sides: "On each side, five feet or ten percent of the lot width at the street right-of-way, whichever is greater, but not required to exceed 15 feet." Lot coverage: minimum pervious 30 percent (70 percent max). Max density 2 du/ac; max FAR 0.25.

LDR.sideNote: Sides: "On each side, five feet or ten percent of the lot width at the street right-of-way, whichever is greater, but not required to exceed 15 feet."

The minimum width for all other new lots is 60 feet at the right-of-way."

Structure height: "A maximum structure height of 45 feet." Lot coverage: minimum pervious 30 percent (70 percent max). Max density 4 du/ac; max FAR 1.0.

desoto_county.source: Code of Ordinances ch. 20 (Land Development Regulations), Article II, Division 4 'Zoning Districts', Secs. 20-125 through 20-144. There is NO consolidated sched

equip.cite: Accessory structures generally (Sec. 20-656(a))
equip.text: (3) Accessory structures shall not be located in a required buffer, landscape area, or minimum building setback area, unless otherwise stated in the LDR. (2) All accessory structures shall comply with standards pertaining to the principal use or structure unless exempted or superseded elsewhere in the LDR. (4) Accessory structures shall be included in all calculations of impervious surface and stormwater runoff. (6) The height and square footage of an accessory structure cannot exceed the height and one-half the actual square feet of a principal building, except in A-5/A-10, for bona fide agricultural uses, for a private garage or carport on a residential lot exceeding 0.34 acre or in a PUD, and for a screen enclosure.

equip.cite: Accessory structure attached to the principal structure (Sec. 20-656(c)(2))
equip.text: An accessory structure attached or connected to a principal structure shall be deemed to be an addition to such structure and subject to the setbacks for the principal structure.

equip.cite: Per-district accessory structure setbacks (A-10, A-5, RSF, RM, RMF, RMF-M, MHS, ROI, P/I)
equip.text: 1. Side yard: five feet. 2. Rear yard: five feet. 3. Front yard: accessory structures are not permitted in the front yard (in A-10 and A-5, 'except for solar facility accessory uses'). In IL and IH the printed minimum yard requirements expressly INCLUDE accessory structures, so the 5-ft allowance does not apply there.

equip.cite: Storage buildings, utility buildings, greenhouses (Sec. 20-657)
equip.text: (a) No accessory buildings used for industrial storage of hazardous, incendiary, noxious, or dangerous materials shall be located nearer than 100 feet from any property line. (b) Storage buildings, greenhouses and the like shall be permitted only in compliance with standards for distance between buildings, and setbacks, if any, from property lines, unless otherwise stated elsewhere in the LDR. (c) Storage and other buildings regulated by this section shall be permitted only in side and rear yards, and shall not encroach into the front yard building setback area, EXCEPT FOR PUMP SHEDS. (d) They shall be included in calculations for impervious surface, floor area ratio, or any other site design requirement applying to the principal use of the lot.

equip.cite: Minimum distance between buildings (Sec. 20-472(a))
equip.text: The minimum distance between adjacent buildings shall be ten feet, measured at the narrowest space between structures, whether a main living unit, principal structure, an allowable attachment, or an accessory use, and shall not include roof overhang (eave).

equip.cite: Setback increase for tall buildings (Sec. 20-472(b))
equip.text: Except for nonresidential uses, when a building exceeds 25 feet in height, the minimum distance from an adjacent building or property line shall be increased by two feet for each story above two.

equip.cite: Corner lots of record (Sec. 20-472(c))
equip.text: In all zoning districts, corner lots of record which do not meet minimum area requirements shall be required to meet only one full depth front yard and all other front yards may be reduced by 50 percent.

equip.cite: Height limit exclusions (Sec. 20-473)
equip.text: Height limits imposed by zoning district regulations shall not apply to customary building appurtenances (spires, ventilators, chimneys, ROOFTOP EQUIPMENT and like) or to antennas, water tanks, silos, windmills and similar structures not intended for human occupancy, provided such heights shall not violate standards prescribed by the Federal Aviation Authority.

equip.cite: Administrative relief for minor accessory-structure setback encroachments (Sec. 20-763)
equip.text: For agricultural, residential single-family and duplex property only, the Chief Building Official or Development Director may grant administrative relief where an ACCESSORY STRUCTURE intrudes into the minimum building or yard setback by not more than FIVE PERCENT of the required setback. This relief does not apply to principal buildings and structures.

equip.cite: Electric substations (all districts listing them)
equip.text: Electric substation in compliance with F.S. 163.3208, as amended, is a permitted use in A-10, A-5, RSF, RM, RMF, RMF-M, MHS, MHP, TTRVC, ROI, PM-I, P/I and RVC. Sec. 20-95(2): 'Automatic substations and switch stations necessary for operation of authorized utility systems that cover more than 80 square feet in size of land area and more than five feet in height' are a SPECIAL EXCEPTION use, and 'electric, coal, and gas generating plants' are likewise a special exception.

equip.cite: Gas/propane cylinders (Sec. 13-16(b), fire code)
equip.text: No person shall place or maintain gas or propane cylinders on porches, breezeways or balconies of multistory buildings.

equip.cite: Noise exemption (Sec. 11-43(a))
equip.text: Air conditioners, lawn mowers, and agricultural pumps are exempt from the noise article when functioning in accordance with the manufacturer's specifications and with all manufacturer's mufflers and noise reducing equipment in use and in proper operating condition.

equip.cite: No generator, A/C, pool-equipment or LP-tank placement rule
equip.text: Washington County's Land Development Code contains NO provision on where a standby generator, an air-conditioning condenser, a pool pump or an LP/propane tank may sit relative to a lot line. The only hits were: an air-conditioning contractor licensing definition (Ch. 18 of the Code of Ordinances); 'air conditioning units' cited as an example of machinery in the noise ordinance definition of 'machinery' (Ch. 30); mechanical equipment named as a kind of litter (Ch. 26 and Ch. 66); hazardous-waste generator classifications; trip generation rates in the road impact fee chapter; and flood-ordinance rules for above-ground tanks (see the flood entry below). None of these sets a setback.

equip.cite: Accessory structures -- the rule that governs a generator pad (§ 2.04.03)
equip.text: 'Barns, pole barns, pool and bath houses, sheds, shops and workshops, and storage buildings, as well as utility buildings, greenhouses, and attached and detached carports and garages. A. Storage buildings, shops, utility buildings, greenhouses, garages, carports, and other accessory structures setbacks shall be established in Table 2.02.06 and shall be determined by the Future Land Use Map category of the property. Accessory structures shall not be located closer than ten (10) feet from any structure. B. Motor vehicles, manufactured homes, mobile homes, trailers, or recreational vehicles shall not be used as storage buildings, utility buildings, or other like uses. C. Building permits are not required for non-residential buildings used for agricultural purposes on bona-fide agricultural properties per F.S. Sec. 604.50(1).' Restated at § 5.01.01.A.5: 'All accessory structures shall meet the setback requirements established in Table 2.02.06, Land Development Code.' In other words, an accessory structure gets the SAME front/side/rear setback as a principal building -- there is no reduced accessory setback in this code.

equip.cite: Separation between structures (§ 2.02.07)
equip.text: 'In addition to the setbacks outlined in Table 2.02.06, and the natural resources setbacks included in Chapter 4, the following setbacks will apply: 1. A minimum ten-foot setback shall be required between buildings and structures.'

equip.cite: Swimming pools (§ 2.04.04)
equip.text: 'A. Swimming pool setbacks shall be established in Table 2.02.06 and shall be determined by the Future Land Use Map category of the property. B. Setbacks for a swimming pool shall be measured from the water's edge. C. Swimming pools shall not be located closer than ten (10) feet from any structure.'

equip.cite: Above-ground tanks in flood hazard areas (Appendix A, Floodplain Management Ordinance, § 306.2)
equip.text: 'Above-ground tanks that do not meet the elevation requirements of Section 306.3 of this ordinance shall be permitted in flood hazard areas provided the tanks are anchored or otherwise designed and constructed to prevent flotation, collapse or lateral movement resulting from hydrodynamic and hydrostatic loads during conditions of the design flood, including the effects of buoyancy assuming the tank is empty.' This is an anchoring rule, not a setback.

equip.cite: Resource-protection setbacks that can control a pad location (Article IV)
equip.text: § 4.04.02.A: 'No development (other than boardwalks, docks, or other shoreline access structures) shall be located within a minimum of thirty (30) feet of a wetland, as measured landward from the upland edge of the wetland.' § 4.04.02.B: 'A minimum fifty-foot development setback is required from the ordinary mean high-water line of all surface water bodies, excluding the Choctawhatchee River, Econfina Creek, Holmes Creek, and Pine Log Creek, which shall require a one-hundred-foot development setback.' § 4.02: 'A setback of five hundred (500) feet shall be required for all development abutting or within five hundred (500) feet of a public water supply well.' § 4.03.02: a minimum 100-foot permanent natural vegetative buffer adjacent to Pine Log State Forest, Falling Waters State Recreational Area, Choctawhatchee Water Management Area, Holmes Creek State Canoe Trail and Econfina State Canoe Trail. Table 4.03 setbacks from specified features: 1st and 2nd magnitude springs 500 ft; 3rd and smaller magnitude springs 500 ft; spring runs 100 ft; sinkholes 100 ft; steephead ravines 100 ft; caves 300 ft; swallets 100 ft.

tamarac.name: Tamarac
tamarac.source: Code of Ordinances Chapter 10, Land Development Code, Article 2 (Zoning Districts): Table 10-2.2 Dimensional Standards for Residential Districts; Table 10-2.3 D

gen.cite: Mechanical equipment - Sec. 10-2.6(C)(6)(b)(ix)
gen.text: "(ix) Mechanical Equipment. A/C units, swimming pool equipment, irrigation pumps, propane tank generators, and backflow devices shall be prohibited in the front yard, and shall comply with the setback provisions in Article 2: Zoning Districts.". This is the operative rule: the equipment gets no projection allowance, is barred from the front yard, and must meet the full district setback.

gen.cite: Screening of accessory structures - Sec. 10-4.4(M)(1)
gen.text: "(1) Accessory Structures. Generators, air conditioning units, bottled gas tanks, irrigation pumps, swimming pool pumps and heaters, garbage containers at ground level, utility boxes, and similar accessory structures shall be screened with shrubs or an opaque fence on all applicable sides. Shrubs planted for this purpose shall be in addition to the requirements in Table 10-4.6 above. A hedge, berm, wood fence, or wall, maintained at a minimum of six inches above the items to be screened, may be used to satisfy the screening requirements as approved by the Director."

gen.cite: Generator noise (community gardens / urban agriculture) - Sec. 10-3.3
gen.text: "(d) Operation of power equipment or generators shall not occur between the hours of 10:00 P.M. and 7:00 A.M."

gen.cite: Generators serving wireless communication facilities - Sec. 10-3.3
gen.text: "No generators utilized in connection with WCFs may be placed in the public rights-of-way, except temporarily in the case of emergency and if approved in advance by the City Engineer."

gen.cite: Temporary generator during emergency housing - Sec. 5-401
gen.text: "d. Electrical service to a commercial source (FPL) must be established. If there is no power available from FPL, the use of a generator will be allowed until power is restored. The use of the generator shall be suspended within seven (7) days of power restoration."

equip.cite: Allowed projections into required setbacks - Sec. 10-2.6(C)(6)
equip.text: "Setbacks shall be unoccupied and unobstructed by any structure or portion of a structure from 30 inches above grade upward, except that certain structures may project into required front, side, or rear setbacks as specified in this subsection." The listed exceptions are unroofed patios and terraces (at least five feet from the lot line), unroofed landings/decks/stairs/balconies, incidental architectural features (not more than three feet), pergolas and trellises (five feet from all side and rear lot lines, prohibited in the front yard), handicap ramps, swimming pools (setbacks measured five feet from the edge of the pool), fences/walls/hedges, freestanding ornamental features, and mechanical equipment.

equip.cite: Projections into easements and rights of way - Sec. 10-2.6(C)(7)
equip.text: "Projections shall not extend or encroach into any easement(s) or right(s)-of-way."

equip.cite: Accessory structures location - Sec. 10-3.4(C)(3)
equip.text: "The accessory use shall be conducted and/or located on the same lot(s) as the principal use and to the rear of the front setback line, unless otherwise approved by the Director. No accessory structure shall be located within ten feet of the site's principal structure. When located to the rear of the primary structure, accessory buildings need not comply with the side or rear setback lines applicable to the primary structure provided that the accessory building is not located closer than ten feet from any alley and not closer than five feet from any property line."

equip.cite: Walkways and driveways - Sec. 10-2.6(C)(5)
equip.text: "Whenever a walkway or driveway is to be located on a lot, it shall be a minimum of three feet from the rear and side property line, except for double-frontage lots."

equip.cite: Air conditioning, mechanical and maintenance equipment - Sec. 9-130(e)(7) (property maintenance, all residential property)
equip.text: "(7) Air conditioning, mechanical and maintenance equipment placed in any front, side or rear yard shall be screened or walled in so as not to be visible from the public rights-of-way and shall not be placed on the roof of any building or structure unless such air conditioning or mechanical equipment is completely screened or walled in so as not to be visible from the public rights-of-way or adjoining properties." The same subsection adds: "(6) All gas and oil tanks must be placed and maintained below ground level or in walled-in areas so as not to be visible from adjacent properties."

equip.cite: Air conditioning or other mechanical equipment - Woodlands Overlay, Sec. 10-2.7(C)(4)(g)
equip.text: "(g) Air conditioning or other mechanical equipment placed in any front, side or rear yard shall be screened or walled in so as not to be visible from the public rights-of-way and shall not be placed on the roof of any building or structure unless such air conditioning or mechanical equipment is completely screened or walled in so as not to be visible from the public rights-of-way or adjoining properties." Subsection (f): "All gas and oil tanks must be placed and maintained below ground level or in walled-in areas so as not to be visible from adjacent properties."

equip.cite: Roof-mounted A/C and accessory equipment - Sec. 5-33 (Chapter 5, Buildings)
equip.text: "(a) The height of exterior walls of all buildings in all zoning districts except R-1, R-1B, R-1C and R-2 shall be higher than the total height of all accessory equipment installed on the roof of the proposed building other than that which is wind-driven. (b) All air-conditioning units, condensers and/or electrical fans attendant thereto, except those that are wind-driven, shall be prohibited from being installed on residential and accessory roof areas, in R-1, R-1B, R-1C and R-2 zoning districts unless the same meets the following requirements: (1) The proposed air-conditioning unit shall be placed on a structural element meeting the requirements of the Florida Building Code, Broward County Amendments... (3) Permanent, obscure screen shall be placed along all sides of the unit which is viewed by the public, the minimum height of which shall be one (1) foot above the top of the unit." NOTE: R-1B and R-1C are districts of the repealed Chapter 24; the cross-reference in this section is to '§ 24-101 et seq.'

equip.cite: Utility sheds - Sec. 5-32(a)
equip.text: "Utility sheds may be permitted providing that they meet the standards set forth in chapter 23 of the Broward Edition of the South Florida Code and provided that such utility shed is not placed in any required setback. A building permit shall be required in any residential district of the city."

gen.cite: PERMANENT GENERATORS - Art. 5.B.1.A.19.b.1)d), Location and Setbacks, PDF p.940
gen.text: 'Generators shall meet the district setback requirements for principal structures, but shall not be located between the front or side street facade of a building and a R-O-W or in an easement, unless: (1) Encroachment is limited to ten percent of setback; (2) Where applicable, the Applicant indicates that an HOA has been notified of the application for Building Permit; (3) The generator shall be screened from view from any public rights-of-way or adjacent property lines by an opaque fence/wall; and, (4) If this criteria cannot be met, the Applicant may apply for a Type 1 Variance, pursuant to Art. 2.C.5.F.' THIS IS THE GOVERNING RULE FOR A STANDBY GENERATOR PAD IN PALM BEACH COUNTY.

gen.cite: PERMANENT GENERATORS - residential setback exception, Art. 5.B.1.A.19.b.2)b), PDF p.941
gen.text: 'Generators less than five feet in height measured from the top of the supporting platform may be allowed within the required side and rear setbacks. The generator rear and side setbacks shall be a minimum of five feet. For SFDs and residential uses within a SFD, the generator side setback shall be a minimum of three feet, and rear setback shall be a minimum of five feet.' Art. 5.B.1.A.19.b.2a, Number: 'A maximum of one generator shall be allowed on a lot with a single dwelling unit. A maximum of one generator per structure shall be permitted for Multifamily developments, with exception to condominiums, which shall be permitted one generator per unit.' Art. 5.B.1.A.19.b.4, Non-Residential: 'There is no limitation to the number of generators.'

gen.cite: PERMANENT GENERATORS - screening, sound and exercise, Art. 5.B.1.A.19.b.1), PDF p.940
gen.text: a Maximum Permissible Sound Level: refer to Art. 5.E.4.B.2 and Table 5.E.4.B, Maximum Sound Levels. b Screening: 'Generators that are not located within, or completely screened by a building, shall be screened from view when adjacent to or visible from a public R-O-W or parcels with a conservation or residential FLU designation or use. Screening may include the use of fences, walls or hedges, or a combination thereof.' c Maintenance Cycle: 'Generators may be operated for exercising purposes one time per week, excluding Sundays, for a period not exceeding 30 minutes between the hours of 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.'

gen.cite: PERMANENT GENERATORS - when one is required, Art. 5.B.1.A.19.a, PDF p.939-940
gen.text: 'Use of permanent generators shall be permitted during periods of electrical power outages in utility systems maintained by the utility service provider or when the BCC declares a State of Emergency.' 'A permanent emergency generator or alternative power source shall be required for all assisted living facilities, excluding personal residences (owner occupied) used as an assisted living facility for five or fewer residents, nursing homes, intermediate care facilities for people with developmental disabilities, or transitional living facilities for brain and spinal cord injury patients, pursuant to F.S. 400.492 and Rule 59A-8.027, F.A.C., and PDD or TDD clubhouses 20,000 square feet, or greater.' Exemptions: developments with a BCC or DRO-approved plan graphically indicating a clubhouse, except projects exceeding 75 percent or more of the Improvement Value; renovations or additions not exceeding 75 percent of Improvement Value; a PDD or TDD clubhouse in the Coastal High Hazard Area; and a PDD or TDD that already has one compliant clubhouse generator. Required capacity (Art. 5.B.1.A.19.b.3): essential electrical systems, lighting for a minimum of 30 percent of GFA, air conditioning for 30 percent of GFA including the largest meeting room, and fuel storage sufficient to operate the generator for a minimum of 72 hours at full load capacity.

gen.cite: PERMANENT GENERATORS - Type 1 Waiver in a PIPD Industrial Pod, Table 3.B.4.F, PDF p.342
gen.text: 'Art. 5.B.1.A.19, Permanent Generators - Permanent generators may be allowed within required side or rear building setbacks' - criteria: 'When all parcels adjacent to the generator location are within an Industrial Pod of the PIPD.' The same table also waives the ground-mounted mechanical equipment screening requirement of Art. 5.B.1.A.20.a.2a in that circumstance.

gen.cite: HVAC units permitted in setbacks - Art. 3.D.1.D.5.a.11), PDF p.473
gen.text: The list of 'Structures, Projections, and Improvements Permitted in Setbacks' includes, at item 11, 'Heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning units (including compressors and condensers)'. NO distance is attached to this item - it is an unqualified permission to place an HVAC unit within a required setback. Related items on the same list: item 23 'Utility transmission lines and associated structures'; item 22 'Wells'; item 28 'Fire hydrants and other government service/utility structures required to be in certain locations by applicable Codes and Ordinances'; item 16 'Roof overhangs projecting into the required setback a maximum of two and one-half feet'; item 3 'Permanent/retractable awnings, canopies, or Bahama shutters projecting a maximum of three feet into a setback'; item 15 'Recreational equipment and structures in the rear setback of residential districts'; item 24 'Basketball goals, provided there is a minimum three-foot setback from the rear and side property lines and a minimum 15-foot setback from the front and side street property lines'. Note the contrast: HVAC is on this list, generators are NOT - generators are governed separately by Art. 5.B.1.A.19 and must meet the principal-structure setback except as that section allows.

gen.cite: Definition of Fixed Mechanical Equipment - Art. 1.H, PDF p.89
gen.text: 'Fixed Mechanical Equipment - mechanical equipment, such as an air-conditioning unit, water-cooling tower, swimming pool pump, irrigation pump, well water pump, fan, POWER GENERATOR, or other similar power source equipment, permanently affixed to land or structure, as distinguished from temporary, portable, non-fixed mechanical equipment.' This definition is what brings a standby generator inside the Art. 5.E.4.B sound-level standards.

equip.cite: MECHANICAL EQUIPMENT - Art. 5.B.1.A.20, PDF p.942
equip.text: a.1a Setback Exceptions: 'Setback exceptions shall be applied pursuant to Art. 3.D.1.D.5, Setback Exceptions.' b Height Exceptions: 'Height exceptions shall be applied pursuant to Art. 3.D.1.E.4, Height Exceptions.' 2 Screening Requirements: 'New and replacement equipment shall be screened on all sides by an opaque barrier constructed of materials, and color compatible with the building or structure, or equivalent landscaping for ground-mounted equipment, to a minimum height equal to the highest point of the equipment.' Roof-mounted screening exemptions: equipment less than one foot in height measured from the roof deck and painted to match; any industrial use with an industrial FLU designation adjacent to a parcel with an industrial use and industrial FLU designation; where a certified letter from a Florida-registered structural Engineer or Architect shows the roof cannot support the screening weight; or any industrial use with an industrial FLU designation where a Line of Sight Analysis shows the equipment cannot be viewed from the adjacent R-O-W.

equip.cite: FUEL, GAS, OR CHEMICAL STORAGE TANKS (LP/propane) - Art. 5.B.1.A.7, PDF p.920
equip.text: 'Above-ground accessory fuel, gas, or chemical storage tanks, three feet or greater in height shall be subject to the zoning district setbacks or the minimum setbacks required by the Florida Building and Fire Prevention Codes, whichever is greater, and screening. New and replacement storage tanks shall be screened from view if adjacent to a residential use or FLU designation and visible from an adjacent R-O-W. The screening shall consist of an opaque barrier or equivalent landscaping a minimum height equal to the highest point of the storage tanks.'

equip.cite: Accessory structures - general location rule, Art. 5.B.1.A.1.b, PDF p.903
equip.text: 'All accessory uses and structures except for approved off-site parking, shall be located on the same lot as the principal use. No accessory structure shall be located in the front or side street yard except for dumpsters, or unless stated otherwise herein.' General Exceptions (Art. 5.B.1.A.1.b.1) allow fences and walls, entry features for access ways internal to a PUD, bike racks, outdoor recreation amenities and support structures such as cabanas within a Neighborhood Recreation Facility or Recreation Pod, and the structures, projections and improvements listed in Art. 3.D.1.D.5 - but that exception EXPRESSLY EXCLUDES 'mechanical equipment accessory to a building' from being allowed within front or side street yards.

equip.cite: Accessory structure setbacks - Art. 5.B.1.A.1.d, PDF p.904-906
equip.text: Residential Districts: Accessory Living Quarters (Guest Cottages, Grooms Quarters, other Accessory Quarters) shall meet the minimum setback in Table 3.D.1.A, except properties with an RR FLU designation which are subject to a 25-foot side or rear setback. Townhouse: accessory structures shall meet Table 3.D.2.A, and no detached accessory building other than permitted fences or walls on any lot less than 30 feet wide. ZLL: accessory structures shall meet Table 3.D.2.B. Single Family and Multifamily in residential zoning districts and AR lots less than one acre: 'Accessory structures ten feet or less in height shall meet a minimum five-foot setback from the side and rear property lines. Accessory structures over ten feet in height shall meet the minimum setbacks in Table 3.D.1.A.' Within the AR district on lots one acre and greater: lots five acres or greater, minimum 25 feet; lots one acre or greater and less than five acres, minimum 15 feet. Accessory structures, excluding fences, shall be a minimum of five feet from all established drainage easements in AR districts. Accessory structures shall NOT be located within a required landscape buffer, or in an established easement unless exempted by Art. 5.F.2.A. Non-residential districts: accessory structures shall meet the Table 3.D.1.A setbacks. In the U/S Tier, all accessory structures on a parcel in a residential district shall not occupy more than 25 percent of the distance between property lines.

equip.cite: Setback reductions - Art. 3.D.1.D.4, PDF p.472
equip.text: 'No setback reduction shall be used in combination with any other setback reduction allowed by this Code.' a Open Space: in residential zoning districts in the U/S Tier, or the Residential Pod of an AGR-PUD, the rear and side setbacks along the length of a property line adjacent to dedicated open space defined by a minimum of 50 feet in width may be reduced by 25 percent. b Alleys: in commercial and industrial districts, the rear and side setbacks from an alley may be reduced by 50 percent. c Railroad R-O-W: in industrial districts, the setback from a railroad R-O-W may be reduced to the width of the required landscape buffer.

equip.cite: Dumpsters - Art. 5.B.1.A.8.c, PDF p.920
equip.text: 'Shall be set back a minimum of 25 feet from all property lines adjacent to residential zoning districts and uses. If adjacent to a non-residential zoning district or use, the landscape buffer width shall serve as the setback.' Storage areas shall have a minimum dimension of ten feet by ten feet and shall not encroach into easements, landscape buffers, or parking spaces.

equip.cite: Electric Transmission Substations - PDF p.777
equip.text: 'Buildings used for Electric Transmission Substations shall be set back a minimum of 50 feet from all property lines. Setbacks for mechanical equipment, related structures, and fencing shall be a minimum of 75 feet, or a minimum of 150 feet when adjacent to or visible from a street or parcels with a [residential FLU designation].'

gen.cite: Definition - 'Outdoor Mechanical Equipment, Residential' (Article 10, PDF p.531)
gen.text: "OUTDOOR MECHANICAL EQUIPMENT, RESIDENTIAL. Electric generators and accessories, utility meters, swimming pool heaters and pumps, and other similar features." This is the definition that brings a standby generator under the rules below.

gen.cite: Site plan exemption - Sec. 2.x Site Plan applicability (PDF p.77)
gen.text: The following development is exempt from site plan review: "3. Installation of generators or other mechanical equipment for operation of a permitted use on site."

equip.cite: Placement - Sec. 4.3.4(n), Outdoor Mechanical Equipment, Residential
equip.text: "Outdoor mechanical equipment shall be located to the rear or side of the principal building on the lot."

equip.cite: Encroachment - Table 10.2.4(a): Allowable Encroachments beyond Setbacks/Build-to Zones
equip.text: The rows 'Air conditioner compressor unit', 'Outdoor mechanical equipment, residential' and 'Solar energy collection facility, small scale' share one entry: "May be located beyond the setback in any side or rear yard, subject to the limitations in Sec. 4.3.4, Specific Standards for Accessory Uses and Structures." 'Accessory structures other than those listed above' read: "May be located beyond the setback in a side or rear yard, subject to the limitations in Sec. 4.3.3, Standards for All Accessory Uses and Structures."

equip.cite: Accessory-structure setbacks - Sec. 4.3.3(c)
equip.text: "Accessory uses and structures shall comply with the minimum yard requirements for the principal structures for which they are accessory in Article 3: Zone Districts, unless otherwise stated in this LDC, and except as follows: (1) On lots with one front yard: (A) Accessory uses and structures other than accessory dwellings such as cottage residences shall be located at least seven-and-one-half (7.5) feet from a rear property line. Cottage residences shall not be in a required rear yard. (B) No accessory uses and structures shall be in required front or side yards. (2) On lots with two (2) front yards (e.g. double frontage, through, or corner lots) in Residential zone districts: (A) Accessory structures may not be in either front yard but may be in one of the required side yards. (B) Any accessory use or structure shall be located at least seven-and-one-half (7.5) feet from any side yard property line." Sec. 4.3.3(b)(3)(C) adds that in Residential zone districts an accessory structure shall "Not be constructed closer to the lot line in a front yard than the principal building or structure to which the use is subordinate," and (b)(5) that it shall "Not intrude into the sight triangle along any street."

equip.cite: Air conditioner compressor - Sec. 4.3.4(a)(1)(A), Residential zone districts
equip.text: "For all residential uses in Residential zone districts, an air conditioner compressor placed in a required side or rear yard setback shall have its nearest point located no further than three (3) feet from the principal structure which it serves."

equip.cite: Air conditioner compressor replacement - Sec. 4.3.4(a)(1)(B)
equip.text: For nonresidential uses in Residential zone districts, where a compressor was in a required rear or side yard as of May 24, 2004, a replacement may be installed in the same location if it is less than five (5) tons and, outside Winfield Units 1 and 2, "replacement air conditioner compressors that are closer than five (5) feet from any side or rear property line or that are within the required side or rear yard and are higher than thirty (30) inches above ground level, shall be subject to the sound rating requirements in Table 4.3.4(a)(1)(B)." Table 4.3.4(a)(1)(B): 4 tons and below 80 decibels; between 4 and 5 tons 84 decibels, measured per AHRI Standard 270-2015.

equip.cite: Air conditioner compressor - Sec. 4.3.4(a)(2), Mixed-Use and Nonresidential districts
equip.text: "in all Mixed-Use and Nonresidential Districts, a new air conditioner compressor, chiller, and/or evaporator unit of an air handler system shall not be located in any required yard."

equip.cite: Pool equipment screening - Sec. 4.3.4 (swimming pools), PDF p.268
equip.text: "In Winfield Units 1 and 2 (single-family residential subdivisions) annexed by Ordinance No. 970, if the pool is located within any front or street side yard, the pool equipment shall be screened from view by landscaping, except if the screening would create a hazardous obstruction to visibility of vehicles or pedestrians."

equip.cite: Swimming pool - Table 10.2.4(a)
equip.text: "May be located beyond the setback, but neither the pool nor enclosure shall be less than five feet from a lot line."

equip.cite: Fence and wall heights around equipment - Table 5.8.4(a)
equip.text: Front yard in RSF-1, RSF-2, RSF-3, RSF-D, R-MF and MX districts 4 feet; front yard in WS, GAP, NC and PD districts 6 feet; side, street side or rear yard (all districts) 8 feet.

equip.cite: Yard and measurement of setbacks (Sec. 16-139(1)) - the operative rule
equip.text: "Every part of front, side, and rear yards shall be unoccupied and vacant from the ground upward, except for eaves, trees, shrubs, landscaping materials, driveways, sunken garbage collection containers, and in rear or side yards, accessory buildings as permitted by this chapter." Mechanical equipment is NOT on this list, so a ground-mounted generator is treated as an accessory structure and falls under Sec. 16-176.

equip.cite: Yard projections (Sec. 16-139(3))
equip.text: "Open or enclosed fire escapes, outside stairways and balconies projecting into a minimum yard or court, and the projection of chimneys and flues are permitted into yard areas, but not to exceed 32 inches."

equip.cite: Accessory structure placement (Sec. 16-176(b)(3))
equip.text: "For residential lots less than two acres, no detached accessory structure shall be located in any required front yard area. Detached accessory structures may be located in the required rear or side yards. For residential lots exceeding two acres, detached accessory structures may be located in the front yard, rear yard, or side yard. On a corner lot, no accessory structure shall be located closer to the side street right-of-way line than the principal structure."

equip.cite: Accessory structure separation and non-residential limits (Sec. 16-176(c)(1))
equip.text: "A detached accessory structure shall not be closer than four feet to the principal building, or closer than five feet to any other accessory building on the same lot. Within nonresidential districts, accessory structures, except for carports, are prohibited within the side and rear yards of lots adjacent to a neighborhood district."

equip.cite: Accessory structure size and height (Sec. 16-176(c)(2)-(3))
equip.text: "Any number of accessory structures are permitted provided that the maximum lot coverage of all accessory structures shall not exceed 50 percent of the total area of the required yards. The total floor area of all accessory structures may not exceed a maximum of 2,500 square feet." "Accessory structures shall not exceed height requirements of the respective zoning district. For residential zoning districts, accessory structures may not exceed 25 feet in height." Table 16-176.1 lists the permitted accessory structures; mechanical equipment is not among them, but the table ends with "Any other building or use that the development director determines is customarily incidental to the permitted principal use or principal building - All zoning districts", and Sec. 16-176(e) allows the development director to determine other accessory uses by interpretation.

equip.cite: Height exceptions (Sec. 16-137(a))
equip.text: "Any chimney, water, fire, radio and television tower, church spire, dome, cupola, cooling tower, elevator bulkhead, smoke stack, flagpole, parapet wall and similar structures and their necessary mechanical appurtenances must have approval of the town council to be located above the height limits herein established; however the heights of these structures or appurtenances thereto shall not exceed the height limitations set forth by FAA regulations affecting the height."

equip.cite: Generators and noise (Sec. 20-65)
equip.text: The noise ordinance's list of exempt sounds includes "(9) Generators used during or as a result of an emergency." A generator run outside an emergency (e.g. a weekly exercise cycle) is not exempted by that clause.

equip.cite: Air conditioning condensate (sewer use ordinance)
equip.text: "Also prohibited are the following: connection of down spouts or air conditioning condensate lines into the sewer system."

equip.cite: Antenna support equipment (wireless telecommunications section)
equip.text: "Stealth design means a method that would hide or conceal an antenna, supporting electrical or mechanical equipment, or any other support structure that is identical to, or closely compatible with, the color to the supporting structure so as to make the antenna and related equipment as visually unobtrusive as possible." Applies to tower/antenna equipment only.

PUD.frontNote: Sec. 16-115(b): "Development standards that depart from certain standards of this Code may be proposed and approved through the PUD process in consideration of unique, innovative, and superior project design. Where not specified in the PUD, the applicable standards of this Code shall apply. Standards that may be varied shall include the following: (1) Setbacks. (2) Lot coverage. (3) Height." Sec.
