equip.text: A yard extending between side lot lines, parallel across the front of a lot adjoining a street. In cases of through lots and corner lots, front yards shall be provided on all frontages. The minimum front building setback distance shall be maintained at every point along the street.

The height limitations contained in the schedule of district regulations of Table 3-1 do not apply to water tanks, ventilators, or appurtenances required to be placed on the roof and not intended for human occupancy.... Non-architectural items extending above or on rooftops which are not governed by the Florida Building Code's height requirements, such as building-mounted flag poles, chimneys, and mechanical equipment, and associated appurtenances shall not extend more than fifteen (15) feet above the eave line. Items on rooftops which are governed by the Florida Building Code's height restrictions shall be limited to the minimum height necessary.

equip.cite: App. A, § 5.11(B), Screening Standards [PDF p. 796]
equip.text: Utility fixtures, ventilation equipment, and mechanical equipment, when outside a structure, shall be screened with walls, fences, dense plant material, or a combination thereof.

equip.cite: App. A, § 5.11(A), Screening Standards [PDF p. 796]
equip.text: Service areas visible from a public right-of-way or abutting properties shall be screened by a six-foot high panel fence or wall, or a combination of berms, panel fences. walls, and landscaping to create a six-foot high screen.

equip.cite: App. A, § 6.11(B), Landscaping of Dumpster Enclosures, Utility and Mechanical Equipment and Signs [PDF p. 812]
equip.text: Utility Fixtures, Ventilation Equipment, Mechanical Equipment. Utility fixtures, ventilation equipment, and mechanical equipment shall be screened with fences, walls, plant materials, berms, or a combination of the above.

equip.cite: § 15.710.5 Yard encroachments, intro [PDF p.536]
equip.text: Every part of a required yard shall be pen and unobstructed from the ground to the sky except as hereinafter provided or as otherwise permitted by this Chapter:.

equip.cite: § 15.710.5(7) Yard encroachments [PDF p.536]
equip.text: Air conditioner units and other mechanical equipment may extend not over four (4) feet into a required side or rear yard.

equip.cite: § 15.710.5(6) Yard encroachments [PDF p.536]
equip.text: Accessory parking may be located in a required side yard if the area so used for parking is properly screened from adjacent property by a fence, wall or planting.

equip.cite: § 15.710.4(2) Accessory uses, buildings or structures [PDF p.535—536]
equip.text: Except as otherwise provided in this Section, detached accessory buildings and structures, including but not limited to garages, carports and storage sheds, but excluding uses set forth under Subsection (a) above, may be located within a rear yard; provided that no such building or structure shall be located nearer than five (5) feet to any property line and not closer than ten (10) feet to the principal structure. An additional setback from a lot line of one (1) foot shall be required for each foot of total building or structure height exceeding eleven (11) feet, until a setback of ten (10) feet is reached.

equip.cite: § 15.710.4 Accessory uses, buildings or structures, intro [PDF p.535]
equip.text: Pool and accessory structure setbacks shall be in full compliance with the yard and buffering requirements of the applicable zoning district, except as follows:.

equip.cite: § 15.575(5) Accessory uses, buildings, or structures [PDF p.476]
equip.text: There shall be full compliance with the yard and buffering requirements of the applicable zoning district except as follows: Except as otherwise provided in this section, detached accessory buildings and structures, including, but not limited to, garages, carports, and storage sheds may be located only within a rear or side yard; provided that no such building or structure shall be located nearer than five (5) feet to any property line and not closer than ten (10) feet to the principal structure. An additional setback from a lot line of one (1) foot shall be required for each foot of total building or structure height exceeding eleven (11) feet until a setback of ten (10) feet is reached.

equip.cite: § 15.575(1)—(3) Accessory uses, buildings, or structures [PDF p.475]
equip.text: Only principal uses are listed as permitted uses within each zoning district. In addition, accessory uses, buildings, or structures as herein defined may be located upon any lot, subject to the following provisions: (1) Accessory buildings and structures shall be limited to a maximum height of twenty-four (24) feet; (2) Total combined building coverage of all principal and accessory buildings and structures shall not exceed the maximum building coverage allowed within the applicable zoning district; (3) No permanent building or structure shall be located within a publicly dedicated easement.

equip.cite: § 15.205 Definitions — Side setback [PDF p.399]
equip.text: Side setback. The distance between the side property line and the side line of a building, measured from the building, not the overhang; excluding uncovered patios and decks, air conditioners, wells, pumps, motors, water purifiers, and other utility systems or appurtenances. (The "side" setback must at least be equal to "required side yard" which may be all, or part, of the "side" yard.)

equip.cite: § 15.205 Definitions — Rear setback [PDF p.397]
equip.text: Rear setback. The distance between the rear property line and the rear line of a building, excluding uncovered patios and decks. (The "rear" setback must at least be equal to the "required rear yard" which may be all, or part of the "rear yard."). To be measured from the building not the overhang.

equip.cite: § 15.205 Definitions — Front setback [PDF p.386]
equip.text: Front setback. The distance between the street right-of-way line and the front line of a building, excluding uncovered steps. (The "front" setback must at least be equal to the "required front yard" which may be all, or part, of "front yard" as defined in Article II of this Chapter. In case of curvilinear front property lines, setbacks are measured from the tangent connecting the arc of the side property lines).

equip.cite: § 15.205 Definitions — Structure [PDF p.402]
equip.text: Structure. Anything constructed or erected, installed or portable, with a fixed locations on the ground, or attached to something having a fixed location on the ground, the use of which requires a location on a parcel of land. It includes a movable structure while it is located on land which can be used for housing, business, commercial, agricultural, or office purposes either temporarily or permanently. "Structure" also includes billboards, swimming pools, poles, pipelines, transmission lines, tracks and advertising signs.

equip.cite: § 15.205 Definitions — Foundation survey [PDF p.385]
equip.text: If the slab is monolithic, the "foundation" survey must also show total square footage covered by the foundation, including all porches, breezeways, patios, garages, or carports, but shall not include pads for accessory structures such as air conditioners, pool pumps, etc.

equip.cite: § 15.710.3(a) Yard Requirements, R-10/R-9/R-7.5/R-7/R-6/R-6M/R-5/R-5M [PDF p.530]
equip.text: As to any lot platted after January 1, 1991, no principal structure, swimming pool, accessory building or other structure shall be located nearer than twenty-five (25) feet to any environmental jurisdictional (DER) line or, where no such environmental jurisdictional line has been established, to the established mean high water line of East Bay, or its tributaries. As to any lot platted before January 1, 1991 no principal structure shall be located nearer than twenty (20) feet to any environmental jurisdictional (DER) line or, where no such environmental jurisdictional line has been established, to the established mean high water line of East Bay, or its tributaries. Further, as to any lot platted before January 1, 1991, no swimming pool, accessory building or other accessory structure shall be located nearer than ten (10) feet to any environmental jurisdictional (DER) line or, where no such environmental jurisdictional line has been established, to the established mean high water line of East Bay, or its tributaries.

equip.cite: § 15.710.3(d)(6) PROF — setbacks for other structures and pads [PDF p.533]
equip.text: Setbacks. The minimum setbacks for other structures, parking lots, on-site private roads and parking aisles (excluding access drives), private walkways, swimming pools, tennis courts or pads for decorative of recreational use shall be: a. Twenty-five (25) feet, fully landscaped, from any road rights-of-way, whether said road rights-of-way are public or private. b. Ten (10) feet fully landscaped from any site or rear property boundaries. c. If the property is located adjacent to a single family detached residential zoning district, one hundred (100) feet therefrom; provided, however, that City Commission may permit a smaller setback, to a minimum of twenty-five (25) feet... d. If the property is located along East Bay or it's tributaries, one hundred fifty (15) feet therefrom or fifty (50) feet from the DER jurisdictional line, whichever is greater...

equip.cite: § 15.750.4 Material and equipment storage in residential zoning districts [PDF p.598—599]
equip.text: The storage of materials, supplies, appliances or equipment used or designed for commercial or industrial use, and the outdoor storage of home appliances and inoperative vehicles is hereby expressly prohibited in any residential zoning district.... This subsection shall not apply to the storage of building materials on a lot if said building materials are being used for construction of a building on said lot in conformity with the terms of this Chapter and this Subsection shall not be deemed to prohibit the restoration of vehicles within an enclosed garage or privacy fence.

equip.cite: § 15.755.5 Swimming pools — Mechanical equipment [PDF p.605]
equip.text: Electric motor driven pumps shall be well ventilated. Pumps may be installed above ground or may be installed in a pit on condition that the pit is provided with appropriate drain line to adequate absorption pit, storm sewers, East Bay or other positive outfall facilities.

equip.cite: § 15.755.8 Swimming pools — Setbacks and ground (lot) coverage [PDF p.605—606]
equip.text: Except as otherwise may be provided as Zoning Standards in other parts of this Chapter: (1) Swimming pools, patios, decks and other outdoor living areas, including screened enclosures, not have a roof impervious to weather, may be located within a rear yard; provided that no such allowed uses shall be located nearer than five (5) feet to any property line. (2) An additional setback from the lot line of one (1) foot shall be required for each foot to total height that such an enclosure not having a roof impervious to the weather exceeds eleven (11) feet, until a setback of ten (10) feet is reached. (3) The total ground coverage of all principal and accessory structures shall not exceed forty-seven and one-half (47.50) percent of the lot or lots' area. Ground coverage calculations shall include all structures, pools, decks, driveways, walkways and pads for recreational decorative use.

equip.cite: § 15.535(d)(4) and § 15.540(d)(4) — rooftop equipment [PDF p.431, p.434]
equip.text: Structure height. Maximum structure height shall be fifty feet or five stories, whichever is less. Rooftop heating and cooling units shall be allowed if the height exceeds fifty feet as long as the structure is five stories or less.

equip.cite: § 15.710.6 Exclusion from height limits [PDF p.537]
equip.text: Penthouses, scenery lofts, towers, cupolas, steeples and domes, not exceeding in gross area at maximum horizontal section thirty (30) percent of the room area and flag poles, airplane beacons, broadcasting towers, antennas, chimneys, stacks, tanks and roof structures used only for ornamental or mechanical purposes may exceed the permissible height limit in any district by not more than twenty-five (25) percent. Parapet walls may extend not more than five (5) feet above the allowable height of the building.

equip.cite: § 15.780.14 Security fence screening requirements [PDF p.647]
equip.text: All public or private utility structures and facilities, including, but not limited to, retention ponds, sanitary sewer lift stations, water supply or irrigation wells, pumps or meters, telephone switching facilities, electric generation or transmission facilities, and cable television receiving and transmission facilities which, for security, safety or other considerations, are enclosed on any side by a security fence not complying with the requirements of this Chapter for solid buffers or wood fence buffers, shall be subject to City approval and shall be screened by a landscaped buffer so as to screen said fence from view of all exterior sides, except where gates providing pedestrian or vehicular access are located.

equip.cite: § 15.561.2(h)(4) North Tyndall Parkway Special Overlay District [PDF p.446]
equip.text: Service areas and utilities shall be fully screened with walls, fences or other forms, which are to be compatible with the building in materials/color. Such structures shall be constructed of similar materials and designed for durability and easy maintenance.

equip.cite: § 15.715.13(f) Flood damage protection — Utility equipment [PDF p.557]
equip.text: Utility equipment. Utility equipment that serves manufactured homes, including electric, heating, ventilation, plumbing, and air conditioning equipment and other service facilities, shall comply with the requirements of the Florida Building Code, Residential Section R322, as applicable to the flood hazard area.

equip.cite: § 15.575(6) Accessory uses, buildings, or structures [PDF p.476]
equip.text: Conex boxes, cargo shipping containers, and other similar structures used for storage or other accessory purposes are prohibited.

equip.cite: § 15.580 Temporary uses — Dwelling units [PDF p.476]
equip.text: Recreational vehicles, travel trailers, or government-provided temporary living accommodations may be established, erected, or placed within any zoning district for temporary occupancy as a single family dwelling unit upon (1) the declaration of a state of emergency by the Governor, (2) the declaration of a state of emergency by the Mayor, and (3) order of the City Manager. Building set backs shall not apply to the placement of any such temporary dwelling unit.

gen.text: Electric meters, fuse boxes, generator control boxes and tankless hot water heaters shall be allowed to be mounted on a wall or structure, provided such attachments do not horizontally extend beyond the roof overhang or two (2) feet from the exterior face of the wall, whichever is less. Hose bibs shall be allowed to extend no further than two (2) feet horizontally from the exterior face of the wall.
Permanently installed generators shall not extend any closer than seven (7) feet to the closest property line.

gen.cite: Sec. 2-36 Portable generators [PDF p. 117]
gen.text: (a) The use and operation of a portable auxiliary electrical generator is prohibited within or on the following areas: (1) Within five (5) feet of any opening (includes but is not limited to doors and windows) into a building or structure; (2) Within garages, enclosed or partially enclosed areas, or under eaves or other overhangs; (3) On roofs or roof areas, balconies, ingress/egress areas and discharge ways, including but not limited to walkways, stairways and stairwells. (b) The generator shall be operated in a safe manner and in accordance with NFPA 70, the National Electric Code and all other applicable laws, regulations and town ordinances.

equip.cite: Sec. 30-66(c) introductory [PDF p. 421]
equip.text: Encroachments into setbacks in the RE, RS, RML, RMM and RMH zoning districts:.
Unless otherwise provided in the Code, the following structures are allowed in the side or rear required setbacks as set forth herein.

Air conditioner condensers, pool heaters, pool equipment or heat pumps, not to exceed five (5) feet in height, from the finished grade, unless otherwise approved by the building official due to flood elevation requirements, shall not extend any closer than seven (7) feet to the closest property line.
Steps/stairways for the principal building shall not extend any closer than seven (7) feet to the closest property line.
If the rear property line borders a body of water, screen enclosures may extend to not less than five (5) feet from the right-of-way line or bulkhead line, whichever is further landward.
Unless otherwise provided in the Code, the following structures are allowed in front, side or rear required setbacks as set forth herein.
All fences, walls, and hedges may be erected or maintained along or adjacent to a lot line, and shall comply with the requirements of subsection 30-68(e).
Buried propane tanks, where the fillable portion of the tank is at or below the adjacent natural grade shall not extend any closer than seven (7) feet to the closest property line.

Equipment allowed in setbacks that emit noise, odors or fumes shall be fully shielded or screened via landscaping in such a way to minimize such noise, odor or fumes as required by the building official prior to the issuance of a permit.

Repair and maintenance of existing equipment and structures within the setback areas is allowed. Replacement is also permitted so long as the equipment is being replaced in the same location and the replacement equipment does not result in any additional encroachment into the required setback.

equip.cite: Sec. 30-67(c)(1) Separation [PDF p. 431]
equip.text: A freestanding accessory structure shall not be located within five (5) feet of any other principal or accessory building.

equip.cite: Sec. 30-67(c)(2) Encroachments [PDF p. 431]
equip.text: Fences, walls, vegetation, poles, and other customary yard accessories, pool decks, ornaments, and furniture may be permitted in any yard subject to height limitations and visibility requirements.

For single-family dwellings, heating, ventilating, air conditioning, and exhaust equipment, and radio or television antenna shall not exceed the height of a parapet wall. In the absence of a parapet wall, such equipment shall be screened in a manner consistent with the architectural style, colors, and materials of the principal structure.

Exceptions. Exceptions to building heights shall include such functional and nonfunctional architectural features as chimneys, cupolas, towers, dormers, parapet walls, domes, and spires. Mechanical features are considered exceptions to height limitations include heating, ventilating, and air conditioning equipment, and flagpoles and radio or television antennae, satellite receivers, digital transmitters, and telecommunication eguipment.

equip.cite: Art. VIII definitions, 'Yard, side corner' [PDF p. 479]
equip.text: Yard, side corner means a required yard or setback extending along the street side of a lot between the required front and rear yards or setbacks and, for the purposes of this Code, all yards adjacent to streets shall be considered front yards, except Block 1, lot 19; Block A 2, lot 1, Bel Lido Subdivision.

equip.cite: Art. VIII definitions, 'Yard, front' [PDF p. 479]
equip.text: Yard, front means the required yard or setback located closest to a public or private street, and extending across the entire front of the lot. Lots extending through blocks in such a way as to have frontage on two public streets shall provide front yards adjacent to each street.

equip.cite: § 62-251(14) Impervious pads and sheds [PDF p.391]
equip.text: The minimum required setback for impervious surfaces, such as concrete pads, and sheds is five feet from adjacent property lines. In addition, they cannot cause the property to exceed the maximum lot coverage or fall below minimum pervious area of the applicable zoning district. Permit applications for impervious pads and sheds must include a current property survey showing the exact location and dimensions of the pad(s) or shed, distance to all property lines, and the lot coverage before and after the impervious pad(s) or shed is added. A permit from the city is required for the installation of impervious pads and sheds. The permit shall be reviewed and approved by the city engineer, city planner and building official. Installation of the pad(s) and/or shed shall be reviewed and approved by the building official.

equip.cite: § 62-251(10) Cornices, eaves, etc. [PDF p.390]
equip.text: Cornices, steps, eaves and signs shall not be closer than three feet to a side or rear lot line. Steps, stoops or terraces not exceeding 24 square feet in area, eaves, cornices, awnings and other projections shall not project more than six feet into a front yard or within the front setback space of a structure, provided it does not extend into or over the official right-of-way specified in section 62-341. No part of any structure shall extend over or into a right-of-way.

equip.cite: § 62-251(4) Chimneys, poles, etc. [PDF p.390]
equip.text: Chimneys, elevators, poles, spires, tanks, towers or other projections not used for human occupancy may extend above the height limits where designed to withstand a minimum of 100 mile-per-hour winds and shall be located a distance from other buildings equal at least to their height.

equip.cite: § 62-251(7) Side and rear setbacks [PDF p.390]
equip.text: The side or rear setback or building line of any building or structure (except fences approved herein) on a corner lot shall be the same as the front building line setback within 200 feet for that side or rear street, except as otherwise provided in article III of this chapter.

equip.cite: § 62-251(6) Right-of-way widths [PDF p.390]
equip.text: Where the right-of-way abutting a lot is not dedicated to public use to the width specified in section 62-341, all setback distances shall be measured from the officially planned right-of-way widths listed in said section 62-341.

Fences not higher than five feet above the grade of the nearest right-of-way may be erected. No fence of any material, including shrubbery, shall be higher than five feet between the right-of-way and the building line or higher than eight feet at any other point.

equip.cite: § 62-251(12) Patio floor and roof structures [PDF p.391]
equip.text: The floor (base) and roof of backyard patios on detached single-family home lots and duplex lots shall be setback a minimum of five feet from the rear property line and have the same side setbacks as the single-family home or duplex. For townhouse lots, the minimum setback is three feet from the side and rear property lines. A permit from the city is required for all patio roof and floor installations.

equip.cite: § 62-251(15) Swimming pools [PDF p.391]
equip.text: Swimming pool decks must be setback a minimum of five feet from rear and side property lines. A permit from the city is required for swimming pool installation. The permit shall be reviewed and approved city planner and building official. Installation of the pool shall be approved by the building official.

equip.cite: § 62-251(5) Open space [PDF p.390]
equip.text: No open space or lot area required for a structure or use shall, during the existence of that structure or use, be occupied by or counted as open space or a part of the requirement for another structure or use.

equip.cite: § 62-271(1) Accessory use [PDF p.392]
equip.text: Accessory use in an R residential zone shall include: Structures and uses (such as private garages) solely for the use of residents of the premises which are customarily incidental to and on the same lot with a permitted use, except where otherwise limited or prohibited by this ordinance, the laws of the state or of the United States. No commercial use shall be considered an accessory use in any R residential zone.

equip.cite: § 62-272 Bungalow court [PDF p.392]
equip.text: No structures or vehicles shall be placed within 15 feet of a side or rear property line in a bungalow or motor court.

The area of the premises used for any purpose is termed a lot. Lot widths shall be measured at the front building line. Unless otherwise approved by the planning and zoning board in writing, the narrowest width of the lot shall be considered the front. Lots shall have at least the minimum areas specified in article III of this chapter. All lot lines shall be marked with stakes set by a registered surveyor at the time construction is started.

equip.cite: § 30-36(a) Maximum sound level in use districts, Table I [PDF pp.185-186]
equip.text: It shall be unlawful, within the use districts as indicated in Table I in this subsection, for a sound or noise source to exceed the maximum levels as set forth in Table I, as measured at any point on or beyond the boundary of the property from which the sound or noise is emanating. Residential and Multifamily: 10:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m. 55 dBA; 7:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. 60 dBA. Commercial, Institutional, Community Facilities, Government, Recreational and Public Facilities: 10:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m. 60 dBA; 7:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. 65 dBA. Light Industrial: 10:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m. 65 dBA; 7:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. 70 dBA. Heavy Industrial: Any time 75 dBA.

equip.cite: § 30-36(c) Correction for intermittency [PDF p.186]
equip.text: If the character of the sound is not steady, an exception to the provisions of this section may be made as follows: Source operates continuously one minute or less in any hour +15 dB(A); five minutes or less in any hour +10; 15 minutes or less in any hour +5; source of repetitive impulse character -5; source has pure tone or is of cyclically varying amplitude -5. Apply one correction only.

equip.cite: § 30-35(7) Muffler required [PDF p.185]
equip.text: No internal combustion engines may be operated without a muffler.

equip.cite: § 34-19(f) Utility equipment (flood provisions) [PDF p.223]
equip.text: Utility equipment. Utility equipment that serves manufactured homes, including electric, heating, ventilation, plumbing, and air conditioning equipment and other service facilities, shall comply with the requirements of the Florida Building Code, Residential Section R322.

Minimum pervious open space, 50 percent. Minimum floor area: efficiency 500, one bedroom 700, two bedrooms or more 900 sq ft. Single-family dwellings in this district are subject to the RS-4 site development standards.

RT, residential mobile home/recreation v.note: Standards are stated per site, not per lot: 'Minimum site area, ten acres' (no square-foot figure printed); 'Minimum site width, 300 feet.' Maximum density, ten dwelling units per net acre. Maximum building height, two stories or 25 feet. All mobile home and recreation vehicle park site plans shall be approved by the city commission after public hearing, pursuant to § 62-69.

RM-20, residential multifamily district.note: Maximum density, 20 dwelling units per net acre. Between Structures: 30 feet. Maximum building height, four stories or 47 feet. Minimum pervious open space, 40 percent. Minimum floor area: efficiency 500, one bedroom 650, two bedrooms or more 850 sq ft.

C-1, neighborhood commercial district.note: Setback table also prints 'Adjacent residential district 25' feet. Maximum building height, two stories or 30 feet. Minimum pervious open space, 20 percent.

C-2, general commercial district.note: Setback table also prints, under 'Adjacent': More restrictive district 25 feet; U.S. Highway No. 1 50 feet; State Road No. 27 (Krome Avenue) 25 feet. Maximum building height, five stories or 50 feet.

C-3, intensive commercial district.note: Setback table also prints 'Adjacent residential 25' feet. Maximum building height, two stories or 30 feet. Minimum pervious open space, 20 percent.

C-4, commercial recreational district.note: The code prints a single combined standard in words: 'Minimum building setback: Thirty feet from any lot line.' No separate front/side/rear figures and no corner-side figure are printed; 'Minimum lot area: Five acres' (no square-foot figure printed).

I, light industrial district.note: Setback table also prints 'Adjacent residential district 100' feet. Maximum building height, two stories or 30 feet. Minimum pervious open space, 15 percent. Maximum building lot coverage, 50 percent.

CF, community facility district.note: Setback table also prints 'Adjacent residential district 25' feet. Maximum building height, two stories or 30 feet. Minimum pervious open space, 25 percent.

Planned unit development (PUD).note: No setback, height or coverage figures of its own are printed. 'The minimum size of a site to be developed as a planned development shall be five acres.' Maximum permitted density is 'established for each development at the time of approval of the development plan by the city commission.' Standards are borrowed by product type: detached single-family areas must conform to RS-4.

Planned commercial development (PCD).frontNote: Minimum setbacks: Same as provided in C-2 general commercial district, except that a minimum of 10 feet is required on all sides.
Planned commercial development (PCD).sideNote: Minimum setbacks: Same as provided in C-2 general commercial district, except that a minimum of 10 feet is required on all sides.
Planned commercial development (PCD).rearNote: Minimum setbacks: Same as provided in C-2 general commercial district, except that a minimum of 10 feet is required on all sides.
Planned commercial development (PCD).heightNote: Maximum building height: Up to 100 percent of the average zoned public right-of-way width across the subject property frontage.
Planned commercial development (PCD).note: PCD means an area of land consisting of a minimum of five contiguous acres. 'All other applicable site development standards are contained in the provisions of C-2, general commercial district.' Landscaping: minimum 30 trees per gross acre; at least 60 hedge and shrub plants per gross acre; minimum 75 percent native South Florida species.

Transit-oriented development (TOD) distr.frontNote: Front: 15 feet on a public street; zero feet elsewhere.
Transit-oriented development (TOD) distr.note: Overlay-style district applied by rezoning; parcels must be within 1,000 feet of an existing or planned South Miami-Dade Busway station or stop in Florida City. Maximum height: 'Fourteen stories or 160 feet, whichever is lower.' Maximum floor area ratio for commercial and civic development is 1.0. Minimum density is ten units per net acre.

Qualifying development (Live Local Act).note: Not a mapped district: standards that apply to a 'qualifying development' as defined in the State Live Local Act (2023) on commercially and industrially zoned parcels. Maximum density: 20 units/acre. Between structures: 30 feet. Maximum building height: four stories or 47 feet. Minimum pervious open space: 40 percent. Minimum floor area: efficiency 500, one-bedroom 650, two-bedroom or higher 850 sq ft.

yankeetown.name: Town of Yankeetown
yankeetown.source: Ch. 18 Land Development Code, Art. X District Regulations, §§ 18-178—18-193 (Code 2015, ch. 21, §§ 21.8.1—21.8.16); supplementary regulations Art. XVI §§ 18-354

equip.cite: § 18-178(s)-(v) Common standards for all districts [PDF pp. 239-240]
equip.text: (s) All principal or accessory uses not specifically allowed in a zoning district are hereby prohibited. (t) The principal structure must have a certificate of occupancy before approval of an allowable accessory structure: (1) With the exception of a dock; (2) With the exception of a storage shed, if an active principal structure construction permit exists.... (v) All accessory structures and uses, with the exception of a dock, shall be located behind the front plane of the structure or dwelling unit (i.e., to the side or rear of the structure), except on islands in the residential environmentally sensitive and resource protection district.

equip.cite: § 18-178(x) Common standards for all districts [PDF p. 240]
equip.text: The noise level of electronic speakers, musical instruments, fixed equipment, machinery, power tools, construction demolition and general construction noise should not be offensive to nearby residents between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m.

equip.cite: § 18-179(d) Additional standards for all CN, CWD, and LI districts [PDF p. 240]
equip.text: The noise level of electronic speakers, musical instruments, fixed equipment, machinery, power tools, construction demolition and general construction noise should not be offensive to nearby residents between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m.

equip.cite: § 18-183(e)(2)-(4) Allowed accessory uses and structures, RHD-1 (identical text at § 18-184(e), § 18-187(e), § 18-190(e)) [PDF pp. 256, 258, 263-264, 268]
equip.text: (2) Accessory structures may be placed in front of the primary residence structure if greater than 100 feet separate the front of the accessory from the front parcel line. (3) Accessory structures may not intrude upon any setback. (4) Accessory structures must be architecturally consistent with the primary residential structure.

equip.cite: § 18-2 Definitions, 'Accessory structure' and 'Accessory use' [PDF p. 196]
equip.text: Accessory structure means a subordinate structure, the use of which is incidental to that of the principal structure on the same parcel. Accessory use means an activity, function, or purpose existing on a parcel as accessory or incidental to the principal use. Accessory uses shall not include guest units or any other potentially habitable structure.

equip.cite: § 18-2 Definitions, 'Structure' [PDF p. 214]
equip.text: Structure means anything constructed, installed or portable, the use of which requires a location on a parcel of land. The term 'structure' includes a movable or anchored building or shed usable for housing, business, commercial, agricultural, storage or office purposes, either temporarily or permanently. The term 'structure' also includes roads, walkways,...

equip.cite: § 18-2 Definitions, 'Setback or setback line' [PDF p. 212]
equip.text: Setback or setback line means a line determined by measurement perpendicular to and parallel with a parcel line. No structures or part of a structure may be erected within any setback distance.

equip.cite: § 18-2 Definitions, 'Height' [PDF p. 205]
equip.text: Height means the vertical distance between the average existing grade and the highest point of the roof of any structure or proposed structure, including mechanical equipment, but excluding chimneys, spires, steeples, and on structures utilized for public uses only, radio or television antennae, flagpoles, solar apparatus, and utility poles. The exclusions listed above shall not permit habitable space or space for other uses to exceed the applicable height limitations.

equip.cite: § 18-2 Definitions, 'Front yard' [PDF p. 204]
equip.text: Front yard means the area between the front parcel line and the front plane of the use structure, extending to the side parcel lines.

equip.cite: § 18-2 Definitions, 'Rear yard' [PDF p. 211]
equip.text: Rear yard means the area between the rear parcel line and the rear of the structure, extending to the side parcel lines.

equip.cite: § 18-2 Definitions, 'Impervious surface' [PDF p. 205]
equip.text: Impervious surface means the square footage of parcel area covered by surfaces that do not allow infiltration of fluids including areas beneath eaves, decks, balconies, buildings, blacktop, or concrete paved areas, and any surface containing road base.

equip.cite: § 18-178(g) Common standards for all districts [PDF p. 238]
equip.text: Contiguous parcels of record, under identical ownership, are not subject to the common boundary setback requirements, as those provisions relate to the common boundaries of said parcels.

equip.cite: § 18-356(d) Architectural standards — accessory structures [PDF p. 293]
equip.text: Accessory structures. The design requirements listed in subsection (b) of this section shall be applicable to all accessory structures, unless they are screened so as not to be visible from the public rights-of-way, waterways, or pedestrian walkways. [Applies to new buildings and structures in all commercial zoning districts, except light industrial.]

equip.cite: § 18-354(e)(2) Fences — height in residential districts [PDF p. 281]
equip.text: In residential districts fences and walls may be located in any front yard, side yard, and/or rear yard, including setback areas subject to the following height limitations: a. No fence or wall shall exceed four feet in height when located in the front yard. For corner lots, all street facing lot sides shall be subject to the four-foot height requirement. b. No fence or wall shall exceed six feet in height when located in the side and rear yard.

equip.cite: § 18-354(f)(1) Fences — town right-of-way [PDF p. 281]
equip.text: It shall be unlawful for any person to place a fence, wall, gate, or hedge in, on, or over, any town right-of-way, utility, or drainage easement.

equip.cite: § 18-182(d)(2) and (e)(1) Light industrial — setback increases [PDF pp. 253-254]
equip.text: (d)(2) Storage of on-site volatile substances. Setback will need to increase to a minimum of the fire code requirements.... (e)(1) Uses requiring primarily outdoor storage or where the industrial activity itself is conducted outdoors. a. Setback may need to be increased for safety reasons. b. Additional space between buildings may be required.

equip.cite: § 18-182(f)(6)-(7) Light industrial — prohibited [PDF p. 254]
equip.text: (6) More than one bulk 400-gallon or greater capacity LP gas storage tank. (7) Distribution of LP gas.

equip.cite: § 18-186(b)(7) Resource protection — protection zone (identical text at § 18-190(b)(17)) [PDF pp. 261, 267]
equip.text: The use of herbicides, pesticides or chemical fertilizers, the parking or storage of vehicles or fuels, the housing of domestic animals and the introduction of nonnative species of vegetation in the protection zone is prohibited. [Protection zone = a buffer of native and/or Florida-friendly vegetation of 50 feet maintained from the MHWL (or MHWL or OHWL in RES).]

equip.cite: § 12-419 Floodplain management — other development, general requirements [PDF p. 161]
equip.text: All development, including manmade changes, to improved or unimproved real estate for which specific provisions are not specified in this article or the state building code, shall: (1) Be located and constructed to minimize flood damage; (2) Meet the limitations of section 12-313 if located in a regulated floodway; (3) Be anchored to prevent flotation, collapse or lateral movement resulting from hydrostatic loads, including the effects of buoyancy, during conditions of the design flood; (4) Be constructed of flood damage resistant materials; and (5) Have mechanical, plumbing, and electrical systems above the design flood elevation or meet the requirements of ASCE 24, except that minimum electric service required to address life safety and electric code requirements is permitted below the design flood elevation provided it conforms to the provisions of the electrical part of building code for wet locations.

equip.cite: § 12-342 Floodplain management — utility equipment [PDF p. 159]
equip.text: Utility equipment that serves manufactured homes, including electric, heating, ventilation, plumbing, and air conditioning equipment and other service facilities, shall comply with the requirements of the state building code, Residential Section R322, as applicable to the flood hazard area.

equip.cite: §§ 12-392—12-395 Floodplain management — tanks [PDF p. 160]
equip.text: § 12-392 Underground tanks in flood hazard areas shall be anchored to prevent flotation, collapse or lateral movement resulting from hydrodynamic and hydrostatic loads during conditions of the design flood, including the effects of buoyancy assuming the tank is empty. § 12-393 Above-ground tanks that do not meet the elevation requirements of section 12-394 shall: (1) be permitted in flood hazard areas (zone A) other than coastal high hazard areas, provided the tanks are anchored or otherwise designed and constructed to prevent flotation, collapse or lateral movement resulting from hydrodynamic and hydrostatic loads during conditions of the design flood, including the effects of buoyancy assuming the tank is empty and the effects of flood-borne debris. (2) not be permitted in coastal high hazard areas (zone V). § 12-394 Above-ground tanks in flood hazard areas shall be attached to and elevated to or above the design flood elevation on a supporting structure that is designed to prevent flotation, collapse or lateral movement during conditions of the design flood. Tank-supporting structures shall meet the foundation requirements of the applicable flood hazard area.

CN.note: Commercial neighborhood. Setbacks: 'Waterfront or wetland setback: 50 feet from the MHWL, excluding manmade slips, may be reduced to 25 with BOA approval in special circumstances. Side: eight feet. Front: 25 feet. Rear: ten feet.' Maximum impervious surface ratios shall not exceed 50 percent of the site; minimum green space requirement shall be 50 percent.

CWD.note: Commercial water dependent. Setbacks: 'Waterfront or wetland setback: 50 feet from the MHWL or OHWL, excluding manmade slips, may be reduced to 25 with BOA approval in special circumstances. Side: eight feet. Front: 25 feet. Rear: ten feet.' Maximum impervious surface ratios shall not exceed 50 percent of the site; minimum open space shall be requirement 50 percent.

LI.note: Light industrial. Setbacks: 'Waterfront or wetland setback: 50 feet from the MHWL or OWHL, excluding manmade slips, may be reduced to 25 with BOA approval in special circumstances. Side: eight feet. Front: 25 feet. Rear: ten feet.' Maximum impervious surface coverage shall not exceed 50 percent of the site; minimum green space (including pervious, permeable surfaces) shall cover at least 50 percent of the site.

RHD-1.sideNote: Side: eight feet. In lots platted prior to June 10, 1991, the minimum side yard shall be ten percent of the total width, to a maximum of eight feet.

RHD-2.sideNote: Side: eight feet. In lots platted prior to June 10, 1991, the minimum side yard shall be 10 percent of the total width, to a maximum of 8 feet.
RHD-2.note: Residential highest density 2. Setbacks: 'Waterfront or wetland setback: 50 feet from the OHWL, excluding manmade slips, may be reduced to 25 with BOA approval in special circumstances.' Septic/WWTF setback from MHWL/OHWL/wetland demarcation line per DOH and OFW requirements. No building shall exceed 35 feet in height from the average existing natural grade. Maximum impervious surface ratio of 50 percent.

A.note: Agriculture. Setbacks: 'Waterfront or wetland setback: 50 feet from the OHWL may be reduced to 25 with BOA approval in special circumstances. Side: eight feet. Front: 25 feet. Rear: ten feet. Nutrient sources other than septic (i.e., fertilized and landscaped areas, livestock sources) of 150 feet from property line.' Septic/WWTF setback from MHWL/OHWL/wetland line per DOH and OFW requirements.

RP.note: Resource protection. Setbacks (§ 18-186(h)): 'Waterfront or wetland setback: 50 feet from the MHWL or OHWL may be reduced to 25 with BOA approval in special circumstances. Side: eight feet. Front: 25 feet. Rear: ten feet. 150 feet to MHWL or OHWL for nutrient sources other than septic.

RLD.note: Residential low density. Setbacks: 'Waterfront or wetland setback: 50 feet from the OHWL, excluding manmade slips, may be reduced to 25 with BOA approval in special circumstances. Side: eight feet. Front: 25 feet. Rear: ten feet.' Septic/WWTF setback from MHWL/OHWL/wetland line per DOH and OFW requirements. No building shall exceed 35 feet in height from the average existing natural grade.

RES.heightNote: No building shall exceed 35 feet in height from the average existing natural grade. Where base flood elevation is 18 feet or more, a building located on an island may exceed the height limit of 35 feet, but may not exceed a height limit of 25 feet above base flood elevation.
RES.note: Residential environmentally sensitive. Setbacks: 'Waterfront or wetland setback: 50 feet from the MHWL or OHWL, excluding manmade slips, may be reduced to 25 with BOA approval in special circumstances. Side: eight feet. Front: 25 feet. Rear: ten feet.

PU.note: Public use. Setbacks: 'Waterfront or wetland setback: 50 feet from the MHWL, excluding manmade slips, may be reduced to 25 feet with BOA approval in special circumstances and shall be consistent with the duly adopted comprehensive plan, including policy 1.1.1.2.7 and policy 1.1.1.2.8. Side: eight feet. Front: 25 feet. Rear: ten feet.

MU.frontNote: Dimensional restrictions as called for in CN and RHD-1 districts. The most restrictive shall apply if a structure has both commercial and residential uses. Setbacks shall apply as in CN and RHD-1 district. The most restrictive setback shall apply if a structure has both commercial and residential uses.
MU.sideNote: Setbacks shall apply as in CN and RHD-1 district. The most restrictive setback shall apply if a structure has both commercial and residential uses.
MU.rearNote: Setbacks shall apply as in CN and RHD-1 district. The most restrictive setback shall apply if a structure has both commercial and residential uses.
MU.note: Mixed use. The section prints no dimensional numbers of its own; it incorporates the CN and RHD-1 standards by reference. Permitted uses: all uses allowed in the CN district; residential uses allowed in RHD-1, limited to two dwelling units per acre.

PUD.note: Planned unit development; PUD. The code prints only: 'Sec. 18-192. Planned unit development; PUD. (Reserved title only.)' No dimensional standards, uses or setbacks are printed for this district.

DRRA (overlay).note: Development rights receiving area (DRRA) overlay district. Overlay; no setbacks, height, coverage or lot dimensions are printed.

Well field overlay district.note: Overlay; no setbacks, height, coverage or lot dimensions are printed.

southwest_ranches.name: Town of Southwest Ranches
southwest_ranches.source: Unified Land Development Code (ULDC), Subpart 2 'District Regulations (Use, Yard, Bulk and Height)' — Art. 45 Agricultural and Rural Districts (§§ 045-010, 045-

gen.cite: ULDC § 015-100(A)(11), Yard encroachments [PDF p.583]
gen.text: Air conditioning condenser units, permanent generators, pool equipment, other customary mechanical equipment, and their associated slabs, may encroach not more than five (5) feet into a required side and/or rear yard, but shall not encroach into a required front yard.

gen.cite: ULDC § 040-080(G), Telecommunication towers and antennas [PDF p.633]
gen.text: Portable emergency generators may be temporarily located at a telecommunications facility in the event of a power outage but must be removed upon resumption of power. Nothing in this section shall preclude the placement of a permanent generator onsite; provided that the generator meets the criteria set forth in the town Code and is in compliance with the building code. Portable emergency generators and permanent generators are required to obtain a permit from the town prior to installation.

gen.cite: ULDC § 051-030(D)(1), US Highway 27 district — fuel storage as an accessory use [PDF p.696]
gen.text: On plots of three and one-half (3.5) acres or more in area, one (1) fuel storage tank up to one thousand one hundred (1,100) gallons capacity is permitted for servicing vehicles or equipment used in the regular course of business and for backup generators.

gen.cite: ULDC § 051-050(C)(2)(d), US 27 master plan Tier II information [PDF p.700]
gen.text: Location of areas for outdoor storage, refrigeration equipment, generators, and fuel tanks larger than 200 gallons both above and below ground.

gen.cite: Code of Ordinances § 9-5(9), Noise — Exemptions [PDF p.259]
gen.text: The provisions of section 9-3 shall not apply at any time to:... (9) Any noise generated by the operation or testing of engines, landscaping equipment, generators, pumps, mechanical equipment, construction tools, emergency equipment or similar noises that are common to residential properties.

equip.cite: ULDC § 015-100(A), introductory [PDF p.583]
equip.text: The following structures may encroach into required yards, as provided:.
Irrigation water pumps, wells, water meters, electrical meters and similar above-ground telephone and cable utility company equipment typically found on single-family residential plots.
Roof projections and eaves may encroach not more than two and one-half (2½) feet into any required yard.

The following structures are specifically not permitted to encroach into required yards: (1) Slabs, decks, and any pavered area other than a walkway of six (6) feet or less in width. (2) Anything not specifically permitted under subsection (A) of this section.

equip.cite: ULDC § 045-100, introductory [PDF p.673]
equip.text: All plots in agricultural and rural districts shall maintain yards for all buildings, structures and accessory uses not less than the following, except as provided in section 015-100, "Yard encroachments". This section does not apply to nonresidential farm buildings.

equip.cite: ULDC § 015-020, Reduction of required areas prohibited [PDF p.580]
equip.text: No plot area, yard, setback, clearance, separation, parking area, landscape area or other space shall be reduced in area or dimension so as to make said area or dimension less than the minimum required by this ULDC; and if already less than the minimum required by this ULDC for a new structure or use, said area or dimension shall not be further reduced, without first obtaining a variance pursuant to article 140, "Variances," that would specifically allow such reduction.

equip.cite: ULDC § 015-030, Exclusions from height limits [PDF p.580]
equip.text: This section applies to both roofed structures and structures detached from a building, as applicable. Scenery lofts, towers, cupolas, steeples and domes, not exceeding in gross area, at maximum horizontal section, thirty (30) percent of the roof area, and flagpoles, airplane beacons, broadcasting towers and antennas, other than those regulated by article 40, "Telecommunication Towers and Antennas," chimneys, stacks, tanks, and roof structures used only for ornamental or mechanical purposes, may exceed the permissible height limit in any district by not more than twenty-five (25) percent. Parapet walls may extend not more than five (5) feet above the allowable height of a building.

equip.cite: ULDC § 010-030, definition of "Yard" [PDF p.578]
equip.text: The term "yard" means a space on the same plot with a structure or use, open and unobstructed from the ground to the sky, except by encroachments specifically permitted in section 015-100, "Yard encroachments." Yard measurements shall be the minimum horizontal distances. Yards shall extend and be measured inward from the respective plot lines except for yards abutting streets, in which case they shall be measured from ultimate street lines...

equip.cite: ULDC § 075-100(C), Screening of equipment [PDF p.777]
equip.text: Dumpsters, mechanical equipment and electrical transformers shall be screened on at least three (3) sides by landscape material that is a minimum of thirty (30) inches in height. Such screening shall not interfere with normal operation of equipment.

equip.cite: ULDC § 075-110(D)(2), Single-family requirements [PDF p.779]
equip.text: Where possible as determined by the town administrator, a minimum of two (2) trees shall be required in the front of the plot. Shrubs shall be incorporated in a manner on the site so as to be a visual screen for mechanical equipment or other accessories to the residence.

Above ground tanks shall be protected on all sides from vehicular impact and potential windstorm-driven debris damage to ensure the continued integrity of the tank, as shall be demonstrated on the site plan to the satisfaction of the town council. The tank and enclosure shall be screened with a hedge on all sides visible from public rights-of-way and adjoining zoning districts.

equip.cite: ULDC § 015-070(A), Dumpster enclosures [PDF p.581]
equip.text: All dumpsters shall be kept within opaque enclosures. No dumpster or dumpster enclosure shall be located within a required landscape buffer, and may be located within a required yard only if a street or dedicated alley separates the plot from any adjacent residential plot.

equip.cite: ULDC § 065-020(B)(1), OSR dumpsters [PDF p.718]
equip.text: Dumpsters located in any OSR district shall only be located on plots where an accessory building is located. Such dumpsters shall be kept within opaque or translucent enclosures and shall not be located within any required yard or buffer.

equip.cite: ULDC § 015-090, Prohibited accessory structures [PDF p.582]
equip.text: (A) Portable storage units shall not be permitted as accessory buildings or structures on plots within all zoning districts except the M, manufacturing and industrial district... (B) Truck bodies shall be prohibited in all zoning districts as accessory structures provided that properties owned or used by the town are exempt from this prohibition.

A-1 Agricultural Estate.note: § 045-100: front yard at least fifty (50) feet; 'On all remaining sides of any plot or portion thereof, there shall be a yard of at least twenty-five (25) feet.' Minimum separation for all dwellings, buildings and roofed structures is ten (10) feet. Yard requirements apply to 'all buildings, structures and accessory uses... except as provided in section 015-100, Yard encroachments'.

A-2 General Agricultural.note: Same standards as A-1: § 045-100 front 50 ft, all other yards 25 ft, minimum separation 10 ft between dwellings/buildings/roofed structures; 50-ft yard for animal shelter structures. § 045-070(A): at least one plot dimension of 250 feet; residential development requires two (2) net or two and one-half (2½) gross acres, subject to exceptions.

RE Rural Estate.note: § 045-070(C)(1): 'Every plot in an RE district shall be not less than one hundred twenty-five (125) feet in width and contain not less than one (1) net acre.' One-family dwellings may be permitted on smaller plots meeting listed exceptions (e.g., 35,000 sq ft net area and 125 ft width for plots of public record prior to Sept. 18, 1979; a plot recorded before Jan. 1, 1973 reduced by right-of-way dedication need be no smaller than 125 ft wide and 30,000 sq ft net).

RR Rural Ranches.note: § 045-070(B): 'Every plot in a RR district shall be not less than one-hundred twenty-five (125) feet in width and shall contain not less than two (2) net or two and one-half (2½) gross acres' unless a listed exception applies or the plot has a minimum area of eighty thousand (80,000) square feet in net area, of record as of February 8, 1993.

RR-A Rural Ranches-A.note: § 045-070(D): 'Every plot in a RR-A district shall be not less than one hundred twenty-five (125) feet in width and shall contain not less than two and one-half (2.5) net acres in area.' § 045-080: plot coverage eight (8) percent of plot area, plus the 2.5 percent roof-eave bonus; pervious 40 percent under 2 net acres, 60 percent at 2 net acres and above. District added by Ord. No. 2022-013.

CB Community Business District.sideNote: Side yard, interior: Determined by required landscape buffer width.
CB Community Business District.rearNote: Rear yard: Determined by required landscape buffer width.
CB Community Business District.heightNote: (A) No building or structure located less than one hundred (100) feet from any residential plot shall be constructed to a height exceeding twenty (20) feet. (B) A maximum height of thirty-five (35) feet is permitted with a minimum setback of one hundred (100) feet from an agricultural or rural district.
CB Community Business District.note: § 050-030(G): '(1) Front yard: Thirty-five (35) feet. (2) Side yard, interior: Determined by required landscape buffer width. (3) Side yard, corner: Thirty-five (35) feet. (4) Rear yard: Determined by required landscape buffer width.

MUS Rural Government Mixed Use Services.sideNote: Side yard, interior: Determined by required landscape buffer width.
MUS Rural Government Mixed Use Services.rearNote: Rear yard: Determined by required landscape buffer width.
MUS Rural Government Mixed Use Services.heightNote: (A) No building or structure located less than one hundred (100) feet from any residential plot shall be constructed to a height exceeding twenty (20) feet. (B) A maximum height of thirty-five (35) feet is permitted with a minimum setback of one hundred (100) feet from an agricultural or rural district.
MUS Rural Government Mixed Use Services.note: Shares the Art. 50 commercial-district standards with CB. § 050-030(G)(5): any yard abutting an agricultural or rural district shall have a minimum dimension of one hundred (100) feet within the MUS district, dedicated as public open space with a landscape buffer. § 050-050(B): minimum plot size five (5) acres in the MUS district. § 050-060: plot coverage 35 percent of net acreage, FAR 0.25, pervious 30 percent.

US Highway 27 Planned Business District.frontNote: Setbacks. Setbacks for each parcel shall be established by the master development plan.
US Highway 27 Planned Business District.sideNote: Setbacks. Setbacks for each parcel shall be established by the master development plan.
US Highway 27 Planned Business District.rearNote: Setbacks. Setbacks for each parcel shall be established by the master development plan.
US Highway 27 Planned Business District.note: Planned development district (Art. 51, Ord. No. 2021-007); rezoning requires a master development plan made part of the rezoning ordinance.

M, Manufacturing and Industrial District.frontNote: No minimum yard is required for the construction or erection of any building or structure except where a landscape buffer is required by article 75, "Landscaping Requirements."
M, Manufacturing and Industrial District.sideNote: No minimum yard is required for the construction or erection of any building or structure except where a landscape buffer is required by article 75, "Landscaping Requirements."
M, Manufacturing and Industrial District.rearNote: No minimum yard is required for the construction or erection of any building or structure except where a landscape buffer is required by article 75, "Landscaping Requirements."
M, Manufacturing and Industrial District.note: § 055-050: minimum plot size five (5) acres unless a larger area is indicated for a particular use under § 055-080. § 055-060: minimum pervious area determined by the stormwater drainage and retention requirements of the applicable drainage district; maximum floor area ratio one half (1/2); maximum plot coverage fifty (50) percent.

CF, Community Facility District.coverageNote: Maximum plot coverage. Properties that have a community facilities land use plan designation and had a zoning designation of I-1 prior to May 9, 2002, shall have a maximum plot coverage of thirty-five (35%) percent. All other properties shall be limited to the plot coverage allowed in the most restrictive of the abutting zoning districts.
CF, Community Facility District.note: § 060-020(G) required yards and plot dimensions: '(1) Fifty (50) feet along any street line; (2) Twenty-five (25) feet from any interior side property line; (3) Fifteen (15) feet from the rear property line; (4) Fifty (50) feet from any residential plot line, except for town uses. equip.text: Mechanical equipment, such as air conditioning units, pumps, heating equipment, solar panels, and similar installations, may not project into the required front yard(s), but may project five feet into the required rear yard(s), and three feet or no more than 50 percent of the required yard, whichever is the most restrictive, into the required side yard(s).

equip.text: Certain architectural features, such as cornices, eaves and gutters, may project no more than three feet into the required front yard, five feet into the required rear yard, and three feet or no more than 50 percent of the required side yard, whichever is the most restrictive.

equip.cite: Sec. 4-8.4(a), Accessory Structures — Generally [PDF p. 626]
equip.text: Accessory structures shall conform to the following regulations, except as may otherwise be provided in this Code. Accessory structures do not include accessory dwellings as regulated by this Code. Accessory structures shall not be utilized for living or sleeping purposes, including guest visits, at any time.

equip.cite: Sec. 4-8.4(b), Accessory Structures — Height [PDF p. 626]
equip.text: Accessory structures shall not exceed 15 feet in height, except 1 where the accessory structure meets the primary structure setback of the district, in which case the maximum height of the accessory structure may be that of the district, or 2 accessory agricultural structures such as barns and silos (See subsection (d) below).

equip.cite: Sec. 4-8.4(c)(1)—(3), Accessory Structures — Location [PDF p. 626]
equip.text: (1) Accessory structures shall not be erected in any required front yard except as outlined in subsections (4), (5) and (6) below. Accessory structures shall be permitted in front yards at twice the depth of the required front yard, or 50 feet, whichever is less. Such structures shall not occupy required side yards. (2) Accessory structures may occupy required side yards provided that such structures are more distant from the street than any part of the principal building on the same lot and any lot abutting said required side yard; provided, however, that such accessory structures are not closer than three feet from any side lot line, including architectural features such as cornices, eaves and gutters. (3) Accessory structures may occupy required rear yards provided that such structures do not occupy more than 20 percent of the required rear yard, excepting swimming pools and swimming pool screened structures, and are not closer than three feet to any rear lot line.

equip.cite: Sec. 4-8.4(c)(4)—(6), Accessory Structures — corner and through lots [PDF p. 626]
equip.text: (4) On any corner lot no part of any accessory structure shall be located in the required front yards except where one front yard functions as a side yard. On these lots, accessory structures shall be permitted to intrude up to ten feet into the required front yard functioning as a side yard. In zoning districts which require side yards greater than ten feet, the permitted intrusion shall be increased up to a distance equal to said required side yard. The intrusion is measured from the required yard line, toward the street. (5) On corner lots which do not have a required rear yard, accessory structures may be located in the functional rear yard (the area behind what is designed to be the rear of the house) provided the accessory structures meets all other requirements. (6) Through lots may have accessory structures located in the front yard that functions as a rear yard provided that any accessory use or structure of a height greater than two feet shall be set back a minimum of ten feet from the front yard which functions as a rear yard.

equip.cite: Sec. 2-3.2, Table 2-3 footnote (9) [PDF p. 510]

equip.text: The following structures or parts thereof are hereby exempt from the height limitations set forth in the zoning districts: a. Chimneys, smokestacks, spires, flagpoles, ventilators, skylights, derricks, conveyors and cooling towers and radio and television antennae. b. Public utility and power transmission towers. c. Other similar and necessary mechanical appurtenances pertaining to and necessary to the permitted uses of the districts in which they are located, provided that they are not used for human occupancy.

equip.cite: LDC § 34-182 Yard, building setback and open space exceptions [LDC PDF pp. 336—337]
equip.text: The following requirements are intended to provide exceptions or qualify and supplement, as the case may be, the specific district regulations set forth in article IV of this chapter. The purpose here is to clarify certain conditions pertaining to the use of lots and access points. (1) Division of a lot. No recorded lot shall be divided into two or more lots unless such division results in the creation of lots each of which conforms to all of the applicable regulations of the district in which the property is located. No reduction in the size of a recorded lot below the minimum requirements of this chapter shall be permitted. (2) Small lots of record. In residential zoning districts, where there are existing recorded lots which do not meet the minimum lot area requirements, single-family dwellings may be constructed when a side yard is provided of not less than five feet and the sum of the side yards shall not be less than 12 feet and providing all other requirements, except lot size, are met. In all other zoning districts, where existing lots of record do not meet the minimum lot area requirement, permitted uses may occur when one-half the required side yard is provided, and providing all other requirements except lot size are met. — NOTE: this is the entire section; it prints NO allowance for mechanical equipment, air conditioners, pool equipment, generators or other appurtenances to project into a required yard.

equip.text: (a) On a corner lot no fence, wall, hedge or planting shall be permitted or allowed to extend in excess of three feet above the curb or established grade level of the street, or other obstruction to the vision of street traffic, on that portion of a front or side yard that is included between the side lines of such intersecting streets and a line connecting such lines at points which are 25 feet distant from their point of intersection measured along such lines. (b) Within the limits of a side yard, no fence or wall, except a retaining wall, shall be more than six feet high, unless the part above such height be not more than one-quarter solid.

equip.text: Accessory equipment buildings used in conjunction with the operation and maintenance of antennas shall be permitted subject to the following requirements: A. Shall be located within close proximity, as is reasonably possible, to the structure upon which the antennas are attached; D. B-1 Business district.sideNote: No side yards are required except for those lots whose side lot lines are on streets. Such lots shall have a ten-foot side yard. When a lot in the B-1 Business district abuts a residential district, there shall be a side yard of not less than 15 feet.
B-1 Business district.rearNote: There shall be a rear yard of not less than ten feet unless abutting an alley.
B-1 Business district.note: § 34-117(e). The 10,000 sq ft / 100 ft figures are the building site area regulations printed 'For single and two-family dwellings'; the district prints no general minimum lot size for commercial uses.

B-2 Business district.note: § 34-118(e). 'When a lot in the B-2 district abuts a residential district there shall be a 15-foot buffer area.' Rear: 'Where a lot in the B-2 district abuts a residential district there shall be one buffer area within the 25-foot setback.' Minimum lot or building site area 10,000 sq ft with a width of 100 ft measured at the front building line.

O-1 Office, medical and related services.note: § 34-119(d). Rear yard: 10 ft, except no rear yard required where the rear lot line is a railroad right-of-way; lots abutting a residential district at least 20 ft plus a fence at least six feet high approved by the city.

L-2 Heavy industrial district.note: § 34-121(e). Minimum lot or building site area printed as 'one acre' (no square-foot figure printed), width not less than 100 ft at the front of the building line. Side yard: 20 ft; lots whose side lot lines are intersecting streets 40 ft; abutting a residential district 40 ft; abutting a railroad right-of-way no side yard required.

'Impacts or uses allowed within the C conservation district must be outlined in a conservation easement or other permanent protection instrument, which shall be required for all land designated within this district.' (Former § 34-125 C-1 Conservation district was repealed by Ord. No. 2024-15, § 3, 9-9-24.)

PUD Planned unit development.frontNote: Lot area and yard requirements shall be determined as part of the development review process and set forth in the master development agreement. Yards abutting the PUD boundary shall not be less than the yard requirements of the zoning district most similar to that portion of the PUD.
PUD Planned unit development.sideNote: Lot area and yard requirements shall be determined as part of the development review process and set forth in the master development agreement. Yards abutting the PUD boundary shall not be less than the yard requirements of the zoning district most similar to that portion of the PUD.
PUD Planned unit development.rearNote: Lot area and yard requirements shall be determined as part of the development review process and set forth in the master development agreement. PUD Planned unit development.heightNote: Maximum building height shall be determined as part of the development review process and set forth in the master development agreement, however, heights of buildings near or along the perimeter of the project area shall be related to and consistent with building heights in adjoining districts.

Mobile home space (Art.
