Minimum site width: '(1) 100 feet at site ingress and egress points. (2) 200 feet at the portion of the site used for mobile home stands.' Minimum site area: '(1) 10 acres.

RMH (mobile home subdivision or individu.note: No maximum building height is printed for the RMH district.

RMH (single-family subdivision).frontNote: Single-family subdivisions shall meet the yard requirements defined in the RG district.
RMH (single-family subdivision).sideNote: Single-family subdivisions shall meet the yard requirements defined in the RG district.
RMH (single-family subdivision).rearNote: Single-family subdivisions shall meet the yard requirements defined in the RG district.
RMH (single-family subdivision).note: Maximum lot coverage by all buildings and structures shall be 35 percent (applies district-wide). No maximum building height is printed for the RMH district.

RPO (other permitted uses).sideNote: Minimum required side yard: 7.5 feet, or 10 percent of the lot width, whichever is greater.
RPO (other permitted uses).note: Residential, professional office. The code prints 'Minimum lot coverage: 35 percent' (so labelled, under 'Minimum lot requirements'); 'Maximum structure height: 35 feet'; 'Site development plan: Approval is required as outlined in section 4-39.'

RPO (single-family dwellings).note: 'Minimum lot requirements … a. Single-family dwellings: As required in the RS-2 district.' No separate figures are printed in the RPO section.

RPO (multiple-family dwellings).note: 'Minimum lot requirements … b. Multiple-family dwellings: As required in the RG district.' No separate figures are printed in the RPO section.

CN.sideNote: Side yard: 15 feet, except, where the commercial neighborhood district abuts a residential district, the minimum side yard shall be increased to 30 feet. No side yard shall be required where 2 or more commercial buildings adjoin side by side.
CN.note: Commercial, neighborhood. 'Lot coverage by all buildings, including accessory buildings and structures, shall be not more than 50 percent of the lot. The minimum landscape area shall not be less than 10 percent of the total lot area.' Churches require a minimum parcel size of not less than 2 acres.

CG.sideNote: Side yard: Five (5) feet, except, where the CG district abuts a residential district, the side yard shall be increased to thirty (30) feet. No side yard shall be required where two (2) or more commercial buildings adjoin side by side.
CG.heightNote: Maximum building height: None, providing that for structures exceeding thirty-five (35) feet or three (3) stories in height the minimum side yard shall be increased by one (1) foot for every two (2) feet of building height exceeding thirty-five (35) feet.
CG.note: Commercial, general. 'Minimum lot requirements. Minimum lot area is ten thousand (10,000) square feet.' — no minimum lot width is printed. No maximum lot coverage is printed; only 'The minimum landscape area shall not be less than ten (10) percent of the total lot area.'

CBD.frontNote: Minimum yard requirements are as follows: None, except as specifically required for certain uses.
CBD.sideNote: Minimum yard requirements are as follows: None, except as specifically required for certain uses.
CBD.rearNote: Minimum yard requirements are as follows: None, except as specifically required for certain uses.
CBD.heightNote: Maximum height of structures is as follows: None, except as specifically provided for certain uses.
CBD.coverageNote: Maximum lot coverage for all buildings is as follows: None, except as specifically required for certain uses.
CBD.minLotNote: Minimum lot requirements are as follows: None, except as specifically required for certain uses, except that where there exists a high-rise residential structure then the minimum lot area shall be seven hundred thirty-five (735) square feet for each family unit (gross density of approximately twenty (20) units per acre).
CBD.note: Commercial, central business district. The district prints no numeric yard, height or coverage standards at all.

IW.heightNote: Maximum building height: None, providing that, for structures exceeding thirty-five (35) feet or three (3) stories in height, the minimum side yard shall be increased by one (1) foot for every two (2) feet of building height exceeding thirty-five (35) feet.
IW.minLotNote: Minimum lot requirements are as follows: None.
IW.note: Industrial, warehouse. 'A minimum of ten (10) percent of the total lot area shall be landscaped.' Junkyards permitted by special exception 'shall be completely screened by a fence or other suitable visual barrier at least six (6) feet in height and shall be located no closer than one hundred fifty (150) feet from a public right-of-way.'

IH.heightNote: Maximum building height is as follows: None, providing that, for structures exceeding 35 feet or 3 stories in height, the minimum side yard shall be increased by 1 foot for every 2 feet of building height exceeding 35 feet.
IH.minLotNote: Minimum lot requirements are as follows: None.
IH.note: Industrial, heavy. 'A minimum of 10 percent of the total lot area shall be landscaped.'

GU.frontNote: Minimum yard requirements shall conform to the CG district.
GU.sideNote: Minimum yard requirements shall conform to the CG district.
GU.rearNote: Minimum yard requirements shall conform to the CG district.
GU.heightNote: Building restrictions shall conform to the CG district.
GU.minLotNote: Minimum lot requirements are as follows: none.
GU.note: Government use. 'Such uses may be located in districts other than GU, provided that such uses conform with all provisions of the district in which they are located.' All development reviewed per chapter 3.

CON.note: Conservation — an OVERLAY district (§ 4-51(c): 'An overlay district is established for conservation areas with the following title and abbreviation: Conservation, CON.'). It prints no dimensional standards: '(b) Regulations. All development shall conform to the provisions, conditions, and requirements of the base district.' Site plan review per chapter 3.

EC.frontNote: Minimum setback requirements from the perimeter of the site are listed below for buildings up to thirty-five (35) feet in height. Buildings that exceed thirty-five (35) feet shall increase all required setbacks listed below by one (1) foot for every three (3) feet in additional building height above thirty-five (35) feet.
EC.note: Enterprise corridor — a corridor district along State Road 228 from the I-10 interchange northwest to Lowder Street; added by Ord. No. 07-29 and not listed among the base districts in § 4-51(b). 'Minimum lot requirements (width and area). Ten thousand (10,000) square feet' — a single figure covering both width and area. No maximum lot coverage is printed.

PUD (planned unit development).heightNote: Where the area proposed for a planned unit development abuts an existing one-family district, no structures over two (2) stories in height shall be permitted within three hundred (300) feet of the abutting one-family district. … Height, density and floor area standards used in the planned unit development shall conform to the requirements of the district.
PUD (planned unit development).minLotNote: A parcel which is proposed for a planned unit development must contain a minimum area of five (5) contiguous acres in single ownership or control to be considered a large-scale development; a small-scale development will consist of less than five (5) acres.
PUD (planned unit development).note: 'An approved planned unit development shall be considered to be a separate zoning district in which the development plan, as approved, establishes the restrictions and regulations according to which development shall occur.' 'The permitted density within any planned unit development shall not exceed the maximum number of dwelling units per acre permitted by housing type in the RG district.' 'The location of all proposed structures shall be as shown on the development plan, subject to minimum lot size, setback lines, and lot coverage or floor area specified in the approved plan.' No front, side or rear yard figures are printed for PUDs.

indian_shores.name: Town of Indian Shores
indian_shores.source: Code of Ordinances, Part II, Subpart B (Land Development Regulations), Ch. 110 Zoning — Art. III District Regulations (§§ 110-121—110-290) and Art. IV Supplemen

equip.cite: § 110-329.1 Mechanical equipment setbacks [PDF p. 697]
equip.text: Mechanical equipment (A/C and etc.) shall not be allowed in the side setbacks. (Ord. No. 03-3, § 6, 6-10-03).

equip.cite: § 110-329 Swimming pool or swimming pool enclosure [PDF p. 697]
equip.text: A swimming pool or swimming pool enclosure, including any mechanical equipment. (Filter, heaters and etc.) and pool accessories (ladders, handrails and etc.) which protrudes above the building grade, shall be a minimum of ten feet from all lot lines. (Code 1979, § 23-22(8); Ord. No. 03-3, § 5, 6-10-03).

equip.cite: § 110-1 Definitions — Structure [PDF p. 667]
equip.text: Structure means anything constructed or erected in or on the ground or attached to anything in or on the ground, including but not limited to buildings, sheds, shelters, gazebos, trellises, walls, poles, signs, seawalls, swimming pools and aboveground exterior mechanical equipment, such as air conditioning compressors, pool filters, fans, pumps and tanks, but not including fences. The term "structure" includes the term "building."

equip.cite: § 110-1 Definitions — Building or structure, lot coverage area [PDF p. 658]
equip.text: Building or structure, lot coverage area, means the total lot coverage, measured in square feet, of the following areas: the area enclosed by the outermost part of the walls of a building or structure, including the area of any inner court or atrium; the area of that part of the roof which projects over or beyond the outermost portion of the walls of a building; the area of any part of any balcony, exterior stairs, and heating and air conditioning units, when such units are not located on top of the building, that is not covered by the roof or any portion of the roof of the building to which the balcony, stairs, and units are attached.

equip.cite: § 110-1 Definitions — Building area [PDF p. 658]
equip.text: ... the area of that portion of roofs, balconies, equipment or attachments (e.g., heating or air conditioning components) which protrude beyond the exterior line of a building's walls. This measurement will be used in determining a building's or structure's floor area ratio...

equip.cite: § 110-330 Distance between buildings [PDF p. 697]
equip.text: The minimum distance between buildings on the same lot, measured from any building protrusion, i.e., balcony, air conditioning unit, etc., shall be as follows: (1) Ten feet of distance between buildings, for the first 20 feet of the height of the sidewall above the minimum required piling height, plus one-half foot increase in side setback for every one foot of increase in sidewall height. (2) The minimum distance between two buildings of different heights shall be determined by applying subsection (1) of this section to the height of the taller building.

equip.cite: § 110-327(7) Setbacks — top-floor roof area [PDF p. 696]
equip.text: The remaining 80 percent roof area of the floor immediately below may not be permanently or temporarily screened or enclosed, in any fashion or manner, nor may it be used as or constructed to be used as a patio, deck, observation deck, platform, stage, floor or other similar use, except for mechanical equipment.

equip.cite: § 110-327(8) Setbacks — accessory structure exemption [PDF p. 696]
equip.text: The rear setback for gulf front lots shall be a minimum of 18 feet. The measurement shall be from the rear property line or from the coastal construction control line, whichever is the most eastward. Accessory structures of 100 square feet of floor area or less are exempt.

equip.cite: § 110-331 Roof overhang [PDF p. 697]
equip.text: The maximum allowable distance a roof overhang may protrude or encroach into any required setback is two feet.

equip.cite: § 110-3 Compliance required [PDF p. 669]
equip.text: (c) No lot, parcel or other land area may be so reduced or diminished that the yards, open areas and setbacks become smaller than prescribed in this chapter. Further no yard, open area or setback provided about any building or structure for the purposes of complying with any applicable section of this Code may be considered as providing any portion of a yard, open area or setback for any other building or structure.

equip.cite: § 110-84 Variances [PDF p. 675]
equip.text: A variance is authorized only for the following numerical provisions of this chapter such as: minimum building area per principal building; minimum building setbacks; swimming pool or swimming pool enclosure setbacks; minimum building height; minimum enclosed floor space; maximum lot coverage; floor area ratio; minimum distance between buildings; minimum required open area; and minimum off-street parking space requirements.

equip.cite: § 18-57 Application for development permit — site plan contents [PDF p. 187]
equip.text: Three copies of a detailed site plan, with architect's certification including: 1. Showing the exact location proposed for all buildings and other structures, including all balconies, overhangs and other projections; 2. All fences, walls, seawalls, swimming pools and associated equipment, electrical equipment, heating or air conditioning equipment located outside the building's or structure's outer wall line, decks, patios, walkways, drives, parking spaces, drainage facilities, all areas to be paved, and any other aboveground structures or equipment.

equip.cite: § 18-51 Permits required [PDF p. 184]
equip.text: (12) Mechanical, including heating and air conditioning (mechanical).

equip.cite: § 110-399 Maximum heights (fences, walls, hedges) [PDF pp. 713, 715]
equip.text: (a)(1) Interior or nonwaterfront lots. The maximum height of any fence, wall or hedge located upon a lot, no side of which borders upon Boca Ciega Bay or the Gulf of Mexico, shall be six feet. (2) Gulf front or bay front lots... a. On or near lot lines which border the coastal construction control line or seawall or water line, the maximum height shall be three feet, except that a four-foot chainlink or any other four-foot open style fence may be erected if the topmost one foot thereof is unobstructed... (3) The maximum height of any fence, wall or hedge which borders Gulf Boulevard shall be four feet except that a reduction to three feet shall be required if the fence, wall or hedge restricts anyone's vision of approaching traffic on Gulf Boulevard.

equip.cite: § 110-368 Noise / § 34-82(8) Loud and raucous noises [PDF p. 278]
equip.text: It shall be unlawful to operate any motor-driven refrigeration unit, generator, compressor, pump or other noise-producing equipment on a parked truck, trailer or similar vehicle within the town between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 8:00 a.m., except in a life threatening emergency and with the approval of the police department. [Vehicle-mounted equipment only — does not govern a permanent generator pad.]

RFM.frontNote: The minimum building setback from any lot line is as follows: (1) From any lot line bordering any portion of Gulf Boulevard: a. Eighteen feet b. Ten foot setback for lots bordering on Gulf Boulevard within the Indian Shores Town Square Plan area. (2) From any lot line bordering any portion of a street other than Gulf Boulevard, ten feet, except lots lines bordering Whispering Pines Drive, 191 Ave., 192 Ave., 193 Ave.
RFM.sideNote: (4) From any lot line not bordering any portion of either a street or the coastal construction control line: Five feet of side setback for the first 20 feet of the height of the sidewall above the minimum required piling height, plus one-half foot increase in side setback for every one foot of increase in sidewall height. (§ 110-327(4)).
RFM.rearNote: (8) The rear setback for gulf front lots shall be a minimum of 18 feet. The measurement shall be from the rear property line or from the coastal construction control line, whichever is the most eastward. Accessory structures of 100 square feet of floor area or less are exempt. (§ 110-327(8)) — no rear setback figure is printed for lots that are not gulf front; such a line falls under § 110-327(4).
RFM.note: Resort Facilities Medium. Boundaries: all real property within the town west of Gulf Boulevard (SR 699) (§ 110-146). Permitted uses are residential/tourist lodging only; business or commercial units and multipurpose buildings are non-permitted (§ 110-149). Maximum density 18.0 residential units per buildable acre; nonresidential maximum FAR.40 (40 percent) (§ 110-147(b)).

ROR.frontNote: The minimum building setback from any lot line is as follows: (1) From any lot line bordering any portion of Gulf Boulevard: a. Eighteen feet b. Ten foot setback for lots bordering on Gulf Boulevard within the Indian Shores Town Square Plan area. (2) From any lot line bordering any portion of a street other than Gulf Boulevard, ten feet, except lots lines bordering Whispering Pines Drive, 191 Ave., 192 Ave., 193 Ave.
ROR.sideNote: (4) From any lot line not bordering any portion of either a street or the coastal construction control line: Five feet of side setback for the first 20 feet of the height of the sidewall above the minimum required piling height, plus one-half foot increase in side setback for every one foot of increase in sidewall height. (§ 110-327(4)).
ROR.rearNote: (8) The rear setback for gulf front lots shall be a minimum of 18 feet. The measurement shall be from the rear property line or from the coastal construction control line, whichever is the most eastward. Accessory structures of 100 square feet of floor area or less are exempt. (§ 110-327(8)).
ROR.note: Residential/Office/Retail. Boundaries: all real property within the town east of Gulf Boulevard (SR 699) (§ 110-171). Maximum density 18.0 residential units per buildable acre; nonresidential maximum FAR.40 (40 percent); residential equivalent use shall not exceed an equivalent of 2.0 to 3.0 beds per permitted dwelling unit at 18 dwelling units per acre, standard 2.5 beds per dwelling unit (§ 110-172(b)).

I.frontNote: See § 110-327(1), (2): eighteen feet from any lot line bordering any portion of Gulf Boulevard (ten feet within the Indian Shores Town Square Plan area); ten feet from any lot line bordering any portion of a street other than Gulf Boulevard.
I.sideNote: (4) From any lot line not bordering any portion of either a street or the coastal construction control line: Five feet of side setback for the first 20 feet of the height of the sidewall above the minimum required piling height, plus one-half foot increase in side setback for every one foot of increase in sidewall height. (§ 110-327(4)).
I.rearNote: (8) The rear setback for gulf front lots shall be a minimum of 18 feet... Accessory structures of 100 square feet of floor area or less are exempt. (§ 110-327(8)).
I.note: Institutional. Boundaries as indicated on the future land use map and addendum (§ 110-201). Impervious surface ratio (ISR) shall not exceed 0.80 (80 percent); maximum density 12.5 residential units per buildable acre; maximum FAR.65 (65 percent) (§ 110-202(b)).

T/U.frontNote: See § 110-327(1), (2): eighteen feet from any lot line bordering any portion of Gulf Boulevard (ten feet within the Indian Shores Town Square Plan area); ten feet from any lot line bordering any portion of a street other than Gulf Boulevard.
T/U.sideNote: (4) From any lot line not bordering any portion of either a street or the coastal construction control line: Five feet of side setback for the first 20 feet of the height of the sidewall above the minimum required piling height, plus one-half foot increase in side setback for every one foot of increase in sidewall height. (§ 110-327(4)).
T/U.rearNote: (8) The rear setback for gulf front lots shall be a minimum of 18 feet... (§ 110-327(8)).
T/U.note: Transportation/Utility. Boundaries as indicated on the future land use map and addendum (§ 110-226). Permitted uses include utility transmission line/electric power substation, telephone switching station, municipal water supply facility, wastewater disposal facility, solid waste/refuse disposal facility, transfer recycling facility (§ 110-227(a)). Impervious surface ratio (ISR) shall not exceed 0.80 (80 percent).

R/OS.frontNote: See § 110-327(1), (2): eighteen feet from any lot line bordering any portion of Gulf Boulevard (ten feet within the Indian Shores Town Square Plan area); ten feet from any lot line bordering any portion of a street other than Gulf Boulevard.
R/OS.sideNote: (4) From any lot line not bordering any portion of either a street or the coastal construction control line: Five feet of side setback for the first 20 feet of the height of the sidewall above the minimum required piling height, plus one-half foot increase in side setback for every one foot of increase in sidewall height. (§ 110-327(4)).
R/OS.rearNote: (8) The rear setback for gulf front lots shall be a minimum of 18 feet... (§ 110-327(8)).
R/OS.note: Recreation/Open Space. Boundaries as indicated on the future land use map and addendum (§ 110-251). Permitted uses: public parks, public recreation facilities, public beach or water access, public or private open space. Impervious surface ratio (ISR) shall not exceed 0.50 (50 percent); maximum density 0.0 residential units per buildable acre; non-residential maximum FAR.20 (20 percent) (§ 110-252(b)).

P.note: Preservation. Boundaries as indicated on the future land use map and addendum (§ 110-276). Areas zoned P are intended for preservation, conservation and protection of vital natural resources.

Town square plan area (overlay).frontNote: (1) From any lot line bordering any portion of Gulf Boulevard:... b. Ten foot setback for lots bordering on Gulf Boulevard within the Indian Shores Town Square Plan area. (2)... lots lines bordering Whispering Pines Drive, 191 Ave., 192 Ave., 193 Ave.
Town square plan area (overlay).sideNote: (4) From any lot line not bordering any portion of either a street or the coastal construction control line: Five feet of side setback for the first 20 feet of the height of the sidewall above the minimum required piling height, plus one-half foot increase in side setback for every one foot of increase in sidewall height. (§ 110-327(4)).
Town square plan area (overlay).note: OVERLAY, not a base district (Art. III, Div. 8, Overlay Districts). § 110-290 defines the town square plan area as 'the area encompassed by 191st Avenue on the south, a mangrove-lined drainage ditch on the east, 193rd Avenue on the north, and Gulf Boulevard on the west.' It overlies RFM/ROR.

north_palm_beach.name: Village of North Palm Beach
north_palm_beach.source: Code of Ordinances, Appendix C—Zoning (Ch. 45): §§ 45-2 (definitions), 45-16, 45-22, 45-23, 45-27 (R-1), 45-28 (R-2), 45-30 (R-3), 45-31 (C-MU, Tables 3-8, 11,

gen.cite: § 45-2, definition of 'Mechanical equipment' [PDF p. 722 / printed p. 2486]
gen.text: Mechanical equipment means necessary or accessory equipment mounted on or adjacent to a principal structure, including but not limited to central air conditioning equipment, ventilation equipment, generators, heating equipment, antennas, satellite dishes, refrigeration equipment, household appliances, solar and conventional hot water heaters, elevator machinery and similar type equipment.

gen.cite: § 45-23, Emergency generators required for automotive service stations [PDF p. 737 / printed p. 2501]
gen.text: All newly constructed automotive service stations shall have a permanently installed emergency generator. Existing automotive service stations shall be required to install permanent emergency generators whenever such service station is rebuilt after being destroyed to an extent of more than fifty (50) percent of its assessed value or whenever a revised site plan for such service station is submitted for approval which enlarges upon or alters in any way the original site plan for that service station. All others shall have a transfer installed within two (2) years of the passage of this section, to allow for a portable generator to be easily connected to the service station. For the purposes of this section, an automotive service station means any commercial establishment engaged in the retail sale of gasoline.

equip.cite: § 45-27.I, R-1 single-family dwelling district — Mechanical equipment [PDF p. 743 / printed p. 2507]
equip.text: I. Mechanical equipment. All non-roof-mounted mechanical equipment shall be located behind the front building face of the principal structure in either the side yard or the rear yard. Such equipment shall be located adjacent to the principal structure whenever practicable, provided, however, that all mechanical equipment shall be located at least five (5) feet from the side property line and at least seven and one-half feet (7½) from the rear property line.

equip.cite: § 45-28.H, R-2 multiple-family dwelling district — Mechanical equipment [PDF p. 746 / printed p. 2510]
equip.text: H. Mechanical equipment. All non-roof mounted mechanical equipment shall be located behind the front building face of the principal structure in either the side yard or the rear yard. Such equipment shall be located adjacent to the principal structure whenever practicable, provided, however, that all mechanical equipment shall be located at least five (5) feet from the side property line and at least seven and one-half feet (7½) from the rear property line.

equip.cite: § 45-27.B, R-1 — height exclusion for mechanical equipment [PDF p. 740 / printed p. 2504]
equip.text: Decorative architectural elements, chimneys, mechanical equipment, non-habitable cupolas, elevator shafts or similar appurtenances shall be excluded from the foregoing height restrictions. Rooftops shall not be used for pools, decks, or other spaces to congregate.

equip.cite: § 45-28.B, R-2 — height exclusion for mechanical equipment [PDF p. 744 / printed p. 2508]
equip.text: Decorative architectural elements, chimneys, mechanical equipment, non-habitable cupolas, elevator shafts or similar appurtenances shall be excluded from the foregoing height restrictions. Rooftops shall not be used for pools, decks, or other spaces to congregate.

equip.cite: § 45-31.G.2.e, C-MU — service or utility equipment along alleys [PDF p. 776 / printed p. 2540]
equip.text: e. Refuse containers and other service or utility equipment must meet the same setbacks as for surface parking. Refuse container areas must be screened in accordance with section 45-88. [Table 15 surface parking lot setbacks: US Highway 1 50' min.; cross street 30' min.; alley 5' min.; New Street 30' min.; side lot lines 0' min.; Local Street 30' min.]

equip.cite: § 45-35.3, Art. 5, Sec. 5-5.D, C-NB — Mechanical equipment screening [PDF p. 828 / printed p. 2592]
equip.text: D. Mechanical equipment screening. All rooftop mechanical equipment shall be located at a distance from the edge of the building and properly screened so as not to be visible from any street or adjoining property. Materials used for screening purposes shall be compatible with the architectural style, color, and materials of the principal building.

equip.cite: § 45-35.3, Art. 8, Sec. 8-1.B, C-NB — Screening of mechanical equipment [PDF p. 846 / printed p. 2610]
equip.text: B. Screening of mechanical equipment. 1. All mechanical equipment shall be screened from public view. 2. Such screening may include any combination of landscaping and non-living opaque materials. 3. If building materials are to be utilized for screening purposes, such materials shall be consistent with the architectural design of the principal structure. 4. Screening shall extend at least one foot above the object to be screened.

equip.cite: § 45-36.B, General provisions — swimming pools and outdoor fireplaces [PDF p. 855 / printed p. 2619]
equip.text: B. Swimming pools shall be set back at least seven and one-half (7½) feet from the back property line measured from the rim of the pool and not less than five (5) feet from the side property line including the two-and-one-half-foot walk around the pool. The highest projection of the swimming pool shall not exceed two (2) feet. Outdoor fireplaces not exceeding six (6) feet in height may be erected and maintained, said structure, however, shall not be erected within five (5) feet of any rear lot line. (a) Swimming pools may be enclosed by screening provided same are not erected closer than five (5) feet from the side and rear yard lines. (b) No swimming pool shall be located in the area lying between the front property line and the front building line in the R-1 and R-2 zoning districts.

equip.cite: § 45-36.C, General provisions — detached garages [PDF p. 855 / printed p. 2619]
equip.text: C. Detached garages not more than one (1) story in height may be erected and maintained at least seven and one-half (7½) feet from the rear property line and ten (10) feet from the side property line of any lot within the R-1 or R-2 residential zoning districts.

equip.cite: § 45-36.H, General provisions — screened patios [PDF p. 856 / printed p. 2620]
equip.text: H. Patios connected to the rear of a dwelling unit may be enclosed by screening provided there shall be a rear yard of not less than fifteen (15) feet measured from the rear of the screened enclosure to the rear lot line.

equip.cite: § 45-36.U.(6)b.-c., General provisions — portable storage containers and roll-off dumpsters [PDF p. 867 / printed p. 2631]
equip.text: b. No portable storage container or roll-off dumpster shall be located within a utility easement, drainage easement, right-of-way, front yard area, alley right-of-way or street right-of-way. Notwithstanding the foregoing, a portable storage container or roll-off dumpster shall be placed on the driveway or designated parking area in the R-1 or R-2 zoning districts unless otherwise approved by the community development department. c. No portable storage container or roll-off dumpster shall be stored within a required side yard setback between a building and an adjacent street or property line. For non-residential properties, no portable storage container or roll-off dumpster shall be located in any required landscape or buffer area.

equip.cite: § 45-38.D.9.e / outdoor storage, I-1 light industrial district [PDF pp. 881, 890 / printed pp. 2645, 2654]
equip.text: e. Storage: Outdoor storage is prohibited. The storage of all accessory equipment or products shall be contained within an accessory structure.... a. Outdoor storage may be permitted adjacent to a structure provided it is located in an area other than a parking area or yard setback area and screened from a street or abutting residentially zoned property by a masonry wall, ornamental fence or dense hedge planting no less than six (6) inches higher than the materials stored... When the outside storage is abutting a residential district, the height of the stored materials shall not exceed seven and one-half (7½) feet from the grade level.

equip.cite: Appendix A — Appearance Plan, § IV.8 [PDF p. 677 / printed p. 2049]
equip.text: 8. Mechanical equipment or other utility hardware on roof, ground, or buildings shall be screened from public view with materials harmonious with the building, or they shall be located so as not to be visible from any public ways, including waterways, service alleys, and adjoining properties.

equip.cite: Appendix A — Appearance Plan, definitions [PDF p. 682 / printed p. 2052]
equip.text: MECHANICAL EQUIPMENT—Equipment, devices, and accessories, the use of which relates to water supply, drainage, heating, ventilating, air conditioning, and similar purposes.

R-1 Single-family dwelling district.note: Front yard 25 ft for the first story and 30 ft for the second story, measured from the street line to the front building line. Rear yard 20 ft for the first story and 25 ft for the second story. Side yard 10 ft each side for the first story and 15 ft for the second story. Corner lots: no building nearer than 20 ft to the side street line. 'For a distance of one block on streets intersecting U.S.

R-2 Multiple-family dwelling district (s.note: 'For single-family dwellings the same as for the R-1 single-family dwelling district' (§ 45-28.C.1) — the 7,500 sq. ft. / 75 ft figures are those printed in § 45-27.C. Yard regulations in R-2 are stated directly: front yard not less than 25 ft; rear yard not less than 20 ft; side yard not less than 10 ft on each side; corner lots not nearer than 20 ft to the side street line.

gen.cite: § 58-336 Generators [PDF pp. 525—527]
gen.text: Sec. 58-336. Generators. Except for generators serving a public purpose and owned and operated by the town or temporary generators used during or after a natural disaster such as a tropical storm or hurricane event, and which are therefore exempt from these regulations, portable or permanent generators temporarily or permanently placed on the ground, on a stand or on a trailer, shall not be placed in the required front, street side or street rear yard setbacks; provided, however, not more than one such generator shall be placed in any given required side or rear yard setback as set forth below. (1) One portable or permanent generator with an output of not more than 30 KW shall be allowed in a required side or rear yard setback provided said generator meets the following conditions: a. Generators shall meet the zoning district setback requirements for principal structures, except that any encroachment of five feet or less is permitted. The generator must be set back a minimum of five feet from the property line. b. The generator shall not, at any time, or for any purpose, exceed 55 dBA at the property line from 7:00 p.m. to 8:00 a.m. c. The highest point on the generator shall not exceed a maximum of five feet above the neighboring property owner's finished grade. d. Generators that are not located within, or completely screened by a building, shall be screened from view from a public right-of-way or adjacent residential property line. Screening may include the use of fences, walls or hedges, or a combination thereof. e. The generator's exhaust is, as much as practically feasible, vented upwards or directed away from neighboring properties. f. The generator shall be used only during periods of power outages or for periodic testing and necessary maintenance operation and shall not be used to sell power back to a power company or for use by power customers during periods of peak demand. g. The generator shall be operated for routine testing and maintenance purposes not more than one time in any seven-day period and no test shall exceed 30 minutes. Testing of emergency generators is permitted Monday through Saturday only (excluding holidays), between the hours of 10:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. h. Testing may be conducted when the unit is being repaired, provided that such testing period shall not exceed 30 minutes and shall be conducted only between the hours of 10:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. Monday through Saturday, excluding holidays. i. Generators are not permitted on the roof of a building. (2) A portable or permanent generator may be permanently or temporarily placed on the ground, on a stand, or on a trailer outside of required yard setback areas; provided, however, said generator meets the following conditions: a. If the generator's output capability is greater than 30 KW, it shall be placed on the property only in conformance with the setback requirements applicable to a principal structure. b. The generator shall not, at any time or for any purpose, exceed 55 dBA at the property line from 7:00 p.m. to 8:00 a.m. c. The generator's exhaust is, as much as practically feasible, vented upwards or directed away from neighboring properties. d. The generator shall be used only during periods of power outages, periods of power reductions resulting from the exercise of utility load control programs or for periodic testing and necessary maintenance operation and shall not be used to sell power back to a power company. e. The generator shall be operated for routine testing and maintenance purposes not more than one time in any seven-day period and no test shall exceed 30 minutes. Testing of emergency generators is permitted Monday through Saturday only (excluding holidays), between the hours of 10:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. f. Testing may be conducted when the unit is being repaired, provided that such testing period shall not exceed 30 minutes and shall be conducted only between the hours of 10:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. Monday through Saturday, excluding holidays. g. Generators are not permitted on the roof of a building. (Ord. No. 457, § 2(Exh. A), 7-26-18).

gen.cite: § 58-8 Definitions — Fixed mechanical equipment [PDF p. 439]
gen.text: Fixed mechanical equipment means mechanical equipment, such as an air conditioning unit, water cooling tower, swimming pool pump, irrigation pump, well water pump, fan, power generator or other similar power source equipment, permanently affixed to land, as distinguished from temporary, portable, non-fixed mechanical equipment.

gen.text: (8) Congregate living facilities shall have a fully operational, whole house emergency generator that will function all electrical items in the event of an electrical power outage.

equip.cite: § 58-337 Air conditioning and swimming pool equipment [PDF p. 527]
equip.text: Sec. 58-337. Air conditioning and swimming pool equipment. (a) No portion of any air conditioning and/or swimming pool equipment (including filter, pump, and heating equipment) shall be located closer than five feet from a side or rear property line. In addition, such air conditioning or swimming pool equipment within ten feet from the side or rear property line shall be completely screened with a wall, or opaque fence or landscaping, as high as said equipment from the neighboring property. (b) Cooling towers shall be required to meet the same minimum yard setback requirements as the principal structure, and shall be screened from the neighbors and/or a street by a three-sided, concrete block masonry finished wall at least as high as said cooling tower. If the required wall is higher than the Code allows in a setback in order to screen the cooling tower from the neighbors and/or a street, said wall shall also meet the minimum yard setback requirement as the principal structure. (c) No air conditioning or swimming pool equipment shall be allowed in a front yard. (d) Any house that fronts on two or more streets shall be allowed to place air conditioning (excluding cooling towers) and/or swimming pool equipment in each required street side or street rear yard setback provided that the combination of said equipment does not exceed two in each of said setbacks; are not more than four feet in height above the natural grade or the minimum flood elevation, whichever is greater, occupy no more than 25 square feet in total area; and are setback a minimum of 20 feet from the street side or street rear property line and are screened from view by a wall as high as said equipment and three foot high hedge outside said wall. (Ord. No. 458, § 2(Exh. A), 7-26-18).

equip.cite: § 58-8 Definitions — Yard [PDF p. 467]
equip.text: Yard shall mean a space open and unobstructed from the ground to the sky, except by encroachments specifically permitted this code, on the same plot with a structure or use. Yard measurements shall be the minimum horizontal distances. See "setback."

equip.cite: § 58-312 Accessory uses [PDF p. 511]
equip.text: Sec. 58-312. Accessory uses. Accessory uses and structures in residential districts shall be constructed to conform with the building and site regulations in the district where the structure is to be located; provided, however, that all accessory uses and structures shall be located only in the side or rear yard at least six feet from the principal building. It shall be the responsibility of the town administrator to determine if a proposed accessory structure is necessarily and customarily associated with, and is appropriate, incidental, and subordinate to the principal structure, based on the evaluation of whether the proposed accessory structure is necessarily or customarily associated with the principal use of the lot. Determinations by the town administrator shall be subject to appeal pursuant to section 58-6(e). (Ord. No. 225, § 2(10-8B.), 2-8-90; Ord. No. 483, § 2, 7-22-21).

equip.cite: § 58-168 Accessory uses (R-1) [PDF p. 486]
equip.text: Accessory uses or buildings customarily incidental and subordinate to the main use or building shall be permitted in an R-1 single-family residential district, subject to Supplemental Regulations as contained in section 58-331 hereof. Accessory uses or buildings shall not be located within any required yard setbacks nor shall any accessory use or building be permitted in the front yard, except as may be allowed in section 58-331. [Identical language appears at § 58-183 for R-2 and, without the front-yard clause, at § 58-198 for R-3: 'Accessory uses or buildings shall not be located within any required yard setbacks, except as may be allowed in section 58-331.' § 58-214 (C-1) and § 58-228 (P): 'Accessory uses shall not be located within any required yard setbacks.']

equip.cite: § 58-331 Accessory buildings and storage sheds [PDF pp. 520—521]
equip.text:
Sec. 58-331. Accessory buildings and storage sheds. (a) Location and other requirements of accessory buildings. In residential districts, all accessory buildings and structures, except accessory dwelling units, that are intended to serve an accessory use, shall be erected in accordance with the requirements of this section, notwithstanding the provisions of section 58-312 regarding accessory uses. In all zoning districts, no garage, tent, trailer or other accessory structure shall be erected or used for residential purposes, prior to, concurrently with or subsequent to the construction of the principal building. Accessory buildings permanently affixed to the ground, including, but not limited to, detached garages, utility buildings and storage sheds, shall be limited to one building for each lot (except that greenhouse, cabana and gazebos may be permitted in addition to garage, carport, storage sheds and utility building); and (1) Shall be located to the rear of the principal building on interior lots and, in the case of corner lots, accessory buildings shall be located in the quarter section of the lot furthest removed from abutting frontages; (2) Shall be located a minimum of ten feet from the principal building; (3) Shall not exceed the height of the house or 15 feet, whichever is less, except that in the case of a principal building having a flat roof, the height of the accessory building may be six feet above the height of the house provided it is no higher than 15 feet; (4) Shall not be located within any required yard setbacks nor shall any accessory use be permitted in the front yard; (5) Shall not exceed more than five percent of the total square feet of the lot, provided that the building shall not exceed 40 percent of the footprint of the principal building, or have a footprint exceeding 1,000 square feet, whichever is less; (6) Shall not have a kitchen or toilet, and the eaves on any structure or building shall not overhang any easement or right-of-way or exceed the setback lines by more than two feet; (7) Shall incorporate design and color schemes compatible to the principal building, and the town may require enhanced landscaping to accompany the accessory building; (8) For any utilities serving the accessory building, they shall be underground; and
(9) Shall meet all other applicable site development and zoning regulations including maximum lot coverage requirements. (b) Utility buildings and storage sheds in setbacks. In all residential zoning districts with lots not exceeding 10,000 square feet, one accessory building used for storage (utility building or storage shed) may be permitted within the setback of the rear yard area of each lot, which, for purposes of this section, is defined to be that area between the primary building and the rear lot line, subject to the following restrictions:
(1) The minimum setback from the side and rear lot line shall be five feet; (2) The maximum height shall be eight feet; and
(3) The size shall not exceed 144 square feet. All other accessory buildings used as utility buildings or storage sheds, that do not meet the foregoing requirements in this sub-section, shall comply with the requirements of sub-section (a) above. (c) Corner lots. On corner lots bounded on two opposite sides by streets, accessory buildings shall not be located in either front yard, regardless of which side is actually considered the front yard.

equip.cite: § 58-319(b), (c), (g) Walls, fences and hedges (screening) [PDF pp. 513—514]
equip.text: (b) In residential areas, all walls, fences, and other such structures in the side and rear setbacks shall be limited to a height of six feet above the finished lot level, and all walls and fences located in the front setback shall not exceed four feet in height above the finished lot level, unless prohibited pursuant to section 58-315. Hedges shall not exceed ten feet in the side and rear setback, and six feet in the front setback, provided, however, that for any hedge in excess of four feet in height in the front setback, running along or parallel to the front property line, shall require that at least 15 consecutive feet of said hedge on or parallel to any front lot line not be opaque above four feet. Notwithstanding the foregoing, residential property abutting Belvedere Road or Haverhill Road, the boundary line of the town, or abutting a non-residential zoning district, may have a ten-foot hedge along the property line abutting the road, town boundary or non-residential property, and a six-foot wall or fence in the front setback if the front yard abuts Belvedere or Haverhill Road. (c) In all districts other than residential, all hedges, shrubbery, walls, fences or other such structures shall be limited to a height of eight feet above the finished lot level for the rear and side setbacks, and four feet for the front setback. (g) Fences and walls may be placed on the property line notwithstanding the applicable setback requirements, but no part thereof shall encroach over the property line.

equip.cite: § 58-319(a) Clearance from utility apparatus [PDF p. 513]
equip.text: (a) Subject to more stringent requirements of a utility provider, no fence, wall or hedge shall be constructed, installed or maintained within three feet of a fire hydrant, water connection, lift station, transformer, or other emergency apparatus placed for the purpose of fire protection, excluding telephone or light poles. Fences, walls or hedges shall not be placed within the area required by applicable fire and life safety codes to be clear and unobstructed for passage of emergency vehicles or for the ingress and egress of persons or animals.

equip.cite: § 58-316(a) Height limitations [PDF p. 512]
equip.text: (a) Generally. Water, cooling and fire towers, church spires, domes, cupolas, flagpoles, electrical and mechanical support systems, and similar structures, and their necessary mechanical appurtenances may be erected within a structure or on top of the structure, above the district height limitations provided in this chapter, after obtaining approval of the town council, based on their consideration of the standards for evaluating exceptions to district height regulations set forth in subsection (d) of this section.

Corner lots: front 30 feet; side (street side) 30 feet; rear 15 feet.

C-1 Limited commercial district.note: Corner lots: minimum front setback 20 feet; minimum side setback 15 feet; minimum rear setback 15 feet. Minimum building area, excluding accessory uses: printed as 'N/A'. Accessory uses (§ 58-214) shall not be located within any required yard setbacks.

P Public ownership district.note: The code prints NO building requirements, setbacks, lot size, coverage or height for the P public ownership district. Division 6 consists only of § 58-226 purpose and intent, § 58-227 permitted uses (public parks and recreation areas), § 58-228 accessory uses ('Accessory uses shall not be located within any required yard setbacks'), and § 58-229 special exceptions; §§ 58-230—58-250 are reserved.

PBI airport overlay (duplex / multifamil.note: Minimum lot size printed as '5,445 square feet per unit for 2 or more units on a single lot or 2 units attached to another unit and joined by a common wall on the lot line' — i.e. 5,445 square feet PER UNIT. Minimum lot width printed as '50 feet; or 45 feet for a unit attached to another unit and joined by a common wall on the lot line.' Side setback printed as '10 feet for duplexes and multifamily'.

PBI airport overlay (townhouse \u2014 in.sideNote: 7.5 feet for a single family detached dwelling; 10 feet for duplexes and multifamily, zero for townhouses and zero lot line homes that share a common wall on both sides; and 10 feet for zero lot line homes and townhouses that share a common wall only on 1 side.
PBI airport overlay (townhouse \u2014 in.note: Maximum lot coverage printed as '50 percent.

PBI airport overlay (townhouse \u2014 en.note: Lot size printed as 'for townhouse development, 1,500 square feet for interior lots, and 2,500 for end lots'; lot width 'for townhouse development, 22 feet for interior lots and 30 feet for end lots.' equip.cite: § 78-79(1) General provisions and exceptions [PDF p. 1026]
equip.text: Chimneys, water, fire, radio or television towers, church spires, domes, cupolas, state towers and scenery lofts, cooling towers, elevator bulkheads, smokestacks, flag poles, parapet walls and similar structures and their necessary mechanical appurtenances may be erected above the height limits prescribed. Every part of every required yard shall be open and unobstructed from the ground to the sky except as hereinafter provided or as otherwise permitted in this chapter: a. Sills or belt courses may project not over 18 inches into a required yard. b. Movable awnings may project not over three feet into a required yard, provided that where the yard is less than five feet in width the projection shall not exceed one-half the width of the yard. c. Chimneys, fireplaces or pilaster may project not over two feet into a required yard. d. Hoods, canopies, or marquees may project not over three feet into a required yard. e. Fences, walls and hedges shall be permitted in required yards subject to the provisions established herein. f. Accessory parking may be located in a required front, rear or side yard for single-family and two-family dwellings. g. In the CLIC-1 and C districts, required off-street parking space may be located in the front yard except that no parking shall be permitted within five feet of the front lot line. h. Open, unenclosed porches, platforms, or paved terraces not covered by a roof or canopy, and which do not extend above the level of the first floor of the building, may extend or project into the required yard area.

equip.cite: § 78-78(k)(1)a. Mixed use, traditional neighborhood district — architectural standards, general requirements [PDF p. 1023]
equip.text: The following shall be located in rear yards or sideyards not facing the streets: 1. Window and wall air conditioners; 2. Air conditioning compressors; 3. Heating and ventilation; 4. Irrigation and pool pumps; and 5. Electrical utility meters.

equip.cite: § 78-78(k)(1)b. Mixed use, traditional neighborhood district [PDF p. 1023]
equip.text: The following shall be located in the rear yards only and screened from view from public rights-of-way: 1. Clotheslines; 2. Clothes drying yards; 3. Antennas (excepting satellite dishes, which are regulated by chapter 74, article II of this Code); 4. Permanent barbecues.

equip.cite: § 78-78(g)(13) Mixed use, traditional neighborhood district — Utilities [PDF p. 1016]
equip.text: Utilities. Utilities shall be installed underground, with the exception of necessary related equipment that can only be located at ground level, such as controller cabinets, transformers, etc. All ground level equipment shall be screened from public view to the extent possible with town-approved landscaping, fences or walls, or combination thereof.

equip.cite: § 78-83(k)(1) MU district walls, fences and hedges standards — Mechanical equipment and service utilities [PDF p. 1051]
equip.text: In addition to the standards found within section 78-253 (Landscaping), the following standards shall apply: a. Mechanical equipment, television antennas, satellite dishes, communication devices, air conditioning units, and similar systems and service areas shall not be visible from the public sidewalk; and shall be located to the rear of a building or on an alley/service road, or on the roof, where feasible. b. Exhaust air fans and associated louvers may be allowed on secondary or tertiary building frontages above the first floor only. c. All mechanical equipment shall be screened from public view. d. Window air conditioning units shall not be visible from any street and shall not be located on the primary building facade. e. Utility connections and service boxes shall not be visible from any street and shall be placed on secondary walls and away from corners. f. Backflow preventers, double detector check valves, Siamese connections, and the like (or any other utility connections and service boxes) shall be located to the rear of the building or on an alley/service road or behind the building line on secondary frontages and away from corners.

equip.cite: § 78-83(k)(2)a. MU district — fences, walls and hedges [PDF p. 1051]
equip.text: Fences, walls, and hedges for nonresidential and mixed use buildings shall not be permitted in the front yard (or in front of the building line) and shall only be permitted along the building line and behind the building line (or along side and rear lot lines) and/or when used in conjunction with the following: i. Screening of mechanical equipment; ii. Screening of off-street loading and service areas; iii. Screening of commercial containers; iv. Required perimeter buffer when abutting residential lot lines; and v. Screening of off-street parking lots.

equip.cite: § 78-253(a)(2) Minimum landscape requirements — nonresidential districts [PDF p. 1179]
equip.text: The following uses within nonresidential zoning districts shall be required to be screened from public view (see also subsection (h) of this section): a. Backflow preventer systems. b. Trash (dumpster) containers and recycling containers. c. Storage or mechanical equipment areas. d. Outside display or sales areas. e. Parking areas.

equip.cite: § 78-253(b)(2) Minimum landscape requirements — residential districts [PDF p. 1180]
equip.text: The following uses within residential zoning districts shall be required to be screened with landscaping: a. Lift stations; b. Backflow preventers; c. Ground-mounted air conditioning units; d. RV parking areas; e. Boat storage areas; f. Maintenance and storage areas; and g. Dumpster or trash pickup areas.

equip.cite: § 78-335(4) Architectural elements — Mechanical equipment screening [PDF p. 1204]
equip.text: Mechanical equipment screening. All rooftop mechanical equipment shall be located at a distance from the edge of the building and properly screened so as not to be visible from any street or adjoining property. Materials used for screening purposes shall be compatible with the architectural style, color, and materials of the principal building.

equip.cite: Appendix A to Ch. 78 (NBOZ), § 6-1.B Screening of mechanical equipment [PDF p. 1260]
equip.text: B. Screening of mechanical equipment. 1. All mechanical equipment shall be screened from public view. 2. Such screening may include any combination of landscaping and non-living opaque materials. 3. If building materials are to be utilized for screening purposes, such materials shall be consistent with the architectural design of the principal structure. 4. Screening shall extend at least one foot above the object to be screened.

equip.cite: Appendix A to Ch. 78 (NBOZ), § 3-5.D Mechanical equipment screening [PDF p. 1227]
equip.text: D. Mechanical equipment screening. All rooftop mechanical equipment shall be located at a distance from the edge of the building and properly screened so as not to be visible from any street or adjoining property. Materials used for screening purposes shall be compatible with the architectural style, color, and materials of the principal building.

equip.cite: Appendix A to Ch. 78 (NBOZ), § 4-5.B Screening required [PDF p. 1240]
equip.text: Screening required. Uses within the overlay zone that shall be required to be screened from public view include mechanical equipment areas, parking areas, satellite dishes mounted on the ground, chainlink or other nonopaque fence or wall type, accessory use structures, and other elements as defined by this division.

equip.cite: § 78-75(2)d. CLIC-1 — Accessory uses [PDF p. 986]
equip.text: Accessory uses. Accessory uses customarily incidental and subordinate to the main use or building shall be permitted in the CLIC zoning district. Accessory uses shall not be located within any required setbacks.

equip.cite: § 78-70(c) PADD — permitted and special exception uses [PDF p. 922]
equip.text: All principal permitted and special exception uses shall occur within enclosed buildings or structures. This requirement shall not apply to permitted accessory uses such as outdoor seating, the permitted outdoor display of merchandise, mechanical equipment, dumpsters and related refuse disposal equipment, or other uses incidental and subordinate to a principal permitted or special exception use.

equip.cite: § 78-82(d) Distribution electric substation — Minimum setbacks [PDF p. 1029]
equip.text: (d) Minimum setbacks. (1) In residential zoning districts, any building or structure must be setback 100 feet from all property lines. (2) In commercial zoning districts, the setback must comply with the applicable criteria for similar uses in that district. [Also: (e)(2)b. A buffer wall that is a minimum of eight feet high to a maximum of 14 feet and within 15 feet of the substation equipment, with native landscaping as required by the town, shall be maintained around the perimeter of the substation equipment.]

equip.cite: § 78-141 Accessory and temporary buildings [PDF p. 1109]
equip.text: (a) No garage or other use appurtenant to a main building shall be erected or constructed except during the progress of the construction of a main building, or until the main building is completed. (b) No trailer, basement, tent, shack, garage, barn or other building shall, at any time, be used as a residence temporarily or permanently, nor shall any structure of a temporary character be used as a residence.

equip.cite: § 78-62(1)c. / § 78-63(1)c. / § 78-64(1)c. etc. — Accessory buildings in residence districts [PDF pp. 909, 910-911, 912-913]
equip.text: Accessory buildings must comply with the requirements of this Code and the Florida Building Code as amended. Accessory uses must be located on the same lot or parcel of land as the principal structure and the accessory use must be customarily incidental to the principal use. Permissible accessory uses for multifamily residences, planned unit developments, commercial and other permitted uses shall be determined in the site planning process or administratively on a case-by-case basis and subject to these standards.

equip.cite: § 26-61 Swimming pools — Setback [PDF p. 388]
equip.text: The outside rim of a private swimming pool shall be set back not less than ten feet from both rear and side property lines.

equip.cite: § 78-325(a) Flexible land development regulations — Building setbacks [PDF p. 1195]
equip.text: Building setbacks. Up to 20 percent of the land development regulations for the front, side yard, side and rear setbacks may be waived, upon the community development director's determination that one or more of the following conditions exists. (1) There are site or structural conditions, such as, but not limited to: the lot size is less than 1.0 acre; or the lot has topographic limitations that require placement of a structure into the required setback area. [§ 78-324(c): These flexible land development regulations are only be permitted in nonresidential zoning districts.]

R-1AA (single-family residences).note: "Single-family residences shall conform with R-1A residence districts, except as follows": building site area not less than 10,000 sq ft and street frontage at least 100 ft, except lots fronting a street-terminating circle may have frontage less than 100 ft (area still not less than 10,000 sq ft, frontage not less than 50 ft); height limit two stories or 30 feet.

R-1AA (multiple-family structures).note: Height limit eight stories or 100 feet. Building site area: not less than 2,000 sq ft of land per dwelling unit, plus an additional 1,000 sq ft per dwelling unit built above three stories or 40 feet. No multiple-family structure shall have less than 7,000 sq ft total floor area nor less than ten dwelling units.

R-1A.note: Height: no building or structure used as a dwelling, or accessory to a dwelling, shall exceed two stories or 30 feet; church height limit 45 feet (nonhabitable architectural features excluded). Building site area 7,500 sq ft with frontage at the building line of at least 75 ft; corner lots not less than 10,000 sq ft and 100 ft frontage.

R-1B (single-family dwelling).note: Height two stories or 30 feet (churches 45 feet). Minimum lot width at the building line 75 ft for interior lots, 100 ft for corner lots. Coverage: no building or structures with accessory buildings shall occupy more than 60 percent of the lot or parcel area, exclusive of front and side yards. Front yard 30 ft except in blocks where a 25-foot front yard has already been established.

R-1B (two-family (duplex) dwelling).note: Building site area 10,000 sq ft for a two-family (duplex) dwelling. Minimum lot width at the building line 75 ft interior / 100 ft corner. Minimum first floor area of a two-family dwelling structure 1,400 sq ft exclusive of carport, garage, unenclosed terraces or porches. No garage apartment permitted as an accessory use on a lot with a two-family dwelling.

R-1.note: Height two stories or 30 feet (churches 45 feet). Building site area 7,500 sq ft with frontage at the building line of at least 75 ft; corner lots not less than 10,000 sq ft and 100 ft frontage. Coverage: not more than 60 percent of the lot or parcel on interior or corner lots, exclusive of front and side yards. Front yard 30 ft except in blocks where a 25-foot front yard has already been established.

R-2A (single-family structures).note: Height two stories or 30 feet (churches 45 feet). Building site area 7,500 sq ft with frontage at the building line of at least 75 ft; corner lots not less than 10,000 sq ft and 100 ft frontage. Coverage: the section prints two different figures — § 78-65(3)a.

R-2A (multiple-family structures).note: Height two stories or 30 feet (churches 45 feet). Building site area: three-family dwellings 12,000 sq ft; structures having more than three dwelling units 2,000 sq ft for each additional unit added to the base of 12,000 sq ft. Minimum lot width at the building line 75 ft interior / 100 ft corner. Front yard 30 ft except in blocks where a 25-foot front yard has already been established.

R-2 (single-family dwellings).note: Building site area 7,500 sq ft. Lot size: minimum width at the building line 75 ft interior / 100 ft corner, except in townhouse developments where these standards apply to the overall townhouse development site; individual townhouse lots are not limited. Coverage: no building or structure with its accessory buildings shall occupy more than 50 percent of the lot or parcel area.

R-2 (two-family duplex dwellings).note: Building site area 10,000 sq ft. Minimum first floor area 1,400 sq ft with each unit comprising 700 sq ft; a one-bedroom unit of not less than 580 sq ft may be built together with a second unit of not less than 820 sq ft. No garage apartment permitted as an accessory use on a lot with a two-story dwelling (duplex) or a multiple-family structure.

R-2 (three-family dwelling).note: Building site area 12,000 sq ft for a three-family dwelling; structures having more than three dwelling units require 2,000 sq ft for each additional unit added to the base of 12,000 sq ft. For structures of more than two dwelling units the minimum required floor area is an additional 580 sq ft for each dwelling unit in excess of two, added to the base of 1,400 sq ft.

R-3.note: Height: for residences, no building or structure shall exceed two stories or 30 feet; for all other permitted uses, no building or structure shall exceed two stories or 30 feet and the minimum height shall not be less than 13 feet. Building site area: "The minimum width and depth of any professional or commercial building shall be 25 feet" — no minimum lot area, lot width or coverage is printed for this district.

C-1B neighborhood commercial district.sideNote: Side yard. There shall be a side yard setback of not less than ten feet, unless the property to be developed abuts a residential district, in which case the setback shall be 15 feet. Provided however, that on a corner lot, there shall be a side yard setback of not less than 15 feet from the property line of the intersecting street.
C-1B neighborhood commercial district.note: Height: no building or structure shall exceed two stories or 30 feet; minimum height of any building or structure shall not be less than 13 feet. "Maximum lot size shall not exceed one-half acre." Front yard setback measured from the street right-of-way line adjacent to the property to the front wall of a building or structure.

PADD \u2014 Core Sub-District.frontNote: Front Setback 15 feet (Maximum). NOTE: At least 50 percent of the building line of all new construction and any substantial repair, renovation, rehabilitation, or restoration of an existing building shall have a front setback of zero feet.
PADD \u2014 Core Sub-District.sideNote: Side Setback (Interior) 15 feet when adjacent to existing buildings.
PADD \u2014 Core Sub-District.note: Park Avenue Downtown District (PADD), Core Sub-District, Table 78-70-2. Building Height (Maximum) 12 stories (160 feet), see § 78-70(b)(7)b.3. for an additional height waiver for structured parking. Story Height Maximum 12 feet per story, 20 feet maximum for ground floor, and top floor or middle floor. Minimum Building Height: new development shall have a minimum building height of two stories.

PADD \u2014 Outer Sub-District.sideNote: Side Setback (Interior) None, 15 feet when adjacent to single-family districts * — (*) For those yards adjacent to single-family districts, even when separated by a right-of-way, a minimum 15 foot setback is required.

PADD \u2014 Outer Sub-District.note: Park Avenue Downtown District (PADD), Outer Sub-District, Table 78-70-3. Front Setback is printed as "15 feet (Minimum)". Building Height (Maximum) 4 stories (56 feet). Story Height Maximum 12 feet per story, 20 feet maximum for ground floor. Parking shall be located at the rear of the site, except for townhouse driveways. Sidewalk Width (Minimum) 10 feet.

C-1 business district.note: No interior side yard is printed; the only side yard requirement is "On a corner lot, there shall be a side yard of not less than 15 feet from the property line of the intersecting streets." Rear yard 15 ft, "except where there is an existing dedicated alleyway adjacent to the rear lot line, the rear yard shall be not less than five feet.

C-2 business districts.note: No interior side yard is printed; only "On a corner lot, there shall be a side yard of not less than 15 feet from the property line of the intersecting streets." Rear yard 15 ft except not less than five feet where there is an existing dedicated alleyway adjacent to the rear lot line.

C-3 Twin Cities Mixed Use District (Towe.note: Table 2: TOWER BUILDING TYPE. Permitted Heights Range: 6-12 Stories or 160 feet. Lot Width and Lot Depth N/A. Lot Area minimum 30,000 SF. Impervious Area maximum 90%; Pervious Area minimum 10%. Street Setbacks (front and side): minimum 10', maximum 15'.

C-3 Twin Cities Mixed Use District (Line.note: Table 3: LINER BUILDING TYPE. Permitted Heights Range: 6-8 stories or 112 feet. Lot Width/Lot Depth N/A. Lot Area minimum 22,000 SF. Impervious maximum 90%, Pervious minimum 10%. Street Setbacks (front and side) minimum 10', maximum N/A.

C-3 Twin Cities Mixed Use District (Cour.note: Table 4: COURTYARD BUILDING TYPE A (detached surface or garage parking). Permitted Heights Range: 4-6 Stories or 88 feet. Lot Width/Depth N/A. Lot Area minimum 24,000 SF. Impervious maximum 90%, Pervious minimum 10%. Street Setbacks (front and side) minimum 10'. Other Setbacks (interior side and rear) minimum 0', "Except 30' minimum when abutting an existing residential district."

Street Setbacks (front and side) minimum 10'. Other Setbacks (interior side and rear) minimum 0', "Except 30' minimum when abutting an existing residential district."

C-3 Twin Cities Mixed Use District (Town.note: Table 6: TOWNHOUSE BUILDING TYPE A (detached garage/parking, private rear yard). Permitted Heights Range: 3 Stories or 44 feet. Lot Width minimum 25', maximum 30'. Lot Depth minimum 80'. Lot Area minimum 1800 sf. Impervious maximum 90%, Pervious minimum 10%. Street Setbacks (front and side) minimum 10'. Other Setbacks (interior side and rear) minimum 0'.

Table 7: TOWNHOUSE BUILDING TYPE B (attached garage, no private rear yard). SUB-AREA: 3 Stories or 44 feet. Lot Width minimum 25', maximum 30'. Lot Depth minimum 70'. Lot Area minimum 1800 sf. Minimum 15 feet between building groups; groups not greater than 7 attached units.

C-4 business district.rearNote: Rear yard. No rear yard is required where the lot abuts on an existing or proposed railroad right-of-way or spur that is utilized by the facility.

Side yard: "No building or structure shall be located closer than 12 feet from one side yard line." CLIC-1 campus light industrial/commercia.sideNote: Side yard. No building or structure shall be located closer than ten feet or a distance equal to one-half the building height, whichever is the greater, to a side yard line, with one of said side setback being paved for its entire length.
