gen.cite: Sec. 30-34(5) Noise — exhausts [PDF p. 406]
gen.text: Exhausts. The discharge into the open air of the exhaust of any engine, stationary internal combustion engine, or motor vehicle or motorboat engine, except through a muffler or other device which will effectively prevent loud or explosive noises therefrom, except for the testing of emergency generators as required by law during the hours of 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. weekdays.

equip.cite: Sec. 31-238(k) Utility/mechanical equipment [PDF p. 748]
equip.text: Utility/mechanical equipment. Utility and mechanical equipment used for a building's operation which is located outside the building shall only be located in a rear or side yard. The equipment shall not be located within a utility easement unless it is equipment serving that specific easement. The minimum distance from a property line to the structure shall be no less than the structure's height. All equipment shall be screened from view by landscape materials as provided for in this Code. These requirements shall not apply to municipal or franchise utilities such as power, phone, cable, communication or drainage equipment which is located within a public utility easement.

equip.cite: Sec. 31-238(a) Accessory uses — General [PDF p. 741]
equip.text: General. No accessory uses shall be permitted in a required yard or bufferyard area, except as set forth below. In no event shall an accessory use be construed to authorize a use not otherwise permitted in the district in which the principal use is located and in no event shall an accessory use be established prior to the principal use to which it is accessory. No permanent structures shall be permitted in utility easements without the prior written approval of the appropriate utilities, and the concurrence of the City.

equip.cite: Sec. 31-238(j) Utility sheds [PDF p. 748]
equip.text: Utility sheds. Utility sheds shall be permitted in all residential districts, subject to the following: (1) No more than one utility shed shall be permitted for each parcel or lot; (2) No utility shed shall be permitted in any required front or side yard area or within utility, drainage or access easements; (3) The maximum dimensions of a utility shed shall be no more than 100 square feet in footprint and eight feet in height; and (4) Rear and side setbacks for utility sheds on single-family and duplex lots shall be a minimum of three feet from the lot lines. Rear and side setbacks for utility sheds on all other property shall be equal to the height of the structure.

equip.cite: Sec. 31-238(l) Waterfront lands [PDF p. 748]
equip.text: Waterfront lands. A rear yard setback of 20 feet from the rear or waterfront line measured landward therefrom shall be provided and no building construction, to include principal and accessory buildings shall be permitted in this setback.

equip.cite: Sec. 31-238(n) Structure parking [PDF p. 749]
equip.text: Structure parking. All structure parking shall be incorporated into the building envelope and shall be compatibly designed to complement the primary use structure for which it serves. If the parking structure is larger than the primary use building and any surface of the top level of the parking structure can be seen from the primary use building on the site, then that area of the top level shall be landscaped and/or decoratively paved so as to provide amenity area(s) for the building occupants. All mechanical equipment on the top level shall also be screened from view.

equip.cite: Sec. 31-238(o)(13) Renewable energy devices — ground installations [PDF p. 750]
equip.text: Ground installations shall comply with the site development criteria of the applicable zoning district.

equip.cite: Sec. 31-233(c)(1)d. Architectural design standards — non-residential development [PDF p. 736]
equip.text: All mechanical equipment (including roof-mounted equipment) shall be screened with materials consistent with those used in the construction of the building. The screening material and structure shall be architecturally compatible with the building. The screening shall be high enough so that the equipment is not visible from any adjacent public right-of-way and designed so that the equipment is well concealed from adjacent properties.

CNS.note: Conservation District. The section prints uses permitted only — no lot, yard, height or coverage standards are printed for this district. Water surface and land under water of all canals, intracoastal waterways, lakes and other water areas in the City not otherwise zoned is placed in the CNS zoning district.

RS1.note: Maximum height: Two stories or 30 feet above the centerline of the road whichever is less. Minimum floor area not including garage or unairconditioned areas: 2,500 square feet. Densities shall not exceed 13 units per net acre. Plot coverage is the combined plot area covered by all principal and accessory buildings.

RS2.frontNote: Front yards: Minimum of ten feet in depth for a maximum of 50 percent of the lot frontage. In all cases a minimum distance of 20 feet shall be maintained between the garage door and the right of way line.
RS2.sideNote: Side yards: Minimum of six feet in width for a maximum of 50 percent of the lot depth. A corner side setback shall be 15 feet on the side of the plot abutting on the side street or canal or waterway.
RS2.rearNote: Rear yards: Minimum of 15 feet. All lots which border in the rear of the lot upon a canal or waterway shall provide a minimum setback of 25 feet in depth from the edge of water or property line, which ever provides the greater setback.
RS2.note: Maximum height: Three stories, not to exceed 55 feet above the centerline of the road whichever is less. Minimum floor area not including garage or unairconditioned areas: 1,500 square feet. Densities shall not exceed 25 units per net acre. Zero lot line dwelling units permitted.

RMF3 (duplexes).note: Each dwelling of a two-family structure shall be located on a plot not less than 60 feet in width and 4,000 square feet in area. Maximum height two stories or 25 feet. Minimum open space 35 percent of total lot area; minimum distances between buildings 30 feet at the closest point or the sum of the building heights divided by two, whichever is greater.

RMF3 (townhouses).note: Townhouses: Not less than 160 feet in width and 16,000 square feet in plot area. Where townhouse dwellings are designed, arranged and constructed for the ownership of each dwelling unit and the land thereunder by a separate and different owner, each dwelling unit may be located on a lot not less than 20 feet in width, and 80 feet in depth.

RMF3 (low- and mid-rise apartments).note: Low- and mid-rise apartments: Not less than 100 feet in width and 16,000 square feet in plot area. Maximum height four stories or 45 feet. Side yards 25 feet in depth. Minimum open space 35 percent of total lot area; minimum distances between buildings 30 feet at the closest point or the sum of the building heights divided by two, whichever is greater.

RMF3A (duplexes).note: Maximum height two stories or 25 feet. Minimum open space 35 percent of total lot area; building separation 30 feet or sum of building heights divided by two, whichever is greater; floor area ratio by height (1 story 0.30, 2 story 0.50, 3 story 0.75, 4 story 0.90, 5 story 1.05, 6 story 1.25, 7 story 1.50).

RMF3A (townhouses).note: Not less than 160 feet in width and 16,000 square feet in plot area; individually owned townhouse lots may be not less than 20 feet in width and 80 feet in depth; each dwelling unit of a quadruplex on a lot of minimum of 1,600 feet. Maximum height three stories or 35 feet. Minimum open space 35 percent of total lot area; building separation 30 feet or sum of building heights divided by two, whichever is greater.

RMF3A (low-rise apartments).note: Not less than 100 feet in width and 16,000 square feet in plot area. Maximum height four stories or 45 feet. Side yards 25 feet in depth. Minimum open space 35 percent of total lot area; building separation 30 feet or sum of building heights divided by two, whichever is greater; floor area ratio by height (1 story 0.30, 2 story 0.50, 3 story 0.75, 4 story 0.90, 5 story 1.05, 6 story 1.25, 7 story 1.50).

RMF3A (mid-rise apartments).note: Not less than 100 feet in width and 16,000 square feet in plot area. Maximum height seven stories or 80 feet. Side yards 25 feet in depth. Minimum open space 35 percent of total lot area; building separation 30 feet or sum of building heights divided by two, whichever is greater; floor area ratio by height (1 story 0.30, 2 story 0.50, 3 story 0.75, 4 story 0.90, 5 story 1.05, 6 story 1.25, 7 story 1.50).

RMF3B (single-family and zero lot line).frontNote: Front yards: Principal buildings fronting the public right-of-way, between one and two stories, shall be setback at least ten feet. Principal buildings fronting the public right-of-way, three stories in height, shall be setback at least 15 feet. Principal buildings fronting the public right-of-way, four stories in height, shall be setback at least 20 feet.
RMF3B (single-family and zero lot line).rearNote: Rear yards: Principal buildings, between one and two stories, shall be setback at least 15 feet. Principal buildings three or more stories in height shall be setback at least 20 feet.
RMF3B (single-family and zero lot line).note: Each dwelling unit shall be located on a plot not less than 40 feet in width and 4,000 square feet in area. Maximum height three stories or 35 feet; structure parking shall be counted in computing building height. Minimum open space 35 percent of total lot area; floor area ratio by height (1 story 0.30, 2 story 0.50, 3 story 0.75, 4 story 0.90).

RMF3B (two-family dwellings).frontNote: Front yards: Principal buildings fronting the public right-of-way, between one and two stories, shall be setback at least ten feet. Principal buildings fronting the public right-of-way, three stories in height, shall be setback at least 15 feet. Principal buildings fronting the public right-of-way, four stories in height, shall be setback at least 20 feet.
RMF3B (two-family dwellings).rearNote: Rear yards: Principal buildings, between one and two stories, shall be setback at least 15 feet. Principal buildings three or more stories in height shall be setback at least 20 feet.
RMF3B (two-family dwellings).note: Each dwelling unit shall be located on a plot not less than 60 feet in width and 4,000 square feet in area. Maximum height two stories or 25 feet. Minimum open space 35 percent of total lot area; floor area ratio by height (1 story 0.30, 2 story 0.50, 3 story 0.75, 4 story 0.90).

RMF3B (triplexes and quadruplexes).frontNote: Front yards: Principal buildings fronting the public right-of-way, between one and two stories, shall be setback at least ten feet. Principal buildings fronting the public right-of-way, three stories in height, shall be setback at least 15 feet. Principal buildings fronting the public right-of-way, four stories in height, shall be setback at least 20 feet.
RMF3B (triplexes and quadruplexes).rearNote: Rear yards: Principal buildings, between one and two stories, shall be setback at least 15 feet. Principal buildings three or more stories in height shall be setback at least 20 feet.
RMF3B (triplexes and quadruplexes).note: Maximum height two stories or 25 feet. No minimum lot area or width is printed for triplexes and quadruplexes in the RMF3B list of minimum lot areas and widths. Minimum open space 35 percent of total lot area; floor area ratio by height (1 story 0.30, 2 story 0.50, 3 story 0.75, 4 story 0.90).

RMF3B (townhouses).frontNote: Front yards: Principal buildings fronting the public right-of-way, between one and two stories, shall be setback at least ten feet. Principal buildings fronting the public right-of-way, three stories in height, shall be setback at least 15 feet. Principal buildings fronting the public right-of-way, four stories in height, shall be setback at least 20 feet.
RMF3B (townhouses).rearNote: Rear yards: Principal buildings, between one and two stories, shall be setback at least 15 feet. Principal buildings three or more stories in height shall be setback at least 20 feet.
RMF3B (townhouses).note: Not less than 160 feet in width and 16,000 square feet in plot area; individually owned townhouse lots may be not less than 20 feet in width and 60 feet in depth; each dwelling unit of a quadruplex on a lot of minimum of 1,600 feet. Maximum height three stories or 35 feet.

RMF3B (low-rise apartments).frontNote: Front yards: Principal buildings fronting the public right-of-way, between one and two stories, shall be setback at least ten feet. Principal buildings fronting the public right-of-way, three stories in height, shall be setback at least 15 feet. Principal buildings fronting the public right-of-way, four stories in height, shall be setback at least 20 feet.
RMF3B (low-rise apartments).rearNote: Rear yards: Principal buildings, between one and two stories, shall be setback at least 15 feet. Principal buildings three or more stories in height shall be setback at least 20 feet.
RMF3B (low-rise apartments).note: Not less than 100 feet in width and 16,000 square feet in plot area. Maximum height four stories or 45 feet. Side yards 25 feet in depth. Minimum open space 35 percent of total lot area; floor area ratio by height (1 story 0.30, 2 story 0.50, 3 story 0.75, 4 story 0.90).

RMF4 (duplexes).note: Minimum lot area and width for duplexes, townhouses and low- and mid-rise apartments: As required in the RMF3 and RMF3A Zoning Districts. Maximum height two stories or 25 feet. Plot coverage 40 percent; minimum open space 40 percent of the lot area used in the Floor Area Ratio calculation; building separation 30 feet or the sum of the building heights divided by two, whichever is greater.

RMF4 (townhouses).note: Minimum lot area and width as required in the RMF3 and RMF3A Zoning Districts. Maximum height three stories or 35 feet. Plot coverage 40 percent; minimum open space 40 percent of the lot area used in the Floor Area Ratio calculation; building separation 30 feet or the sum of the building heights divided by two, whichever is greater.

RMF4 (low- and mid-rise apartments).note: Minimum lot area and width as required in the RMF3 and RMF3A Zoning Districts. Side yards 25 feet in depth. The RMF4 maximum-height list prints heights only for duplexes, townhouses and high-rise apartments — no height is printed for low- and mid-rise apartments in this district. Plot coverage 40 percent; minimum open space 40 percent of the lot area used in the Floor Area Ratio calculation.

RMF4 (high-rise apartments).note: High-rise apartments: Not less than 100 feet in width and 16,000 square feet in plot area. Maximum height 25 stories or 250 feet.

B1.sideNote: There is no side or rear yard setback for a plot which is not adjacent to a street or alley.
B1.rearNote: There is no side or rear yard setback for a plot which is not adjacent to a street or alley.
B1.note: Neighborhood Business. Setbacks: Except as otherwise provided every plot shall have a front yard not less than 25 feet in depth. Every plot shall have a street side yard of not less than 20 feet in depth. Maximum height two stories or 35 feet. Floor area ratio 0.40 at one story, increased by 0.11 for each additional story; total lot coverage not to exceed 40 percent of total lot area.

B2.sideNote: Side and rear yard: There is no side or rear yard setback required for a plot which is not adjacent to a street or alley. A side and rear yard setback of 20 feet in depth is required for a plot adjacent to a residentially zoned district, street or alley.
B2.rearNote: Side and rear yard: There is no side or rear yard setback required for a plot which is not adjacent to a street or alley. A side and rear yard setback of 20 feet in depth is required for a plot adjacent to a residentially zoned district, street or alley.
B2.note: Community Business. Minimum lot area and width: There shall be no minimum required width or area of plot except as otherwise provided. Maximum height 12 stories or 120 feet overall maximum height, including structure parking, provided that a height limitation of five stories shall apply only for shopping center buildings subject to subsection (5)a.4.

B3.sideNote: Side and rear yard: There is no side or rear yard setback required for a plot which is not adjacent to a street or alley. A side and rear yard setback of 20 feet in depth is required for a plot adjacent to a residentially zoned district, street or alley.
B3.rearNote: Side and rear yard: There is no side or rear yard setback required for a plot which is not adjacent to a street or alley. A side and rear yard setback of 20 feet in depth is required for a plot adjacent to a residentially zoned district, street or alley.
B3.note: Heavy Business. Minimum lot area and width: There shall be no minimum required width or area of plot except as otherwise provided. Maximum height 12 stories or 120 feet overall maximum height, including structure parking.

OP.rearNote: Rear yard: Not less than 25 feet in depth. Adjacent to any RS districts, the rear yard setback shall be 30 feet in depth.
OP.note: Office Park. Minimum lot area: 1.5 acres including right-of-way dedications; minimum frontage 100 feet. Maximum height ten stories, or 100 feet overall maximum height, including structure parking. No parking areas shall be located within 30 feet of any residentially zoned property or within ten feet of any street line. Street side yard not less than 15 feet in depth. No interior side yard setback is printed.

MO.note: Medical Office. Minimum lot area 1.5 acres including right-of-way dedications; minimum frontage 100 feet. For properties lying between NE 206 Street to the south, NE 209 Street to the north, NE 28 Avenue to the east and East Dixie Highway to the west: minimum frontage 100 feet with a minimum lot area of 0.5 acres; minimum front yard ten feet in depth for the first two stories and 15 feet for additional stories.

TC1.sideNote: Side: There is no side yard setback required for a plot not adjacent to a street or alley, or where such setback is necessary to provide light and air to residential units. In such cases a side yard setback of 20 feet in depth is required.
TC1.rearNote: Rear: There is no rear yard setback required for a plot not adjacent to a street or alley, or where such setback is necessary to provide light and air to residential units. In such cases a rear yard setback of 20 feet in depth is required.
TC1.note: Town Center District. Maximum height four stories or 50 feet, including parking structures. Maximum floor density: residential component 25 dwelling units per gross acre; nonresidential component 2.0 floor area ratio.

TC2.sideNote: Side: There is no side yard setback required for a plot not adjacent to a street or alley, or where such setback is necessary to provide light and air to residential units. In such cases a side yard setback of 20 feet in depth is required. A minimum side yard setback of ten feet from edge of water is required, where applicable.
TC2.rearNote: Rear: There is no rear yard setback required for a plot not adjacent to a street or alley, or where such setback is necessary to provide light and air to residential units. In such cases a rear yard setback of 20 feet in depth is required. A minimum rear yard setback of ten feet from edge of water is required.
TC2.note: Town Center Marine District. Maximum height four stories or 50 feet, including parking structures. Maximum floor density: residential component 25 dwelling units per gross acre; non-residential component 2.0 floor area ratio. Between buildings: no minimum separation normally required, except where necessary to provide light and air to residential units, in which case buildings may be no closer than 25 feet.

TC3.sideNote: Side: There is no side yard setback required for a lot that is not adjacent to a street or alley, unless such setback is necessary to provide light and air to residential units. In such cases a side yard setback of 20 feet in depth is required.
TC3.rearNote: Rear: There is no rear yard setback required for a plot not adjacent to a street or alley, unless such setback is necessary to provide light and air to residential units. In such cases a rear yard setback of 20 feet in depth is required.
TC3.note: Town Center Neighborhood District. Minimum lot size: Five gross acres. Maximum lot coverage 45 percent of total lot area, provided that if 80 percent or more of the required parking spaces is provided in a parking structure, lot coverage may be increased to a maximum of 55 percent. Maximum height four stories or 50 feet, including parking structures. Street side 20 feet; rear street 20 feet.

TC4.sideNote: Side: There is no side yard setback required for a lot that is not adjacent to a street or alley, unless such setback is necessary to provide light and air to residential units. In such cases a side yard setback of 20 feet in depth is required.
TC4.rearNote: Rear: There is no rear yard setback required for a plot not adjacent to a street or alley, unless such setback is necessary to provide light and air to residential units. In such cases a rear yard setback of 20 feet in depth is required.
TC4.note: Town Center Office Park Mixed Use District. Minimum lot size: Five gross acres. Maximum lot coverage 45 percent of total lot area, provided that if 80 percent or more of the required parking spaces is provided in a parking structure, lot coverage may be increased to a maximum of 55 percent. Maximum height ten stories or 100 feet, including parking structures. Street side 20 feet; rear street 20 feet.

TC5.frontNote: Frontages abutting public or private streets: No required setback as long as a minimum 10-foot-wide clear pedestrian path is provided within a combination of the right-of-way or private property. The pedestrian path may be reduced to five feet in order to accommodate street trees, required utility apparatus, or other street furniture.
TC5.note: Town Center North Planned Development District (a planned development district implemented through a City Commission-approved General Plan of Development and Design Guidelines, which prevail over the Code in the event of conflict). Maximum height: 30 stories — no height in feet is printed. Maximum density and floor area: residential component 62 dwelling units per gross acre.

M1.rearNote: Rear: 15 feet. Rear, from edge of water: Ten feet.
M1.note: Light Industrial District. Maximum height: No building or structure shall be erected or altered to a height exceeding three stories or 45 feet, whichever is less. Setbacks: Front 25 feet; no parking areas shall be located within 30 feet of any residentially zoned property or within ten feet of any street line. Side street 15 feet. Rear 15 feet. Rear, from edge of water: ten feet.

CF.rearNote: Rear: 20 feet. Rear, from edge of water: 10 feet.
CF.note: Community Facilities District. Maximum height: No building or structure shall be erected or altered to a height exceeding ten stories or 120 feet, whichever is less. Setbacks: Front 25 feet; no parking areas shall be located within 30 feet of any residentially zoned property or within 10 feet of any street line. Side street 30 feet. Rear 20 feet. Rear, from edge of water: 10 feet.

ROS.note: Recreation/Open Space District. Setbacks: All 25 feet. Adjacent to any trafficway 75 feet. Maximum height: No building or structure shall be erected or altered to a height exceeding five stories or 60 feet, whichever is less. No lot coverage or floor area ratio is printed.

U.note: Utilities District. Setbacks: All 25 feet. Adjacent to any trafficway: 75 feet. No parking areas shall be located within 20 feet of any residentially zoned property or within ten feet of any street line. Maximum height: No building or structure shall be erected or altered to a height exceeding seven stories or 80 feet, whichever is less. No lot coverage or floor area ratio is printed.

gulfport.name: City of Gulfport
gulfport.source: Code of Ordinances, Chapter 22 (Zoning), Article V (Schedule of District Regulations), §§ 22-5.01—22-5.16; Article VI (Supplementary Regulations for All Distric

equip.cite: § 22-6.03(a) Accessory uses and structures — general provisions [PDF p.771]
equip.text: In conjunction with a principal use, building or structure provided in this chapter, accessory uses, buildings or structures, as herein defined, may be located upon any lot, provided there is full compliance with all setback, height, building coverage, and off-street parking and loading requirements. No accessory building or structure, except commercial satellite dishes, as defined in Article XXII of this chapter, shall be located closer than twelve (12) feet to a principal building or structure, and no accessory building or structure shall be located closer than six (6) feet to any other accessory building or structure on the same lot. Home satellite dishes, as defined in Article XXII of this chapter, shall be exempt from the provisions of this section. Accessory uses, buildings, or structures may also be located within required yards, subject to the following limitations:.

No accessory use, building, or structure shall be located within the lot's front yard or within that portion of any side or rear yard subject to a special yard setback requirement. Accessory uses, buildings, and structures shall be located in rear or interior side yards. These shall not occupy any area subject to setback requirements. All other applicable regulations, such as but not limited to height restrictions, shall be complied with.

A swimming pool including patio and/or screen enclosure, shall be located a minimum distance of seven (7) feet from a rear property line, six (6) feet from a side property line on an interior lot, and twelve (12) feet from a side property line on a street side of a corner lot; provided however, that if the minimum setbacks are measured to the water's edge of the pool then a screen enclosure will not be allowed; and that a swimming pool shall be located a minimum distance of fifteen (15) feet from a seawall to the water's edge of the pool and a patio and/or screen enclosure shall be located a minimum distance of seven (7) feet from a seawall.

Other accessory buildings and structures shall be located a minimum distance of fifteen (15) feet from a rear property line, six (6) feet from a side property line on an interior lot, and twelve (12) feet from a side property line on the street side of a corner lot.

One (1) storage building, properly anchored and not exceeding eighty (80) square feet in area or eight (8) feet in height, may be located within a required rear or side yard of a residential lot; provided that a minimum distance of three (3) feet is maintained from a rear property line or a side property line on an interior lot, and a minimum distance of twelve (12) feet is maintained from a side property line on the street side of a corner lot.

Except as provided in subsection (1) above, no accessory structure shall be located upon a lot within fifteen (15) feet of any seawall; provided, however, that a dock, with or without hoist facility, may be constructed along a canal or waterway when authorized by law.

Whenever an accessory structure is attached in any manner to a principal building or structure, it shall cease to be considered an accessory structure for purposes of this chapter and shall be considered as a part of the principal building or structure. It shall be unlawful to attach an accessory structure to a principal building or structure which does not comply in all respects with the requirements of this chapter applicable to the principal building or structure.

equip.cite: § 22-6.02(a) Permitted yard encroachments [PDF p.770]
equip.text: Every part of a required yard shall be open and unobstructed from the ground to the sky except as hereinafter provided or as otherwise permitted by this chapter: (1) Sills or belt courses may project not over twelve (12) inches into a required yard; (2) Cornices, eaves, gutters, or movable awnings may project not over four (4) feet into a required yard; (3) Chimneys, fireplaces, or pilasters may project not over two (2) feet into a required yard; (4) Hoods, canopies, or marquees may project not over three (3) feet into a required yard, but shall not extend closer than one (1) foot to any lot line; (5) For residential uses, open front porches may extend into the required front yard setback by no more than twenty-five (25) percent of the required yard setback, without a variance. For purposes of this paragraph, an open porch shall be an unenclosed area which may have a pitched roof tied into the main structure; (6) Unless otherwise provided for in this or other sections of the zoning code, no encroachment shall be allowed outside of the property line.

equip.cite: § 22-6.02(b) Exclusions from height limits [PDF p.770]
equip.text: Utility penthouses, scenery lofts, cupolas, steeples and domes, not exceeding in gross area, measured at the maximum horizontal section thereof, thirty (30) percent of the roof area, and flag poles, airplane beacons, home antennas, as defined in Article XXII of this chapter, chimneys, stacks, tanks and roof structures used only for ornamental or mechanical purposes, may exceed the permissible height limit in any district by not more than twenty-five (25) percent. Parapet walls may extend not more than five (5) feet above the allowable height of a building.

equip.cite: § 22-2.02 Definitions — Accessory use or structure [PDF p.678]
equip.text: A use or structure of a nature customarily incidental and subordinate to the principal use or structure and, unless otherwise provided herein, on the same premises. 'On the same premises' with respect to accessory uses and structures shall be construed as meaning on the same lot or on a contiguous lot in the same ownership. Where a structure is attached to the principal structure by a breezeway, roofed passage, or otherwise, it shall be considered a part thereof, and not an accessory structure.

equip.cite: § 22-2.02 Definitions — Setback line [PDF p.690]
equip.text: The rear or inner edge of any required front, side or rear yard. Except as specifically provided by this chapter, no building, carport, garage, porch or other structure may be extended to occupy any portion of a lot beyond the required setback line.

equip.cite: § 22-6.01(c) Setback required from natural or man-made body of water [PDF p.768]
equip.text: The full extent of all required yards and setback areas shall be maintained landward from the mean high-water line of any natural or man-made body of water, irrespective of whether the parcel ownership involved may include all or part of said body of water; provided, that an exception may be applied as part of a marina or marina-associated structure.

equip.cite: § 22-6.01(d) Special yard requirement for a corner lot [PDF p.768]
equip.text: The narrow width of a corner lot shall determine its front for purposes of meeting the requirements of front and side yards. In case of reversed frontages, the determination of front and side yard depths may be made by the board of adjustment. The side yard setback on the secondary street shall be twelve (12) feet.

equip.cite: § 22-6.01(e) Special yard requirement for a double lot [PDF p.768]
equip.text: On a double frontage lot, the full front yard depth requirement shall also apply to the yard facing the secondary street wherever said yard adjoins or faces a lot having its principal frontage upon said secondary street; provided, however, that no setback shall be required along a secondary street which exceeds the established setback of a building upon said adjoining or facing lot.

equip.cite: § 22-6.01(b) Base building line requirements [PDF p.768]
equip.text: In order to provide for necessary street improvements and extensions to streets, certain base building lines may be established from time to time as part of the comprehensive plan. Where any base building line has been so established, all required setbacks shall be measured from said line, and in no case shall any part of a building, structure, parking area, or other site improvement of a permanent nature be constructed or extended streetward beyond said line.

OS (open space).frontNote: Minimum yard requirements and buffering. There are no specific requirements for this district.
OS (open space).sideNote: Minimum yard requirements and buffering. There are no specific requirements for this district.
OS (open space).rearNote: Minimum yard requirements and buffering. There are no specific requirements for this district.
OS (open space).note: Minimum lot requirements: 'There are no specific requirements for this district.' Minimum green space: 'No use shall exceed in impervious surface ratio (ISR) of 0.60.' Maximum building or structure coverage: 'shall not exceed a floor area ratio (FAR) of 0.25.'

R-1A (single-family residential).note: Minimum green space shall be no less than twenty (20) percent. 'No building shall have more than two (2) stories of living area.' Section heading is printed as 'R-IA' in this supplement; the chapter table of contents and text style it R-1A.

R-1 (single-family dwelling lots).note: Residential use shall have a minimum green space of twenty (20) percent. 'No building shall have more than two (2) stories of living area.'

R-1 (all other uses).coverageNote: Nonresidential use shall not exceed a floor area ratio (FAR) as provided in the comprehensive plan.
R-1 (all other uses).note: Nonresidential use shall have an impervious surface ratio (ISR) as provided in the comprehensive plan. 'No building shall have more than two (2) stories of living area.' The comprehensive plan FAR/ISR figures are not printed in the zoning chapter.

R-2 (single-family dwelling lots).note: Residential use shall have a minimum green space of twenty (20) percent. 'No building shall have more than two (2) stories of living area.'

R-2 (duplex dwelling lots).note: Residential use shall have a minimum green space of twenty (20) percent. 'No building shall have more than two (2) stories of living area.'

R-3 (duplex dwellings).note: Residential use shall have a minimum green space of twenty (20) percent. 'No building shall have more than two (2) stories of living area.'

Residential use minimum green space twenty (20) percent. Multiple-family dwellings are subject to site plan review under articles VII and VIII.

R-3 (townhouse dwelling complexes).minLotNote: Townhouse dwelling complexes shall have a gross lot area of two (2) acres, and gross lot width of two hundred forty (240) feet.
R-3 (townhouse dwelling complexes).note: Yard, height and coverage shown are the § 22-5.05(h) figures for 'all uses, except multiple-family'. § 22-6.04 separately prints, for townhouse development in any district: minimum lot area 1,800 square feet of usable land and minimum width 20 feet per townhouse dwelling; front yard minimum depth 25 feet and rear yard minimum depth 20 feet.

R-3 (all other uses).heightNote: All other uses shall not exceed a maximum building height of thirty (30) feet, unless authorized up to forty-five (45) feet as a conditional use herein.
R-3 (all other uses).coverageNote: Nonresidential use shall not exceed a floor area ratio (FAR) as provided in the comprehensive plan.
R-3 (all other uses).note: Nonresidential use shall not exceed an impervious surface ratio (ISR) as provided in the comprehensive plan.

equip.text: There shall be a five-foot setback from all apparatus of the utility system. It shall be a violation of this rule to allow, plant or place anything which will obstruct city staff from maintaining the city system within the setback. Violation of this rule shall be subject to section 1-11 of the city Code.

There shall be a five-foot setback radius around all utility structures, such as, but not limited to, meter boxes, valves, utility poles, lift stations, etc. No plants, trees, barriers or coverings, or anything shall be placed within the five-foot radius.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 5.6.A.6 (opening clause) [PDF p. 239]
equip.text: 6. Setback encroachments for uses and structures other than sheds. No accessory use or structure shall be located in any required front yard or in any required side or rear yard except as provided for below:.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 5.6.A.6.a [PDF p. 239]
equip.text: a. Accessory structures may be located no closer than five feet from the rear property line.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 5.6.A.6.b [PDF p. 239]
equip.text: b. Air conditioner compressors may extend three and one-half feet into a required yard. In no case should this encroachment exceed 50 percent of the required setback.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 5.6.A.6.c [PDF p. 239]
equip.text: c. Roof overhangs may extend three feet into a required yard. In no case should this encroachment exceed 50 percent of the required setback.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 5.6.A.6.d [PDF p. 239]
equip.text: d. Structures which are not enclosed by walls or roofs may be allowed in any required side or rear yards as long as a minimum distance of five feet from the lot line is maintained, except that driveways, concrete pads, sidewalks, etc. may be closer than five feet from the lot line if the chief building official determines that proper drainage can be maintained.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 5.6.A.6.e [PDF p. 239]
equip.text: e. In all residential districts, the height of accessory structures shall not exceed 15 feet.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 5.6.A.4 [PDF p. 239]
equip.text: 4. Unless otherwise expressly permitted in this section, any structure with a hard roof is required to meet the principal building setbacks for the respective zoning district.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 5.6.A.5 [PDF p. 239]
equip.text: 5. All accessory structures require the issuance of building permits by the city building department.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 5.6.A, 'In general' [PDF p. 237]
equip.text: In general. Accessory structures and uses are permitted in conjunction with any principal use, provided that they are recognized as clearly incidental and subordinate to the principal use and do not alter the characteristics of the lots. Regulations under this section shall apply to all zoning districts and to all buildings, structures, and uses of land or water in all zoning districts except as may otherwise be provided in the following regulations:.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 5.6.A.1-3 [PDF p. 237]
equip.text: 1. No accessory structure or use shall be permitted on any lot which does not have an existing or permitted principal use or structure. 2. All accessory structures are required to be located on the same lot as the principal structure or use. 3. No accessory structure or use shall be permitted in any platted easement, unless otherwise specifically permitted by the easement dedication. Fences may be located within certain easements with the condition that if the fence is required to be removed as a result of the existing easement, the property owner is solely responsible for replacement of the fence.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 5.6.A.11, Prohibited accessory structures [PDF p. 253]
equip.text: 11. Prohibited accessory structures. Accessory structures shall be of the same building material, color, shape and dimension as the principal structure on the same property, unless the city manager or designee approves a variation.... All accessory structures, including sheds, located on a corner lot must be positioned behind the front plane of the principal structure on the adjacent lot(s).

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 2.2, definition 5 [PDF p. 114]
equip.text: 5. Accessory use or structure means any use or detached structure customarily incidental and subordinate to the principal use or structure and located on the same lot with such principal use or structure.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 2.2, definition 207 [PDF p. 137]
equip.text: 207. Structure means anything constructed or erected which requires fixed location on the ground or attached to something having a fixed location on the ground. The word "structure" shall include the word "building." However, the word "uncovered" includes the word "screened", pool decks and patios, sidewalks, decorative trellises which are open on three sides, and other non-enclosed outdoor use areas.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 2.2, definition 235 [PDF p. 139]
equip.text: 235. Yard means a required open space area which shall not be occupied or obstructed by a structure or portion thereof except as otherwise permitted in this Code.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 5.5, Figure 2 footnotes [PDF p. 231]
equip.text: All waterfront yards shall meet the requirements set forth for front yards. Riverfront properties shall have a setback of 50 feet from the bulkhead line to the principal building. In all residential districts, the height of accessory structures shall not exceed 15 feet.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 5.6.N.1, Swimming pools [PDF p. 259]
equip.text: 1. Location. Swimming pools shall be located only in areas permitting the principal building and accessory structures and shall meet the yard and setback requirements for the principal building if such pool is constructed within the permitted building area, and shall meet the yard and setback requirements for accessory structures if constructed in the rear yard. Pools decks and patios may extend into the side or rear yards, provided a minimum of five feet from the lot lines is retained.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 5.8 (special uses), Public utility stations [PDF p. 281]
equip.text: 7. Public utility stations. A special use may be granted under the following conditions: a. All equipment shall be contained in an enclosed building or within a walled or fenced-in area that is 75 percent opaque.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 7.5 [PDF p. 373]
equip.text: [8] The operation of compressors, generators, or other noise-generating equipment associated with MRE when parked or stored on residential premises is prohibited.

equip.cite: Code of Ordinances Sec. 10-33(12) [PDF p. 581]
equip.text: (12) Portable mechanical equipment. It shall be a violation of this section to use or operate any power tools or portable mechanical equipment, including a power saw, sander, drill, grinder, lawn or garden tool, or similar device, when used outdoors in residential areas between the hours of 8:00 p.m. of one day and 7:00 a.m. of the next day so as to cause a noise disturbance that is plainly audible across a real property line of any residential zoning district or residential area, except when emergency repairs are made to public utilities or to private property to prevent immediate threats to the health, safety and welfare of the public, occupants or owner of private property.

equip.cite: Code of Ordinances Sec. 10-34(9), Exempt noises [PDF pp. 583-584]
equip.text: (9) Noise generated by air conditioners when functioning in accord with the manufacturer's standard mufflers and noise reducing equipment in use and in proper operating condition according to the standards promulgated by the American Refrigeration Institute.

equip.text: (g) Mechanical equipment. Mechanical equipment shall not be placed in required side Setbacks or Yards.

equip.cite: § 21-1 Definitions — Mechanical Equipment [PDF p. 705]
equip.text: Mechanical Equipment includes but is not limited to air conditioning compressors and condensers, heating-ventilation equipment, electrical transformers, and pool or spa equipment, ground-mounted or on pads.

equip.cite: § 21-1 Definitions — Yard [PDF p. 708]
equip.text: Yard means the open space required adjacent to Lot Lines for the control of the Density of Building. Such Yards shall be unobstructed from the ground to the sky except as otherwise provided in this chapter.

equip.cite: § 21-1 Definitions — Setback [PDF p. 707]
equip.text: Setback means the minimum horizontal distance between the street line and the front line of the Building, or between the Bulkhead, Seawall or other established line and the Building, or between the side Lot Lines and the Building or any projection, except as otherwise provided in this chapter.

equip.cite: § 21-1 Definitions — Accessory Building / Structure [PDF pp. 701, 708]
equip.text: Accessory Building means a subordinate Building or outbuilding, or a portion of the main Building, which is located on the same Lot or which is on a contiguous Lot, the use of which is clearly incidental to the use of the main Building.... Structure means anything constructed or erected, the use of which requires more or less permanent location on the land, or attached to something having a permanent location on the land.

equip.cite: § 21-353(a) Setbacks generally [PDF p. 776]
equip.text: (a) No Building or parts or projections of Buildings shall encroach on Setback or Yard areas, nor shall the density of population be increased in any manner, except in conformity with the regulations established under section 21-354.

equip.cite: § 21-355 Accessory Buildings [PDF p. 779]
equip.text: (a) Unless specifically permitted in the district regulations, Accessory Buildings shall not occupy in aggregate more than 20 percent of the maximum Lot area. (b) No Accessory Building, including Cabanas, shall be constructed except concurrently with or subsequent to the construction of the main Building.

equip.cite: § 21-351 Compliance with district regulations [PDF p. 775]
equip.text: In all zoning districts as listed and designated in section 21-76, no Building or land shall be used and no Building shall be erected, constructed, reconstructed or structurally altered which is designed, arranged or intended to be used or occupied for any other purpose than the classification and requirements as listed under each zoning district.

equip.cite: § 5.5-5(1)f and (2)f Appearance Code — screening of Mechanical Equipment [PDF p. 292]
equip.text: f. Mechanical Equipment and Utility Hardware on roofs, ground or buildings shall be screened from public view with materials harmonious with the building, or shall be located so as not to be visible from streets, Waterways, service alleys, and adjoining properties. Screening shall be of such material and color so that it matches or blends with the existing roof or portion above the top floor where it is installed. This provision shall not be interpreted to require screening of Mechanical Equipment and Utility Hardware from adjoining buildings that exceed the height of the rooftop upon which the Mechanical Equipment and Utility Hardware is installed. In such instance, only screening to the maximum height of the equipment or hardware is required. [Chapter 5.5 is applicable throughout all zoning districts within the Village except in the Business (B) District — § 5.5-4(a).]

equip.cite: § 5.5-2 Appearance Code Definitions — Mechanical Equipment / Utilitarian Structure / Utility Hardware [PDF p. 290]
equip.text: Mechanical Equipment shall mean equipment, devices and accessories, the use of which relates to water supply, drainage, heating, ventilating, air conditioning and similar purposes.... Utilitarian Structure. A structure or enclosure relating to mechanical or electrical services to a building or development.... Utility Hardware shall mean devices such as poles, crossarms, transformers and vaults, gas pressure regulating assemblies, hydrants and buffalo boxes that are used for water, gas, oil, sewer and electrical services to a building or a project.

equip.cite: § 21-322(d)(1)g Site plan review — ARB criteria, B Business District [PDF p. 766]
equip.text: g. Mechanical Equipment and Utility Hardware on roofs, ground or buildings shall be screened from public view with materials harmonious with the building, or shall be located so as not to be visible from streets, Waterways, service alleys, and adjoining properties. Screening shall be of such material and color so that it matches or blends with the existing roof or portion above the top floor where it is installed. This provision shall not be interpreted to require screening of Mechanical Equipment and Utility Hardware from adjoining buildings that may exceed the height of the rooftop upon which the Mechanical Equipment or Utility Hardware is installed. In this instance, only screening to the maximum height of the equipment or hardware is required.

equip.cite: § 21-293(a), (c) OF Ocean Front — roof Mechanical Equipment [PDF p. 747]
equip.text: (a) The maximum Height of a flat roof deck or the midpoint of a sloped roof of any Principal Building or Structure, other than decorative architectural roof features, Mechanical Equipment or Rooms, elevator equipment Rooms, water storage facilities, air conditioning equipment, accessory recreational facilities, fences, wall and similar facilities (non-habitable roof features) shall be 275 feet above the average Street Grade (or Bridge Lot Street Grade if applicable) adjoining the Property. Non-habitable roof features may extend above the height of the Building by no more than 25 feet.... (c) Roof Structures designed and utilized for the housing of Mechanical Equipment such as elevators, water storage, air conditioning and similar facilities shall not be considered in calculating the number of Stories, provided: (1) The Structure is fully enclosed or screened and does not exceed 25 feet in Height. (2) The outside walls of the roof Structure are set back a minimum of 20 feet from the exterior walls of the principal Structure. (3) No Guest Rooms, dwelling units, business establishments or other accommodations or public spaces, are contained within this Structure.

equip.cite: § 21-361(a) Utility lines and connections [PDF p. 783]
equip.text: (a) In all zoning districts, the electric and telephone wires from all utility easements shall be run underground only.

equip.cite: § 21-299(c)(3) PD Planned Development — Utilities [PDF p. 752]
equip.text: Facilities for utilities including, but not limited to, power and light, cable television, telephone, water, sewer and gas utilities, shall be constructed and installed underground. This subsection shall not prohibit the erection on the ground or flush with the ground of transformers, or other similar on-the-ground facilities normally used with and as a part of an underground distribution system.

equip.cite: § 21-358(f) Walls, fences and landscape plantings [PDF p. 781]
equip.text: (f) In all zoning districts, ornamental entrances, fountains, rotisseries, flower bins and similar architectural features exceeding the wall height restriction will be permitted, provided that: (1) No such feature shall exceed in height the wall height restriction for that district plus three feet. (2) There shall be only one such feature in any front, side or rear Yard, except that there may be two entrance gates. (3) There shall be at least ten feet between any such feature and any part of any Building on the same Lot, measured at right angles from the feature. (4) Such features shall not restrict passage through front, rear or side Yards to less than 88 inches in any place.

equip.cite: § 21-358(a)-(d) wall and fence heights [PDF p. 780]
equip.text: (a) In the Single Family Residential Districts (R Districts), Private Club District (PC District) and the Multiple Family Residential Districts (RM Districts), no wall or fence shall be erected outside of the Building Lines which is higher than five feet above the elevation of the centerline of the adjoining Street.... (b) In Blocks 1 and 12 in zoning districts R-1 and RM-4, and in Block 12a of RM-5, no wall or fence more than four feet in height shall be created between the Seawall and the front Setback line. (c) In the Ocean Front District (OF District), no boundary wall or fence shall be constructed which is more than six feet above the elevation of the center of the adjoining Street. (d) In the Business District (B District), no boundary wall or fence shall be constructed which is more than 20 feet above the elevation of the center of the adjoining Street along Bal Bay, Bal Cross and Park Drive and no more than six feet above the elevation of the center of the adjoining Street along Collins/Bal Harbour Boulevard, Harding and 96th Street. No other wall or fence shall be constructed which is more than six feet above the elevation of the center of any adjoining Street.

R-1 Single Family Residential.sideNote: The minimum side Setback shall be ten feet for a single-story construction up to 18 feet of Structure Height. For every additional foot in Height above 18 feet, there shall be one additional foot of side Setback for that portion of the building over 18 feet in height.
R-1 Single Family Residential.note: the 15-foot figure is the rear line, which the code states is the line abutting the Street. § 21-102(b): garages and Accessory Quarters may be built as part of the residence; if a wall is erected along the rear line of the Lot (outside face of such wall not nearer than ten feet to the street line), garages and Accessory Quarters not more than one Story in height may be constructed as part of or abutting such wall.

R-2 Single Family Residential.sideNote: The minimum side Setback shall be ten feet for single-story construction up to 18 feet of structure Height. For every additional foot in Height above 18 feet, there shall be one additional foot of side Setback for that portion of the building over 18 feet in height.
R-2 Single Family Residential.rearNote: No Building or any part thereof may be erected in the R-2 Single Family Residential District beyond the front Setback lines of 30 feet as shown on the recorded plat of the Residential Section of Bal Harbour, or nearer than 15 feet to the rear Lot Lines.
R-2 Single Family Residential.note: Height § 21-125: "shall not exceed two stories in Height and shall not exceed 30 feet in Height." Coverage § 21-129: maximum Lot Coverage shall not exceed 50 percent of Lot area; maximum Lot Coverage by buildings and structures shall not exceed 40 percent; combined total not to exceed 50 percent; with Accessory Quarters a bonus of 3% (43% buildings and structures / 53% total).

PC Private Club (single-family residenti.note: § 21-146.1(a): "Where land in the PC Private Club District is used for R-1 Single-Family Residential District uses, the standards for development including, but not limited to, maximum density, maximum building height, minimum floor area, setbacks, and maximum Lot coverage shall be those standards as set forth in sections 21-99 through 21-103, inclusive, relating to the R-1 Single-Family Residential District.

PC Private Club (Private Recreation Faci.note: § 21-146.1(b)(1): "The principal Building(s) or any part thereof shall be set back a minimum of (a) 100 feet from the front Lot Line; (b) 50 feet from each side Lot Line.

§ 21-146.1(b)(1): "All Buildings and Structures other than principal Building(s), including swimming pools and tennis courts, or any part thereof shall be set back a minimum of (a) 25 feet from the front Lot Line; (b) 25 feet from each side Lot Line; and (c) 25 feet from the rear Lot Line or the Erosion Control Line, whichever is greater." This is the PC row that would govern a detached accessory structure.

RM-1 Multiple Family Residential.frontNote: No Building or any part thereof may be erected in the RM-1 Multiple Family Residential District beyond the front Setback lines as shown on the recorded plat of the Residential Section of Bal Harbour, or nearer than ten feet to the side or rear lines.
RM-1 Multiple Family Residential.note: No numeric front setback is printed — the front Setback lines are those shown on the recorded plat. Height § 21-170: "shall not exceed two Stories in Height and shall not exceed 30 feet in height." Density § 21-169: not more than eight dwelling units per platted Lot. Minimum floor area § 21-171: not less than 600 square feet per Apartment Unit, and not less than 1,800 square feet in a Single-Family Dwelling.

RM-2 Multiple Family Residential.frontNote: No Building or any part thereof may be erected in the RM-2 Multiple Family Residential District beyond the front Setback lines as shown on the recorded plat of the Residential Section of Bal Harbour, or nearer than ten feet to the side or rear lines.
RM-2 Multiple Family Residential.note: No numeric front setback is printed. Height § 21-195: "shall not exceed two Stories in Height and shall not exceed 30 feet in height." Density § 21-194: not more than ten dwelling units per platted Lot. Minimum floor area § 21-196: not less than 600 square feet per Apartment Unit, and not less than 1,800 square feet in a Single-Family Dwelling. § 21-193 prints no numeric minimum lot area, lot width or yards.

RM-3 Multiple Family Residential.frontNote: No Building or any part thereof may be erected in the RM-3 Multiple Family Residential District beyond the front Setback lines as shown on the recorded plat of the Residential Section of Bal Harbour, or nearer than ten feet to the side or rear lines.
RM-3 Multiple Family Residential.note: No numeric front setback is printed. Height § 21-215: "shall not exceed two Stories in Height and shall not exceed 30 feet in height." Density § 21-214: not more than 12 dwelling units per platted Lot. Minimum floor area § 21-216: not less than 600 square feet per Apartment Unit, and not less than 1,800 square feet in a Single-Family Dwelling. § 21-213 prints no numeric minimum lot area, lot width or yards.

RM-4 Multiple Family Residential.note: § 21-242: "No Building or any part thereof, except a second or third story balcony overhang of four feet, may be erected on Lots in the RM-4 Multiple Family Residential District nearer to the front line, which is the waterfront, than 40 feet, or nearer to the side lines or to the rear or street line than ten feet, as shown on the recorded plat of the Residential Section of Bal Harbour." The front line is expressly the waterfront.

RM-5 Multiple Family Residential.note: § 21-267: "No Building or any part thereof, except a second and third story balcony overhang of four feet, may be erected in the RM-5 Multiple Family Residential District nearer to the front line, which is Bal Harbour Boulevard, than 50 feet, or as otherwise shown on the recorded plats of the Residential Section of Bal Harbour, and Resubdivision of Lot 21, Block 12 and Tract F of the Residential Section of Bal Harbour, or nearer to the side lines than 25 feet, or nearer to the rear lines than 50 feet, except that one-story garages and one or two-story Accessory Quarters may be erected within the rear 30 feet of the Lot, but not nearer than five feet to the side or rear lines.

OF Ocean Front.frontNote: All Buildings and Structures, except for fully enclosed Parking Structures as allowed in section 21-288 of this article, of 17 Stories or less shall be set back a minimum of 150 feet from the right-of-way of Collins Avenue. Each Story above the 17th Story shall be set back an additional 25 feet from the Story below; i.e., 18 Stories, 175-foot Setback; 19 Stories, 200-foot Setback; etc.
OF Ocean Front.sideNote: All Principal Buildings and Structures shall maintain a minimum side Setback from each side Lot Line equal to 25 percent of the Street frontage of the Lot.... Side Setbacks shall be equal, except that Lots over 250 feet in width may have unequal side Setbacks, provided, however, that not less than a 50 foot side Setback shall be provided for Lots equal to or more than 250 feet in width.
OF Ocean Front.rearNote: No Building or Structure of any kind, except Cabanas not greater in Height than ten feet above the finished Grade, shall be erected or maintained on any Lot beyond the east Setback line as shown on the recorded plats of the Ocean Front Section of Bay Harbor and the Bal Harbour Ocean Front Addition.
OF Ocean Front.note: § 21-291 also prints: Bulkhead — "No Building or Structure of any kind, except those necessary for the control of beach erosion, shall be built east of the existing Bulkhead"; Erosion Control Line — "No Building or Structure of any kind shall be erected or constructed within 55 feet west of the Erosion Control Line".

PD Planned Development.frontNote: Required perimeter Building Setback. No Building shall be located closer than 100 feet to Collins Avenue, or closer than 25 feet to any other perimeter Property line of a PD. The perimeter Building Setback shall be landscaped to the standards of, and maintained as required by, subsection 21-292.
PD Planned Development.note: PD is an optional rezoning available only to OF Ocean Front District properties containing four or more contiguous acres (§ 21-299(a)). § 21-299(g)(1): "Subject to final PD site plan approval, Building Setbacks may be modified from the provisions of the underlying OF Ocean Front District.

B Business.frontNote: (1) Front Yard Setback. The following front Yard Setbacks shall be maintained: a. From Collins/Bal Harbour Boulevard and Harding Avenues: 1. 50 feet for Buildings occupied and used for the sale of merchandise or services at retail. 2. 100 feet for Parking Structures and all other Structures. b. From 96th Street: 7.5 feet for all Buildings, Parking Structures and all other Structures. c.
B Business.note: § 21-319(a)(2): "There shall be interior, side and rear Yards having a width of not less than seven feet six inches on each side of a Building or Structure, including Parking Structures." § 21-319(a)(3): "There shall be a waterfront Setback of 40 feet, as measured from the outside face of the Seawall." Height § 21-318: "no Building or Structure in the B Business District shall exceed 56 feet or three Stories in Height, whichever is less.

P Off-Street Parking.note: § 21-336 prints permitted uses only ("parks, playgrounds, municipal buildings, and Parking Lots owned and operated by the Village") and § 21-337 the boundary. No setback, height, lot area, lot width or coverage standards are printed for this district.

oldsmar.name: City of Oldsmar
oldsmar.source: Code of Ordinances, Part III Land Development Code, Article V (Zoning Regulations) §§ 5.1—5.9; Part IV Town Center Development Code, Article III (Land Use and Z

equip.cite: LDC § 5.1.4, Setbacks [PDF p. 806-807]
equip.text: Setbacks shall be measured as the minimum distance, as established in each zoning district in this section, running from the property line to the building line. For purposes of this measurement the building line shall be considered as the solid vertical wall of the building. The following conditions shall also apply to the measurement of setbacks: 1. Projections shall not extend farther than three feet into a required yard or setback area. 2. Wing walls shall conform to the normal setback requirements whenever they exceed the allowable height of a fence. 3. For determination and measurement of setbacks, corner lots, double frontage lots and through lots shall be considered to have two front yards, one on each street.

equip.cite: LDC § 5.1.6, Yards [PDF p. 807-808]
equip.text: The minimum setback distances as established by this section shall be considered to be the minimum yard areas for front, side, and rear yards. Said setback yards shall be open spaces, being unoccupied and unobstructed from the ground upward, with the exception of trees and other natural vegetation, as well as meeting the following: 1. Sills, eaves, cornices, chimneys, and flues may project into a setback area not more than three feet. 2. No portion of an alley shall be considered as a part of a required setback. 3. All residential structures containing less than four dwelling units, and their accessory structures on waterfront lots or parcels, shall be set back a minimum of 25 feet from the mean high-water mark.... 4. In all residential districts no structure shall be permitted, except building additions to the principal building, within the front yard area, not to extend beyond the front setback line. 5. In all residential districts swimming pools must maintain a minimum rear yard setback of five feet from the pool cage, decking or paving to the property line, and eight feet from the edge of pool water to the property line. A minimum side yard setback of five feet is also required.

equip.cite: LDC § 5.1.9, Location of accessory structures and uses in residential districts [PDF p. 809-810]
equip.text: 1. A detached accessory structure shall not be closer than five feet to the main structure, nor closer than five feet to any other accessory structure on the same lot or parcel, except as may be permitted in the R-6 zoning district. In all residential districts, a detached accessory structure shall not be closer than five feet to any property line on the lot. 2. In all residential districts no detached accessory structure shall be located in the front yard of a lot or parcel.

equip.cite: LDC § 5.1.10, Utility stations [PDF p. 810]
equip.text: In residential areas all utility stations shall be fenced or enclosed within a structure, and no part of any structure (or fence) shall be less than 22 feet from a property line of an abutting street, lot, or parcel.

equip.cite: LDC § 5.1.5, Setbacks at railroad tracks [PDF p. 807]
equip.text: Wherever a side or rear lot line in a C-3, L-1, M-1, IPD or MUPD district abuts a railroad right-of-way, a railroad siding track or a railroad easement, the side and rear setback requirements will not apply at the abutting side or rear line and construction of buildings will be permitted up to the abutting side or rear property line.

equip.cite: LDC Art. II, Definitions — Accessory structure [PDF p. 616]
equip.text: Accessory structure. A structure which a is subordinate to and serves a principal building b is subordinate in area, extent, and purpose to the principal building served c contributes to the comfort, convenience or necessities of the users or occupants of the principal building and d is located on the same lot as the principal building. Accessory structures shall not be used for human habitation, and be designed to have minimal flood [damage potential].

equip.cite: LDC § 5.1.7, Fences or walls [PDF p. 808]
equip.text: In any district, no fence, wall, or other obstruction shall be erected or maintained at a corner within 15 feet from the intersection of the right-of-way lines. No fences shall be erected within two feet of the back of public sidewalks. Fences or walls beyond the front building line and extending across the principal front yard in residential districts shall be limited to a maximum height of three and one-half feet.... Rear and side yard fences shall not exceed a height of six feet.... 4. Easements and rights-of-way. No fence or wall may be located within any easement or right-of-way or enclose any water meter box or manhole without approval by the public works director... 5. The fence will maintain at least two feet separation from any water line, sewer pipe, sewer line, or other drainage or utility structure.

equip.cite: LDC § 5.1.8, Height and bulk [PDF p. 809]
equip.text: Chimneys, water, fire, radio, television and cellular telephone towers, smokestacks, flagpoles and similar structures and their necessary mechanical appurtenances may be erected above the height limits herein established; however, the heights of these structures or appurtenances thereto shall not exceed the height limitations prescribed by the Federal Aviation Agency within the flight approach zone patterns of airports.

equip.cite: LDC § 5.1.12, Multiple use of required open space prohibited [PDF p. 810]
equip.text: No part of a required yard or other required open space, required off-street parking, or off-street loading space, provided in connection with one building, structure, or use, shall be included as meeting the requirements for any other building, structure, or use, except where specific provision is made in this Code.

equip.cite: TCDC § 3.3.7, Accessory structures within the Town Center Residential and Town Center Boulevard Districts [PDF p. 1363]
equip.text: 1. Accessory structures shall not be located within the front setback. All accessory structures shall maintain a five foot side and rear setback unless expressly permitted in this Code. 2. No accessory structure that can provide storage, such as a shed or detached garage, shall be closer than five feet to the principal structure or another accessory structure capable of storage. 3. Swimming pools must maintain a minimum rear yard setback of five feet from the pool cage, decking or paving to the property line, and eight feet from the edge of pool water to the property line. A minimum side yard setback of five feet is also required. 4. Fences shall not be considered accessory structures.

equip.cite: TCDC § 5.2.6, Underground utilities [PDF p. 1389]
equip.text: All on-site utilities, including individual distribution lines for electric, cable and telephone, shall be installed underground.

equip.cite: LDC Appendix 3, Tampa Road Corridor Plan, Sec. 3 — Mechanical equipment/On-site utilities [PDF p. 1287-1288]
equip.text: All mechanical equipment, including elevator equipment, shall be integrated into the site design and screened from view of Tampa Road, side street, and adjacent properties. Mechanical equipment located on the roof must also be screened from view from Tampa Road. To limit visual clutter and interference of landscaping, all on-site utilities shall be installed underground. Acceptable: Behind the front of the building and screened from adjacent properties. Located on the roof behind parapet walls or other decorative features.... Screening includes walls, fences, berms, and landscaping.... Screening material and color shall be compatible with the overall building design and colors. Individual distribution lines for electric, cable, telephone, shall be installed underground. Electrical wiring for accessory structures shall be underground. Not acceptable: Unscreened mechanical equipment. Mechanical equipment in front of building. Lattice work. Utilities installed above ground. Electrical wiring or decorative strings connecting accessory structures.

equip.cite: LDC Appendix 3, Tampa Road Corridor Plan, Sec. 3 — service station site requirements [PDF p. 1291]
equip.text: Air, vacuums, and like automotive mechanical equipment shall be located behind the principal building. Landscaping or decorative wall shall be placed around equipment that is visible from Tampa Road and/or the side street.

equip.cite: TCDC Appendix A, Architectural and Design Pattern Book, Sec. 7 [PDF p. 1441]
equip.text: Window/wall mounted air conditioning units should not be placed in street-facing windows or walls unless no alternative exists. Exterior supports or brackets should not be used. All roof mounted equipment, including telecommunications, ventilation, elevator and alternative energy, shall be screened from view of adjacent right-of-way. Swimming pools and spas shall be located to the side or rear of the property.... Solar collectors, if utilized, should be located on the roof. Placement to the rear or sides of the structure is permissible.

equip.cite: LDC § 5.5.3.2(18)(d), C-2 brewpubs (same text at § 5.7.4.2(12)(4) C-3 microbreweries, § 5.7.6.2(20)(4) M-1 microbreweries, TCDC § 3.6.2(10)(d) TCCN and § 3.7.2(15)(d) TCCR) [PDF pp. 837, 853, 859, 1370, 1372]
equip.text: All mechanical equipment, visible from the street or adjacent to residential uses, shall be screened using architectural features consistent with the principal structure.

equip.cite: Code of Ordinances § 26-32, Construction noise [PDF p. 251]
equip.text: (a) No construction activities shall be permitted between the hours of 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m., Monday through Friday, 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 a.m. Saturdays, and all day Sunday. Construction equipment that must be operated near a residentially zoned area on a 24-hour per day basis (i.e. pumps, well tips, generators, etc.) shall be shielded by an acoustical enclosure during the hours of 6:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m.

PRE.note: Preservation district. Maximum area of impervious surface: 0.10 percent. Maximum floor area ratio (FAR): 0.10 percent. Public/semipublic uses shall not exceed a maximum area of three acres. No front/side/rear setbacks, lot area, lot width or lot depth are printed for this district.

CON.note: Conservation district. Maximum impervious surface ratio: 0.20 percent. Maximum floor area ratio (FAR): 0.10 percent. Public/semipublic uses shall not exceed a maximum area of three acres. No front/side/rear setbacks are printed for this district.

REC.note: Recreation/open space district. 'There shall be no minimum land area requirement for the recreation/open space district.' Maximum impervious surface ratio: 0.20 percent. Maximum floor area ratio (FAR): 0.20 percent. No front/side/rear setbacks, lot width or lot depth are printed for this district.

E-1.note: Estate residential. Maximum lot coverage: 40 percent (except as permitted for pools under section 5.4.1.8). Minimum floor area: 2,000 square feet. For residential pool construction, impervious surface area/total lot coverage may be permitted up to 60 percent. Nonresidential uses shall not exceed FAR 0.30 or ISR 0.60. Public/semipublic uses shall not exceed a maximum of three acres.

E-2.note: Estate residential. Maximum lot coverage: 45 percent (except as permitted for pools under section 5.4.2.8). Minimum floor area: 1,800 square feet. Pool construction may reach 60 percent impervious/total lot coverage. Nonresidential uses shall not exceed FAR 0.40 or ISR 0.65. Public/semipublic uses shall not exceed three acres.

R-1.note: Residential single-family. Code prints setbacks as 'Front: 25.0 feet. Side: 7.5 feet. Rear: 10.0 feet.' Maximum lot coverage: 50 percent (except as permitted for pools under section 5.4.3.8). Minimum floor area: 1,250 square feet. Pool construction may reach 65 percent ISR/total lot coverage. Nonresidential uses shall not exceed FAR 0.40 or ISR 0.65.

R-2.note: Residential single-family. Maximum lot coverage: 50 percent (except as permitted for pools under section 5.4.4.8). Minimum floor area: 1,250 square feet. Pool construction shall not exceed 65 percent impervious/total lot coverage. Nonresidential uses shall not exceed FAR 0.40 or ISR 0.65.

R-3.note: Residential two- and three-family. No minimum lot area is printed for this district (only lot width and lot depth). Maximum impervious surface ratio (ISR): 0.35 percent. Maximum floor area ratio (FAR): 0.30 percent. Single-family dwellings permitted consistent with the R-2 zoning standards.

RM-15 (multifamily dwelling structures).note: Residential multifamily (townhouse or garden type). No minimum lot area is printed. Maximum ISR: 0.50 percent. Maximum FAR: 0.40 percent. Residential equivalent use shall not exceed 3.0 beds per permitted dwelling unit at 15.0 units per acre. Public/semipublic uses shall not exceed three acres.

RM-15 (two- and three-family dwelling st.note: Same district-wide lot and intensity standards as RM-15 multifamily; only the yard regulations differ (§ 5.4.6.8(2)).

RM-15 (all other structures).note: Yard regulations for 'All other structures' per § 5.4.6.8(3).

R-6 (mobile home development site).note: Residential mobile home, parks and subdivisions district. 'Each mobile home development site shall contain a minimum of 20 acres.' Site shall be a minimum of 150 feet wide at the building front setback line and a minimum of 200 feet in depth. Total structural coverage of the entire mobile home development shall not exceed 40 percent of the site area. Maximum building height is not printed for this district.

R-6 (mobile home lot or space).frontNote: Front setback shall be 15 feet from right-of-way line or utility easement in a mobile home subdivision, and 15 feet from the established property line in a mobile home park.
R-6 (mobile home lot or space).note: Each mobile home lot or space shall be at least 4,000 square feet in area and at least 40 feet wide where said lot abuts any public or private roadway or drive. Maximum density shall not exceed 7 1/2 mobile home units per gross acre. Each mobile home shall have a living area of at least 900 square feet.

CL-20.note: Congregate living facilities district, from the table at § 5.4.8.4. Maximum number of dwelling units per gross acre: 20 (maximum units shall be limited by the permitted density on the future land use map). Minimum lot area printed as '5 acres'. Maximum ISR: 0.65 percent; maximum FAR: 0.50 percent; minimum open space 35 percent.

CL-30.note: Congregate living facilities district, from the table at § 5.4.8.4. Maximum 30 dwelling units per gross acre (limited by permitted density on the future land use map). Minimum lot area printed as '5 acres'. 175 feet is printed as 'Minimum lot frontage'; 35 feet as 'Minimum side yard abutting a public road'.

R/O/R.note: Residential/office/retail district. Maximum ISR shall be 0.70 or, depending on use, to be consistent with and not to exceed ISR's in either the RM-15 or C-2 districts, whichever is most restrictive. Maximum FAR shall be 0.40 or, depending on use, consistent with RM-15 or C-2, whichever is most restrictive. Maximum one curb cut per 100 feet of frontage. Public/semipublic uses shall not exceed three acres.

C-1.note: Commercial neighborhood district. Maximum ISR: 0.60 percent. Maximum FAR: 0.30 percent. Public/semipublic uses shall not exceed a maximum area of five acres. Institutional conditional uses subject to a five-acre maximum.

C-2.note: Commercial general district. Maximum ISR: 0.70 percent. Maximum FAR: 0.45 percent. § 5.5.3.4: 'A 50-foot setback for all structures, including parking lots, will be required for any lands abutting residentially owned property.' Conditional retail major automobile repair requires at minimum a 20-foot side yard setback and a ten-foot landscape strip along all street frontages.

OF.note: Office general district. Maximum ISR: 0.50 percent. Maximum FAR: 0.40 percent. Public/semipublic uses shall not exceed three acres.

RO (nonresidential and multifamily).note: Residential office district. Code prints 'Side: Seven and one-half feet.' Lot standards at § 5.6.2.5.2 apply to non-residential and multi-family; § 5.6.2.5.1 states single-family development is 'consistent with the R-2 regulations.' Maximum ISR: 0.65 percent.
