RO (single-family).note: § 5.6.2.5.1 prints only 'Single-family development consistent with the R-2 regulations.' No separate numeric lot or setback standards are printed for single-family in the RO district.

C-3.note: Commercial wholesale and warehousing district. Yard regulations printed as 'Minimum front: 35 feet. Minimum side: 20 feet. Minimum rear: ten feet.' Maximum ISR: 0.80 percent. Maximum FAR: 0.45 percent. § 5.1.5: where a side or rear lot line in C-3 abuts a railroad right-of-way, siding track or easement, the side and rear setback requirements will not apply at that line.

L-1.note: Industrial light district. Code prints 'Area: 43,560 square feet. Width: 75 feet. Depth: 100 feet.' Maximum ISR: 0.80 percent. Maximum FAR: 0.55 percent. § 5.1.5 railroad exemption applies to side and rear lines abutting a railroad right-of-way, siding track or easement. Buffer yard I required between the industrial limited land use category and an adjoining residential land use classification.

M-1.note: Limited manufacturing district. Code prints 'Area: 12,000 square feet. Width: 75 feet. Depth: 100 feet.' Maximum ISR: 0.80 percent. Maximum FAR: 0.55 percent. § 5.1.5 railroad exemption applies. Buffer yard I required adjoining residential land use classifications. Ancillary non-industrial uses shall not exceed five acres.

PUB.note: Public/semipublic district. Maximum ISR: 0.80 percent. Maximum FAR: 0.60 percent. Ancillary non-residential/transportation-utility use shall not exceed a maximum of ten acres.

PUD.note: Planned unit development district (umbrella provisions for RPD, CPD, IPD, MUPD and PUD overlay). § 5.9.1.3.2: 'Any property proposed for development as a planned unit development shall not be less than ten acres.' No front, side, rear, height, coverage or lot dimensions are printed for the PUD district itself.

RPD (multifamily structures).frontNote: Front yard. A minimum of 30 feet from any public right-of-way line to any structure. For any private street lying in an RPD district, setback shall be 50 feet from the centerline of pavement.
RPD (multifamily structures).sideNote: Side yard. A minimum of 25 feet between structures and side lot lines, and for each story over one story an additional five feet between structures shall be required.
RPD (multifamily structures).rearNote: Rear yard. A minimum of 25 feet measured from the rear property line to any structure, and for each story over one story an additional five feet between structures shall be required.
RPD (multifamily structures).note: Residential planned development district. Perimeter: a minimum of 35 feet shall be maintained between the outside walls of all structures and the perimeter of the RPD district. Maximum building height 35 feet.

RPD (single-family detached structures).frontNote: Front yard. A minimum of 25 feet from any public right-of-way line to any structure. For any private street lying in an RPD district, setback shall be a minimum of 50 feet from the centerline of pavement.
RPD (single-family detached structures).sideNote: Side yard. A minimum of 7 1/2 feet measured from the side lot line to any structure. On side streets the minimum setback shall be 25 feet from any public rights-of-way, or 50 feet from the centerline of pavement for private streets. A minimum side setback of five feet is required.
RPD (single-family detached structures).rearNote: Rear yard. A minimum of 20 feet measured from the rear property line to any structure, except that swimming pool structures may be no closer to the rear property line than ten feet, with the distance measured from the edge of the pool cage, pool decking, or paving, to the property line, and a minimum of eight feet from the edge of the pool water.
RPD (single-family detached structures).note: Each lot shall contain a minimum of 7,500 square feet and shall be a minimum of 75 feet in width at the front building setback line and a minimum of 100 feet in depth. The trailing sentence of the side-yard rule ('A minimum side setback of five feet is required.') is printed as shown and appears in context to address pools; it is recorded verbatim rather than interpreted.

RPD (zero lot line single-family detache.sideNote: Side yards. Side yards shall be zero feet on one side and a minimum of 20 feet on the other side. Side yard of ten feet each side may be permitted provided 20 feet is maintained between structures. A minimum side setback of five feet is required for pools.
RPD (zero lot line single-family detache.rearNote: Rear yard. A minimum of 20 feet measured from the rear property line to any structure, except that swimming pool structures may be no closer to the rear property line than five feet, with the distance measured from the edge of the pool cage, pool decking, or paving, to the property line, and a minimum of eight feet from the edge of the pool water.
RPD (zero lot line single-family detache.note: A maintenance easement of five feet shall be designated on the adjacent lot abutting the zero lot line boundary and recorded on the plat; roofs or awnings shall not project into a maintenance easement. RPD (single-family attached).frontNote: Front yard, side yard and rear yard setbacks shall be identical to the setbacks for single-family detached structures.

RPD (single-family attached).rearNote: Front yard, side yard and rear yard setbacks shall be identical to the setbacks for single-family detached structures.
RPD (single-family attached).note: Each lot to be developed as a single-family attached unit shall contain a minimum of 5,000 square feet for each single-family unit occupying such lot or parcel. No separate lot width or depth is printed.

CPD.sideNote: All setbacks, yards and other requirements shall be determined during the concept development plan review process and shall, at a minimum, take into consideration appropriate open space around each building and separation for fire safety and adequate light and air considerations.

IPD.frontNote: Front: 50 feet from any arterial highway and collector street and 25 feet from any minor street, measured from any right-of-way line to a structure.

MUPD.frontNote: All setbacks, yards and other requirements may be established at the time of MUPD approval or alternatively, may be determined during the concept development plan review process and shall, at a minimum, take into consideration appropriate open space around each building and separation for fire safety and adequate light and air considerations.
MUPD.sideNote: All setbacks, yards and other requirements may be established at the time of MUPD approval or alternatively, may be determined during the concept development plan review process and shall, at a minimum, take into consideration appropriate open space around each building and separation for fire safety and adequate light and air considerations.
MUPD.rearNote: All setbacks, yards and other requirements may be established at the time of MUPD approval or alternatively, may be determined during the concept development plan review process and shall, at a minimum, take into consideration appropriate open space around each building and separation for fire safety and adequate light and air considerations.

TCR (two-family dwellings).note: No minimum lot area and no ISR are printed for the two-family variant.

equip.cite: Schedule F, § 4.0.B.1, Prohibited encroachments [PDF p. 1216]
equip.text: B. Prohibited encroachments. 1. No electrical, plumbing and mechanical equipment, dumpster or area specifically designated for garbage cans shall be located within a front yard or front yard setback.

equip.cite: Schedule F, § 2.0.D, Accessory buildings and structures [PDF p. 1213]
equip.text: D. Accessory buildings and structures. The following regulations apply to the construction of all accessory buildings and structures: 1. Accessory buildings and structures shall be designed to blend aesthetically with the main structure. Accessory buildings or structures equal to or greater than 200 square feet shall match the principal building in materials, color and architectural style. 2. Accessory buildings and structures are prohibited in front or side yards. Garages and carports greater than 200 square feet that comply with the applicable required district setbacks may be permitted in the side yard. 3. An accessory building or structure shall not be erected, constructed, or modified for residential purposes, unless specifically provided for in these land development regulations. 4. The total square footage of all accessory buildings shall not exceed the square footage or height of the principal building. 5. An accessory building or structure shall not be constructed or erected on a lot prior to the principal use that it serves.

equip.cite: Schedule F, § 2.0.G, Height exceptions [PDF p. 1214]
equip.text: G. Height exceptions. 1. Fire towers and water towers are excluded from the height requirements of these regulations. 2. Height requirements apply to buildings and do not apply to necessary mechanical appurtenances or structures which are not intended for occupancy by human beings unless such mechanical appurtenances or structures exceed 125' in SR-1AA, SR-1A, SR-1, SR-2, MR-1, MR-2, MR-3 and AG zoning districts or 200' in any other zoning district in which case conditional use approval shall be required.

equip.cite: Schedule F, § 4.0.A.2.e, Pool equipment [PDF p. 1215]
equip.text: e. Pool equipment. Pool equipment is prohibited and unlawful within the front yard of a lot. Pool equipment must be located a minimum of 5' off the property line and cannot be attached to a common fence separating an adjoining property. Pool equipment shall not be installed in drainage swales and designated drainage flows.

equip.cite: Schedule F, § 4.0.A.2.c, Easements [PDF p. 1215]
equip.text: c. Easements. Pools, pool decks, and pool equipment cannot be located within any easement.

equip.cite: Schedule F, § 4.0.A.5, Building projections [PDF p. 1216]
equip.text: 5. Building projections. Building projections may encroach into front, side and rear yards as follows: a. Sills or belt courses may project up to 12" into a yard. b. Awnings or canopies shall project a maximum of 4' from the building when located over pedestrian areas and no less than 2' otherwise. Awnings or canopies shall maintain a minimum clearance of 8' above any sidewalk or pedestrian route. c. Chimneys, fireplaces or pilasters may project up to 2' into a required yard. d. Projected or recessed covered public entry providing a minimum horizontal dimension of 8' and a minimum area of 100 square feet. e. Overhangs, maximum of 3'. f. Balconies may project a maximum of 2' into any required setback so long as the support structure for the balcony does not encroach into the setback.

equip.cite: Schedule C, footnote (1) [PDF p. 1141]
equip.text: (1) Accessory buildings are not permitted in required front yards or required side yards when such side yard abuts a street. Also, in addition to a building setback of four feet, all accessory buildings which are greater than 15 feet in height shall be set back an additional one foot from the side and rear parcel line for each foot or fractional portion thereof, of height over 15 feet.

equip.cite: Schedule D, § 4.0.B.1.d, Residential planned development (PD) [PDF p. 1151]
equip.text: d. All outdoor mechanical equipment, such as heating, air conditioning, ventilation systems, propane gas tanks, pool equipment and other similar appurtenances shall be located in rear yards on lots with lots less than 7.5 feet on side yard. They shall not be adjacent to the right-of-way whenever possible; if such appurtenances are visible from the right-of-way, they shall be visually screened.

equip.cite: Schedule E, § 16.0.C.7, Multiple-family housing design guidelines [PDF p. 1193]
equip.text: Mechanical equipment. All mechanical equipment, whether mounted on the roof or ground shall be screened from view. All screening devices shall be compatible with the architecture and color of the dwelling structures.

equip.cite: Schedule E, § 18.0.M, Townhouse development [PDF p. 1199]
equip.text: M. Mechanical equipment. All mechanical equipment, whether mounted on the roof or ground shall be screened from view. All screening devices shall be compatible with the architecture and color of the dwelling structures.

equip.cite: Schedule J, § 3.6, Screening of equipment [PDF p. 1275]
equip.text: Section 3.6. Screening of equipment. All nonresidential and multifamily dumpsters, recycling bins, trash/garbage areas, mechanical equipment located below the roofline, backflow preventers and electrical transformers shall be screened on a minimum of three sides. A. Screening material. A hedge or solid fence not to exceed six feet in height shall be used as a screening material. If landscape material is used, it shall be a minimum of 30 inches from the existing grade at the time of planting and maintained at the height of the device; in no case shall the landscape material exceed six feet. B. Mechanical equipment. Trees or shrubs shall be installed to shade mechanical equipment and aide in energy conservation. Landscape material shall be installed in such a manner that it does not interfere with the normal operations and maintenance of mechanical equipment. C. Residential air conditioners. Single and two-family residences and mobile homes shall install trees or shrubs to shade all exterior air-conditioning units located below the roofline of the structure.

equip.cite: Schedule S, § 9.0.C, Accessory structures and pool enclosures (historic districts) [PDF p. 1488]
equip.text: Accessory structures and pool enclosures. • Prefabricated accessory storage structures shall not exceed 100 square feet in area, and are subject to the setback requirements of the district. • There shall be a minimum separation of 10 feet between principal and accessory structures. • Accessory structures, such as garages, sheds, etc. shall not exceed the height of the main structure. • Accessory structures shall be of similar style, color, design and materials as used for the principal residence. • Air conditioning, mechanical equipment and other support equipment shall not be placed in a setback and must be screened from view.

equip.cite: Schedule S, § 9.0.C, New construction/commercial design (historic districts) [PDF p. 1476]
equip.text: • Mechanical units and their ancillary equipment shall not be visible from the right-of-way. • Mechanical equipment shall be integrated into the overall mass of a building by screening it behind parapets or by integrating equipment into roof forms. Plain boxes are not acceptable as screening devices.

equip.cite: Schedule U, § 3.0.N, Screening (Downtown/Riverfront/Midtown overlays) [PDF pp. 1538-1539]
equip.text: N. Screening. 1. Trash, recycling receptacles, loading docks, service areas, and other similar areas must be located in parking areas or in a location that is not visible from "pedestrian priority" and "A" street frontages, and must be screened to preclude visibility from adjacent streets. 2. Mechanical equipment at ground level shall be incorporated into the building and placed on the parking lot side of the building away from view from adjacent "pedestrian priority" and "A" street frontages. Loading docks, truck parking, outdoor storage, utility meters, HVAC equipment, trash dumpsters, trash compaction, and other service functions should be incorporated into the overall design of the building utilizing walls of a material compatible with the material, style, color, texture, pattern, trim, and details of the main building and landscaping. The wall shall be one foot higher than the largest object being screened, but not more than ten feet high, on all sides where access is not needed. All loading, service and trash collection shall be accessed from "B" streets. 3. All rooftop mechanical equipment shall be integrated into the overall mass of a building by screening it behind parapets or by recessing it into roof structure.

equip.cite: Schedule V, § 3.0.N, Service and utility areas [PDF pp. 1572-1573]
equip.text: N. Service and utility areas. Buildings require mechanical equipment and service areas that are normally unsightly and sometimes noisy. Utilities can be a visually dominant element in the landscape. These areas include, but are not limited to loading docks, exterior storage areas, dumpsters, and mechanical equipment such as plumbing vent stacks, HVAC transformers, fans and cooling towers.... 1. Locate all service and utility areas away from the street and concealed from building entrances, pedestrian areas, and adjacent residential structures.... 6. Utility service areas should be screened from public view with architectural materials and colors that are harmonious with the building; and/or with landscape plantings that can be incorporated as a part of visual screen. 7. Locate all above grade utility connections, vents, and other projections through exterior walls away from high visibility areas, such as front facades or pedestrian areas, preferably in the service area of the building. Do not locate any utility projections or equipment, such as air conditioning units or air exchangers on the street side of the building. 8. Rooftop mechanical equipment shall not be mounted on the buildings unless the roof itself acts as a screen or other integral architectural treatment is provided to screen such equipment from view.

equip.cite: Schedule J, § 3.4.A, Table A — land use compatibility setbacks [PDF p. 1274]
equip.text: Table A — Proposed Use / Abutting Use / Setback (In Feet) / Buffer (In Feet) / Visual Screen (Type): Multifamily abutting Single-Family — One-story buildings 50 / 25 / 1; Two or more stories 100 / 50 / 1. Commercial abutting Residential — ?50 / 25 / 1; 75 / 50 / 2. Industrial abutting Residential — 75 / 50 / 1; 100 / 75 / 1 or 2. B. Front yard buffer and visual screen requirements for proposed commercial and industrial uses. Front yards of commercial and/or industrial uses abutting residential uses shall provide a ten-foot buffer and a Type One or Type Two visual screen.

equip.cite: Sec. 38-61, Definitions — "Necessary business equipment" (noise ordinance, NOT a siting rule) [PDF p. 444]
equip.text: Necessary business equipment means equipment physically affixed, joined, or connected to the outside of a building, and without which a business located inside the building would not be able to operate. Examples include but are not limited to heating and air conditioning units, electrical generators, water pumps, ventilation systems, and air/water chillers.

Applies to any development over two stories in height adjacent to single-family residential zoning; the mid-block portion may transition up to four stories not to exceed 56 feet. A landscape buffer of 20 feet may be required as determined by the administrative official.

Downtown/Riverfront/Midtown Overlay \u20.frontNote: Setbacks. The setback shall be determined by the existing adjacent structure(s). It will be permitted to vary the setback up to five feet from the average of the existing structure.
Downtown/Riverfront/Midtown Overlay \u20.note: Schedule U, § 3.0.E.6 (Figure K), a single building within an existing built-out block. No height, lot area, side, rear or coverage figure printed.

Marina Isle (within the Downtown/Riverfr.note: Schedule U, § 3.0.B: "The maximum height of structures on Marina Isle is 90 feet as measured from sidewalk grade to the rooftop including attics, mechanical equipment and raised basements.

Sanford Residential Historic District (h.note: Schedule S, § 9.0.C, Residential lot layout: "Setbacks: Setbacks apply to both principal and accessory structures. Residential lot development shall have the following setbacks: Front yard: 25 feet; Rear yard: 2 feet; Side yard: 5 feet; when a side yard is located adjacent to a street, the side yard setback shall be 7 1/2 feet.

mary_esther.name: City of Mary Esther
mary_esther.source: PRIMARY: Land Development Code (Supp. No. 11, Jan. 2026), Article 7 "Land Use, Type, Density, Intensity, Zoning and Regulatory Controls", Secs. 7.14.00 General

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 7.15.01.J.2 — R-1 setbacks, other low density residential areas [PDF p. 137]
equip.text: All houses in the City located on residential building lots shall have a setback of twenty-five (25) feet from the front lot line, seven and a half (7 1/2) feet from the side lot line and twenty (20) feet from the rear lot line. No structure shall be permitted nearer than fifteen (15) feet to the side street line of any corner lot; a side street line shall be that line opposite a side of the dwelling located thereon other than the front of the dwelling. Eaves, steps, fire places and compressors slabs shall not be considered as a part of the building; however, this shall not be construed to permit any portion of a building to encroach upon another lot or the required front yard.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 7.15.02.J.2 — R-2 setbacks, other residential areas [PDF p. 140]
equip.text: All houses in the City located on residential building lots shall have a setback of twenty-five (25) feet from the front lot line, seven and a half (7 1/2) feet from the side lot line and twenty (20) feet from the rear lot line. No structure shall be permitted nearer than fifteen (15) feet to the side street line of any corner lot; a side street line shall be that line opposite a side of the dwelling located thereon other than the front of the dwelling. Eaves, steps, fire places and compressors slabs shall not be considered as a part of the building; however, this shall not be construed to permit any portion of a building to encroach upon another lot.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 7.15.01.J.3 — Accessory structures (all low density residential areas) [PDF p. 138]
equip.text: In all low density residential areas in the City, a detached garage or other detached structure whose dimensions equal or exceed two hundred (200) square feet may be constructed to within seven and a half (7 1/2) feet of the side and rear lot lines provided the minimum front setback of the structure is seventy (70) feet from the front property line. Small utility sheds (under two hundred (200) square feet), screen pool enclosures, cabanas, greenhouses and the like may be constructed to within three and a half (3 1/2) feet of the side and rear lot lines. Attached and detached open carports may be constructed to the side lot line. Additionally, attached and detached open carports may be constructed to within five (5) feet of the front yard lot line. At no time shall the side(s) or front of the carport be enclosed without a permit from the City. A permit is required for an attached or detached carport regardless of size. No other accessory structure including fences shall extend forward of the front of the dwelling or encroach into the required front yard.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 7.15.02.J.4 — R-2 Accessory Structures [PDF p. 141]
equip.text: For single-family and duplex structures within this district, the regulations in Section 7.15.01 apply. All accessory structures, except parking lots, must conform to requirements for a principle structure in this district. Parking lots may be located within ten feet of side and rear lot lines, if such lots lines do not abut the R-1 district, in which case the setback shall be 20 feet.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 9.06.01 — Accessory Structures and Uses, General Standards and Requirements [PDF p. 192]
equip.text: Any number of different accessory structures may be located on a parcel, provided that the following requirements are met: A. There shall be a permitted principal development on the parcel, located in full compliance with all standards and requirements of this Code. B. All accessory structures shall comply with standards pertaining to the principal use, unless exempted or superseded elsewhere in this Code. C. Accessory structures shall not be located in a required buffer, landscape area or minimum building setback area. D. Accessory structures shall be included in all calculations of impervious surface and storm water runoff. E. Accessory structures shall be shown on any concept development plan with full supporting documentation.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 9.06.03 — Storage Buildings, Utility Buildings, Greenhouses [PDF p. 194]
equip.text: A. No accessory buildings used for industrial storage of hazardous, incendiary, noxious or pernicious materials shall be located nearer than one hundred (100) feet from any property line. B. Storage buildings, greenhouses and the like shall be permitted only in compliance with standards for distance between buildings and setbacks, if any, from property lines. C. Storage and other buildings regulated by this section shall be permitted only in side and rear yards, and shall not encroach into any required building setback from an abutting right-of-way. D. Storage and other buildings regulated by this section shall be included in calculations for impervious surface, floor area ratio, or any other site design requirements applying to the principal use of the lot. E. Vehicles, including manufactured housing and mobile homes, shall not be used as storage buildings, utility buildings or other such uses.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 9.06.04.B — Swimming Pools, Location (nearest analogue to a mechanical-equipment pad rule) [PDF p. 194]
equip.text: Location. A swimming pool, regardless of depth, may be located in the side or rear yard only and shall comply with the following. No portion of a swimming pool outside a building shall be located at a distance less than seven and one-half (7 1/2) feet from a building measured from the outermost part of vertical construction of the building to the water's edge. No portion of a swimming pool outside a building to include pumps, filters, and ancillary equipment shall be located at a distance less than seven and one-half (7 1/2) feet from any side or rear property line measured from the property line to the water's edge. A certified original boundary survey and foundation survey may be required by the City of the applicant to ensure compliance with the location and setbacks of the swimming pool.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 7.14.02 — Encroachment of Yard or Open Space [PDF p. 134]
equip.text: The minimum yards and other open space provisions contained in this ordinance for each and every building hereinafter erected or structurally altered, shall not be encroached upon or considered as yard or open space requirements for any other building.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 7.14.01 — Compliance with Code [PDF p. 134]
equip.text: No principal or accessory building, structure or use shall be erected, reconstructed or structurally altered, extended or enlarged while such building, structure or use does not comply with all applicable regulations established by this Code including parking, landscaping and all other Performance Standards for the location in which the building, structure or land is situated.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 7.15.03.I.3 and I.4 — C-1 rear and side yards; accessory structures [PDF p. 144]
equip.text: 3. Rear Yard: There is no rear yard requirement except where a rear yard abuts a residential district, then the rear yard shall have a depth of not less than fifteen (15) feet from a residential district. There is no setback requirements for accessory buildings except where the property abuts a residential district, then the accessory buildings must be set back fifteen (15) feet from the rear property line. The builder or owner must leave ample space for a fire lane for access to the rear of the building and for off-street parking. 4. Side Yard: There is no side yard setback required unless the development parcel abuts a residential district, in which case the setback is fifteen (15) feet. This setback applies to all improvements to the commercial property, including parking and accessory structures but not including landscaping.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 7.15.03.I.6.b — C-1/C-2 screening of outdoor equipment [PDF p. 145]
equip.text: b. (1) For all other areas of the property, all storage of parts; supplies; raw materials; items for disposal, equipment, vehicles, vessels and trailers being serviced or repaired; or products shall be screened with a masonry wall or fence of solid-faced construction and sufficient in height to screen from view by a person off premises and shall not be less than six (6) feet in height or more than eight (8) feet in height; or (2) Stored in a permitted fully enclosed building or structure.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 7.15.05.F — PL district yards [PDF p. 148]
equip.text: 1. No parking area shall be located within ten (10) feet of any residentially zoned property. 2. No structure, (except benches, tables, sitting areas, fountains, fences, or walls) as hereinafter provided, shall be located within twenty-five (25) feet of any property line.

equip.cite: LDC Sec. 9.06.05.B — Fences [PDF p. 195]
equip.text: Fences or hedges may be located in all side and rear yard setback areas. Each fence located in the side and rear yard setbacks shall not exceed the height of eight (8) feet.

equip.cite: Code of Ordinances Sec. 21-43(b) — Appurtenant buildings [PDF p. 435]
equip.text: All nonsubdivision property shall be as provided for herein which shall require all such appurtenant buildings to have a setback of a minimum of ten (10) feet from the back lot line and seven and one-half (7 1/2) feet from the side lot line unless it is for buildings located south of U.S. Highway 98 which shall have a setback as provided for in section 21-52 which was passed on February 8, 1973, and adopted that date.

equip.cite: Code of Ordinances Sec. 21-101 — Definitions, wireless communication facilities (only 'generator' text in either document that is not about litter) [PDF p. 447]
equip.text: Accessory equipment building shall mean any building, cabinet or equipment enclosure constructed for the primary purpose of housing the electronics, backup power, power generators and other freestanding equipment associated with the operation of antennas.

equip.cite: Code of Ordinances Sec. 21-105 — Accessory equipment building (wireless facilities only) [PDF p. 454]
equip.text: Accessory equipment buildings used in conjunction with the operation and maintenance of antennas shall be permitted subject to the following requirements: (a) Shall not exceed seven hundred fifty (750) sq. ft. of gross floor area per provider; (b) If ground constructed or mounted, shall not exceed twenty (20) feet in height; (c) Shall be located within close proximity, as is reasonably possible, to the structure upon which the antennas are attached; (d) If ground constructed or mounted, shall meet the underlying zoning district setback requirements for accessory structures; (e) Shall be designed, constructed, and installed in compliance with all applicable local building codes.... (g) If ground constructed or mounted shall meet the landscaping requirements of section 21-104(i) of this article.

R-1 Single-Family Residential District -.note: Land Development Code. Density: maximum 5.51 units per acre (7.15.01.F). Lot size (7.15.01.G): minimum width 50 ft measured at the minimum front setback line, total lot area not less than 7,500 sq ft; on dead-end cul-de-sac lots the width may be reduced but in no case less than 40 ft measured at the top of the arc of the minimum front setback line, area still not less than 7,500 sq ft.

R-2 - Medium Density Residential Distric.frontNote: On every lot or parcel, there shall be a front yard (setback) of not less than twenty-five (25) feet. However, if the parcel abuts an arterial roadway, the minimum front yard shall be thirty-five (35) feet from the adjacent right-of-way of said arterial.
R-2 - Medium Density Residential Distric.note: Land Development Code. Row for single-family / two-family (duplex) development in R-2. Density: maximum 10 units per acre (7.15.02.F). Lot width (7.15.02.G): 50 ft for one- or two-family dwelling units measured at the minimum front setback line; 100 ft for a multiple family dwelling lot or project parcel; in all cases minimum width at the street right-of-way line not less than 40 ft.

R-2 (townhouse or row house).note: Land Development Code, Sec. 7.15.02.D (site plan provisions for townhouse / row house developments): maximum 10 units per acre; minimum lot width 20 ft; minimum lot size 1,600 sq ft per unit; no townhouse or row house complex, part thereof, or accessory building constructed within 20 ft of any other such complex, part or accessory building; no more than 6 contiguous units in a row.

R-2 (zero lot-line, patio and cluster ho.note: Land Development Code, Sec. 7.15.02.G: 'Zero lot-line, patio, and cluster homes shall provide a minimum forty (40) foot wide lot at the minimum front setback line. In all cases minimum width at the street right-of-way line shall be not less than forty (40) feet.

C-1 Limited Commercial.frontNote: On every lot or parcel, there shall be a front yard (setback) of not less than fifty (50) feet. No building, structure, accessory structure, fence, wall, seating or other use is permitted within the front setback or forward of the building unless otherwise authorized by this code. Parking is permitted in the setback but not including parking garages.
C-1 Limited Commercial.sideNote: There is no side yard setback required unless the development parcel abuts a residential district, in which case the setback is fifteen (15) feet. This setback applies to all improvements to the commercial property, including parking and accessory structures but not including landscaping.
C-1 Limited Commercial.rearNote: There is no rear yard requirement except where a rear yard abuts a residential district, then the rear yard shall have a depth of not less than fifteen (15) feet from a residential district. There is no setback requirements for accessory buildings except where the property abuts a residential district, then the accessory buildings must be set back fifteen (15) feet from the rear property line.
C-1 Limited Commercial.heightNote: Except for elevated municipal water storage facilities, no building or structure inclusive of all roof top appurtenances, shall exceed the building height limits as set forth in exhibit A.... From Doolittle Boulevard in a north and south straight line extension to the westernmost City limits, no building or structure shall exceed eighty (80) feet in height above mean sea level (MSL).
C-1 Limited Commercial.note: Land Development Code. Height is zone-dependent (80/90/100 ft above MSL for Zones A/B/C) so no single height number is printed for the district. Structures south of U.S. Highway 98 (7.15.03.I.1): side lot line 7 1/2 ft, rear lot line 20 ft; properties bordering U.S. Highway 98 a minimum of 50 ft from the back of the curb regardless of structure orientation.

C-2 General Commercial District.sideNote: There is no side yard setback required unless the development parcel abuts a residential district, in which case the setback is fifteen (15) feet. This setback applies to all improvements to the commercial property, including parking and accessory structures but not including landscaping.
C-2 General Commercial District.rearNote: There is no rear yard requirement except where a rear yard abuts a residential district, then the rear yard shall have a depth of not less than fifteen (15) feet from a residential district. There is no setback requirements for accessory buildings except where the property abuts a residential district, then the accessory buildings must be set back fifteen (15) feet from the rear property line.
C-2 General Commercial District.note: Land Development Code. C-2 prints no dimensional standards of its own. Sec. 7.15.04.C: 'All other regulations and provisions of the C-1 district (Section 7.15.03) govern developments within the C-2 district.' The figures shown are therefore the C-1 figures carried by that express incorporation clause, not inferred. C-2 height is likewise the Zone A/B/C limits of 80/90/100 ft above MSL. Sec.

PL Public Land District.note: Land Development Code, Sec. 7.15.05.F Yards: '1. No parking area shall be located within ten (10) feet of any residentially zoned property. 2. No structure, (except benches, tables, sitting areas, fountains, fences, or walls) as hereinafter provided, shall be located within twenty-five (25) feet of any property line. 3.

PUD Planned Unit Development District.frontNote: Dimensional and Bulk Regulations: The location of all proposed building sites shall be shown on the final development plan.
PUD Planned Unit Development District.sideNote: Dimensional and Bulk Regulations: The location of all proposed building sites shall be shown on the final development plan.
PUD Planned Unit Development District.rearNote: Dimensional and Bulk Regulations: The location of all proposed building sites shall be shown on the final development plan.
PUD Planned Unit Development District.heightNote: Except for elevated municipal water storage facilities, no building or structure shall exceed three (3) stories above a ground floor parking area or 45 feet in height above the highest natural elevation of the property to the bottom of the cornice line, whichever is less.
PUD Planned Unit Development District.note: Land Development Code. A PUD is a free-standing district whose own approved development plan sets lot size, lot coverage, setbacks, off-street parking, bulk, type of dwelling and density (7.15.06.B.5); no front/side/rear yard numbers are printed.

PMDD Planned Mixed Development District.frontNote: Dimensional and Bulk Regulations: The location of all proposed building sites shall be shown on the Final Development Plan, subject to minimum lot sizes, setback lines, as specified in the Master Plan and approved by the City Council.
PMDD Planned Mixed Development District.sideNote: Dimensional and Bulk Regulations: The location of all proposed building sites shall be shown on the Final Development Plan, subject to minimum lot sizes, setback lines, as specified in the Master Plan and approved by the City Council.
PMDD Planned Mixed Development District.rearNote: Dimensional and Bulk Regulations: The location of all proposed building sites shall be shown on the Final Development Plan, subject to minimum lot sizes, setback lines, as specified in the Master Plan and approved by the City Council.
PMDD Planned Mixed Development District.heightNote: Except for elevated municipal water storage facilities no building or structure inclusive of all roof top appurtenances, shall exceed the building height limits as set forth in exhibit A.... no building or structure shall exceed eighty (80) feet in height above mean sea level (MSL) [Zone A];... ninety (90) feet... [Zone B];... one-hundred (100) feet... [Zone C].
PMDD Planned Mixed Development District.note: Land Development Code. Minimum frontage width (7.15.07.D.1): 'The development parcel shall have a minimum frontage width of one hundred (100) feet on a public roadway to be considered for Planned Mix Use Development.' Density/intensity (7.15.07.D.3): maximum 20 units per gross acre and maximum 1.92 Floor Area Ratio.

Residential zone \u2014 R1 / R2 (Code of.frontNote: All houses in the residential zone erected in the city shall have a setback from the side lot line of seven and one-half (7 1/2) feet, thirty-five (35) feet from the street line and one hundred (100) feet from the water line and there shall be twenty (20) feet between houses on the same lot.
Residential zone \u2014 R1 / R2 (Code of.note: SECOND DOCUMENT — Code of Ordinances, Chapter 21 ZONING (not the Land Development Code). This is the older 1947-1990 zoning text that remains codified alongside the LDC. Sec. 21-52 prints 35 ft from the street line (the LDC prints 25 ft front for R-1 and R-2); LDC Sec. 7.07.02 provides that where there is conflict between the LDC and the cited Code of Ordinances chapters, the LDC takes precedence. Sec.

High Density Residential Areas \u2014 to.note: SECOND DOCUMENT — Code of Ordinances, Chapter 21, Division 3 'High Density Residential Areas'. Sec. 21-61(a): maximum 10 townhouse units per acre; minimum lot width 20 ft; minimum lot size 1,600 sq ft per unit; no townhouse complex or accessory building within 20 ft of any other townhouse complex or accessory building; no more than 6 contiguous townhouses in a row; each unit on its own platted lot.

PUD (cluster housing) (Code of Ordinance.frontNote: There shall be no yard requirements for dwellings located within a PUD except that the main structure together with any accessory buildings shall not occupy more than two-thirds of any platted lot.
PUD (cluster housing) (Code of Ordinance.sideNote: There shall be no yard requirements for dwellings located within a PUD except that the main structure together with any accessory buildings shall not occupy more than two-thirds of any platted lot.
PUD (cluster housing) (Code of Ordinance.rearNote: There shall be no yard requirements for dwellings located within a PUD except that the main structure together with any accessory buildings shall not occupy more than two-thirds of any platted lot.
PUD (cluster housing) (Code of Ordinance.note: SECOND DOCUMENT — Code of Ordinances, Chapter 21, Sec. 21-61(b). CAUTION: the coverage value 66.67 is my decimal rendering of the ordinance's printed 'two-thirds' and is arithmetic, not the ordinance's own figure — the ordinance prints the words 'two-thirds (%)' (the fraction glyph is corrupted in the published text as '%'). Height per Sec. 21-62 is 2 1/2 stories or 35 feet.

C-1 limited commercial / C-2 general com.rearNote: There is no rear yard requirement except where a rear yard abuts a residential district, then the rear yard shall have a depth of not less than fifteen (15) feet from a residential district. There is no setback requirements for accessory buildings except where the property abuts a residential district, then the accessory buildings must be set back fifteen (15) feet from the rear property line.
C-1 limited commercial / C-2 general com.note: SECOND DOCUMENT — Code of Ordinances, Chapter 21, Division 4. Sec. 21-84: buildings in C-1 and C-2 shall not exceed 35 ft in height, exclusive of skeletal tower structures for television/telephone/radio transmission or any appurtenance necessary for facilities and utilities — this conflicts with the LDC's 80/90/100 ft MSL Zone A/B/C limits and is superseded by the LDC (Sec. 7.07.02). Sec.

new_port_richey.name: City of New Port Richey
new_port_richey.source: Code of Ordinances, Appendix A—Land Development Code, Chapter 7 (Zoning) §§ 7.01.00—7.24.00; Chapter 12 (Accessory Uses) §§ 12.01.00—12.05.00; Chapter 2 (Defini

equip.cite: App. A LDC § 2.01.00, definition of "Setback" [PDF p.1115]
equip.text: Setback: The required yard (see definition for yard), or the distance between the lot line and the line of a building or any projection thereof, excluding uncovered steps, mechanical units, and architectural features such as bay windows, columns, trellises, and similar structures which create a theme or design highlighting the principle structure, provided none of the aforementioned excluded items shall encroach into the front or rear yard setback more than five (5) feet or into the side yard setback more than three (3) feet.

equip.cite: App. A LDC § 2.01.00, definition of "Accessory use" [PDF p.1087]
equip.text: Accessory use: A use of land or structure or portion thereof customarily incidental and subordinate to the principal use of the land or structure and located on the same parcel with the principal use.

equip.cite: App. A LDC § 2.01.00, definition of "Structure" [PDF p.1118]
equip.text: Structure: A combination of materials to form a construction for use, installed on, above or below the surface of land or water. For purposes of this code, unless otherwise defined, a structure is any material as defined herein which exceeds a height of twelve (12) inches above grade level excluding mail boxes, decorative statues, fountains, flag poles, lampposts, and landscaping structures such as trellises and planters.

equip.cite: App. A LDC § 2.01.00, definition of "Yard" [PDF p.1120]
equip.text: Yard: An open area between building(s), structure(s), or use(s) and the adjoining lot line unoccupied and unobstructed by any building structure or use from the ground up except as otherwise provided in this code.

equip.cite: App. A LDC § 2.01.00, definition of "Yard, waterfront" [PDF p.1121]
equip.text: Yard, waterfront: A yard required on waterfront property with a depth measured perpendicular to the centerline of the seawall or waterside lot line for non-seawalled lots.

equip.cite: App. A LDC § 12.01.00 Purpose [PDF p.1373]
equip.text: Accessory uses are those structures, buildings or uses which are incidental to the principal or main use of a parcel of land. Accessory uses regulated in this section include satellite television dishes, detached storage or other buildings, greenhouses, swimming pools and fences. The purpose of this section is to establish standards necessary to promote and protect the public health, safety and welfare while allowing the development of accessory uses. Standards are established to protect adjacent property owners and properties from potential adverse impacts.

equip.cite: App. A LDC § 12.02.00 General standards [PDF p.1373]
equip.text: Any number of accessory uses may be located on a parcel, subject to the following standards: 1. There must be a permitted principle development on the parcel located in full compliance with all standards of this Code. 2. All accessory uses must comply with all standards of this Code pertaining to a principal use, unless specifically exempted elsewhere in this Code. 3. Accessory uses shall not be located in a required buffer area nor a minimum building setback area. 4. Accessory uses shall be included in impervious surface calculations and stormwater runoff calculations. 5. Accessory uses shall be indicated on any concept plan or site plan with full supporting documentation as required by this code.

equip.cite: App. A LDC § 12.03.00(3) Detached storage buildings and greenhouses [PDF p.1374]
equip.text: a. Detached storage buildings and greenhouses may be permitted in all land use categories, provided all standards and provisions are followed. b. Detached storage buildings and greenhouses shall be permitted only in side and rear yards and shall not encroach into any required building setback from an abutting road or property line. c. Detached storage buildings and greenhouses may be permitted in compliance with the standards for minimum distance between buildings. d. Detached storage buildings and greenhouses shall not exceed fifteen (15) feet in height.

equip.cite: App. A LDC § 7.22.01 Easements [PDF p.1275]
equip.text: Unless otherwise provided for in this land development code, no structure can be constructed or erected on or within a recorded easement, exclusive of portable items which can easily be removed such as, but not limited to, playground equipment and lawn furniture.

equip.cite: App. A LDC § 7.22.02 Impervious surface area [PDF p.1275]
equip.text: Unless otherwise specified in this code, no more than sixty (60) percent of residential lots and seventy (70) percent of commercial lots shall be covered with paving or other types of impervious surfaces, including structures. A waiver to this requirement can be granted by the city council.

equip.cite: App. A LDC § 12.05.00(6)(g) Downtown Zoning District fences [PDF p.1382]
equip.text: Privacy fences used to screen dumpsters, heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) units or other ancillary equipment, for commercial purposes, are permitted in the Downtown Zoning District. Such fences are limited to six (6) feet in height and must be fully opaque. Such fences shall be constructed of PVC or masonry material and designed to match the principal structure on the property.

equip.cite: App. A LDC § 7.27.04(f)(iv), (vi), (vii) Multi-Family site design standards [PDF pp.1297—1298]
equip.text: (iv) Service and utility areas are encouraged to be located inside the building or integrated into the architecture of the building. However, if service and utility areas are located externally to the building, they shall be enclosed or screened from the public view with fencing, walls, and/or landscaping.... (vi) Utilities shall be buried and located at the rear or side lot lines. Meters and transformers shall be placed at the side or rear of lots and screened from public view with fencing, walls, and/or landscaping. (vii) Roof mounted mechanical equipment, other than vents or ventilators, shall be screened from ground level view. The screening shall be as high as the height of the equipment and shall be integrated with the exterior building design.

equip.cite: App. A LDC § 8.01.01 Buffer matrix description [PDF p.1302]
equip.text: A 100 feet 25' — Six (6) foot high fence, four (4) canopy trees thirty-three (33) feet apart at centerline, continuous shrub. B 100 feet 20' — Six (6) foot high fence, three (3) canopy trees fifty (50) feet apart at centerline, continuous shrub. C 100 feet 15' — Three (3) canopy trees, fifty (50) feet apart at centerline, continuous shrub. D 100 feet 10' — Three (3) canopy trees, fifty (50) feet apart at centerline. E 100 feet 5' — Continuous shrub. [These are the buffer widths the commercial, office and industrial districts cross-reference as their rear and side setback where a property abuts a different land use district.]

equip.cite: App. A LDC § 10.02.00 Free vision zones [PDF p.1353]
equip.text: 3. A free vision zone is defined as that area of each corner located at each street intersection which is formed by commencing at the extreme point or middle of the arc where the outside edge of two (2) intersecting streets meet and thence proceeding along the outside edge of each such intersecting street a distance of thirty (30) feet to separate positions and thence proceeding along a diagonal line which shall connect the separate positions, all of which shall give the general appearance of a triangular area. 4. It shall be unlawful for any person, firm, corporation, business enterprise or other entity to erect, plant or allow to grow any hedge, fence, wall, vegetation or any other obstruction to vision, other than a single post or tree, which is higher than three (3) feet above ground level within any such free vision zone.

equip.cite: Land Development Code § 7.09.02.B.1, Mechanical equipment [LDC PDF pp.262-263]
equip.text: Mechanical equipment. Outdoor mechanical equipment, such as heating, air conditioning, and ventilation systems, must be placed on the roof, in the rear or to the side of the building, or otherwise visually screened. In no case shall mechanical equipment be located between the principal structure and the front property line or any property line facing a right-of-way. All mechanical equipment located on the roof shall not be visible from adjacent properties or rights-of-way from heights equal to or less than the equipment. All mechanical equipment located in the rear or to the side of the building shall be enclosed by opaque fence, wall or hedge a minimum of six feet in height or to the highest point of the equipment, whichever is lower. For air conditioning or other equipment requiring airflow, a lattice screen of at least 50 percent opacity shall be sufficient to meet this requirement. [Applicability, § 7.09.02.B: "This section shall apply to all development located within the MDR-V, MDR-HI, HDR, CBN, CG, CL, CTS, CBR, ROI-GD, ROI-TD, CMU, NHMU, SHMU, HIMU, TCMU, GRMU, IN, A, INST and REC zoning designations."]

equip.cite: Land Development Code § 7.09.02.B.4, Parking, loading or accessway areas [LDC PDF p.263]
equip.text: Parking, loading or accessway areas. Areas used or set aside for parking, loading, accessways or service and utility areas shall not be located within ten feet of the property line when such property line abuts single-family, duplex, townhouse or multi-family uses.

equip.cite: Land Development Code § 7.09.02.B.10.m, Luxury recreational vehicle (RV) resorts - Noise [LDC PDF p.266]
equip.text: Noise: Recreational vehicles shall not be maneuvered on-site after 10:00 p.m. or before 6:00 a.m. Power generators shall not be operated within fifty feet (50') of residential areas unless there is a declared emergency.

equip.cite: Land Development Code § 7.09.02.B.13.a.1, Electric distribution substation and electric transmission substation [LDC PDF pp.267-268]
equip.text: Minimum setback from the property line to any permanent equipment structure: 100 feet from any lot line where the adjoining lot is zoned for residential use and 50 feet from any lot line where the adjoining lot is zoned for any nonresidential use. The setback requirement along all public or private rights-of-way shall be based on the zoning of the property on the opposite side of the right-of-way as if there were no intervening right-of-way. The setback requirement of this subsection applies to all buildings and structures, including but not limited to transformers, breakers, buses, switch houses, relays, switches, regulators, and capacitors. The setback requirements do not apply to poles and pole anchoring devices.

equip.cite: Land Development Code § 7.09.03.1.f.1, Supplemental setback and buffering requirements from single-family, duplex, or townhome uses [LDC PDF p.274]
equip.text: All development located in the NHMU, HIMU, CG, HDR, and TCMU zoning designations that abut single-family, duplex or townhome uses located in zoning designations different from the previously mentioned designations shall meet the following supplemental setbacks and buffers requirements: 1. Setbacks. Any portion of a building that abuts single-family, duplex or townhome uses shall provide a setback from those uses that is the greater of one foot for every foot in height (e.g. 160-foot tall project will have an 160-foot setback). 2. Buffers.... a. Areas used or set aside for parking, loading, accessways, or service and utility areas shall not be located within 20 feet of the property line when such property line abuts single-family, duplex or townhome uses.

equip.cite: Land Development Code § 7.12.09.C and E, Compliance with dimensional requirements [LDC PDF p.324]
equip.text: C. Rear property line setback requirements do not apply to boat docks, piers, bulkheads (seawalls) or boathouses. For waterfront lots the rear property line setbacks do not apply.... E. The footprint for all structures shall meet all setback requirements; however, cornices, canopies, eaves, garden windows, exterior stairways or other architectural features may extend 24 inches into the required setback provided the extension does not interfere with access to the property. Bay windows, balconies, and portions or projections from a building or structure that add to the gross floor area are not allowed to extend into the required setback.

equip.cite: Land Development Code § 9.06.01, Accessory structures and uses - General standards and requirements [LDC PDF p.506]
equip.text: Any number of different accessory structures may be located on a parcel, provided that the following requirements are met: A. There shall be a permitted principal development on the parcel, located in full compliance with all standards and requirements of this Code, except that boat docks may be permitted prior to construction of [the] principal structure when submitted as part of a master plan which shows the location of the principal structure. B. All accessory structures shall comply with standards pertaining to the principal use, unless exempted or superseded elsewhere in this Code. C. Accessory structures shall not be located in a required buffer, landscape area or minimum building setback area. D. Accessory structures shall be included in all calculations of impervious surface and stormwater runoff. E. Accessory structures shall be shown on any concept development plan with full supporting documentation.

equip.cite: Land Development Code § 9.06.03, Storage buildings, utility buildings, greenhouses [LDC PDF p.507]
equip.text: A. No accessory buildings used for industrial storage of hazardous, incendiary, noxious or pernicious materials shall be located nearer than 100 feet from any property line. B. All accessory buildings shall meet the minimum yard setback requirements for the district in which they are located. C. Storage and other buildings regulated by this section shall not be permitted between the principal structure and the right-of-way, and shall not encroach into any required building setback. Exception: When a storage building or other building regulated by this section is setback from the right-of-way a distance equal to or greater than the width of the lot frontage of the property upon which the building is located and the building is visually screened from the right-of-way, this building may be permitted between the principal structure and the right-of-way.

equip.cite: Land Development Code § 7.20.04.C, Small-scale alternative energy generation regulations [LDC PDF p.366]
equip.text: No portion of a small-scale solar and wind energy conversion systems shall be located between the principle building and front property line, along any street frontage, or within any required setback area. [§ 7.20.02 Applicability: "The provisions of this Section shall apply to the following accessory uses as they are defined in Article 3.00.01 of this Code: A. Energy Conversion Systems, Small-scale Solar. B. Energy Conversion Systems, Small-scale Wind." Standby/emergency generators are not within this section.]

equip.cite: Code of Ordinances § 14-56(7) and (18), Exemptions (noise) [Code of Ordinances PDF p.371]
equip.text: The provisions of section 14-54 shall not apply to the following sounds:... (7) Generators used during or as a result of an emergency.... (18) Air conditioners are exempt from all provisions of this article when the equipment is functioning in accord with the manufacturer's specifications and with all manufacturer's standard mufflers and noise-reducing equipment in use and in proper operating condition according to standards promulgated by the American Refrigeration Institute.

equip.cite: Code of Ordinances § 14-55(a)(2)a.-b., Measurement or assessment of noise [Code of Ordinances PDF p.370]
equip.text: a. Residential properties abutting residential properties: i. Time: At all times of the day. ii. Distance: Noise or noise disturbances shall not be plainly audible at a distance more than the setbacks of the underlying Zoning District for the abutting property line. b. Non-residential properties abutting residential properties: i. Time: Noise disturbances shall not be allowed between 10:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m. ii. Distance: Noise or noise disturbances shall not be plainly audible at a distance more than the setbacks of the underlying residential zoning district for the abutting property line of the source.

equip.cite: Code of Ordinances § 14-63(a), Exemptions in SHMU only [Code of Ordinances PDF p.374]
equip.text: Air conditioners are exempt from provisions of Table I of this article when this equipment is functioning in accord with the manufacturer's specifications and with all manufacturer's standard mufflers and noise-reducing equipment in use and in proper operating condition according to standards promulgated by the American Refrigeration Institute. The same exception shall apply to lawn mowers, agricultural equipment and homeowners' mechanized tools during daylight hours.

gen.cite: Sec. 285-10, Emergency generators in residential districts [PDF p.1362]
gen.text: (A) Emergency generators and associated fuel tanks which operate with liquid propane or natural gas for fuel shall be permitted as accessory structures to single-family detached dwellings and two-family (duplex) dwellings, as provided in this article. (B) Generators are not permitted in a front yard. Generators not to exceed five (5) feet in height are permitted in side and rear yards with a minimum ten-foot setback to any side lot line, a minimum ten-foot setback to any rear lot line adjacent to a public alley or street line, and a minimum fifteen-foot setback to any other rear lot line. (C) Above-ground liquid propane tanks are not permitted in a front yard or side yard. A maximum of two (2) above-ground tanks with a maximum collective capacity of five hundred (500) gallons and a maximum height of five and one-half (5½) feet are permitted in the rear yard subject to the same setback requirements that apply to generators in subsection (B), above. (D) One (1) underground propane tank is permitted in lieu of any above-ground tank, or in combination with no more than one (1) above-ground tank, provided that the collective capacity of the underground tank and any above-ground tank shall not exceed five hundred (500) gallons. An underground tank is permitted only in the front or rear yard, if a minimum twenty-five-foot setback is provided to any street line and a minimum ten-foot setback is provided to any lot line. (E) Above-ground storage tanks shall be screened with an opaque fence at least six (6) inches higher than the top of any portion of the tank. (F) A generator located in an interior side yard and situated between two (2) dwellings shall be positioned to direct exhaust toward the rear yard. (G) Generators and fuel tanks shall not be located in any easement. (H) Any generator with a noise rating on its specifications sheet exceeding seventy (70) db (decibels) at a distance of twenty-three (23) feet is prohibited. (Ord. No. 2010-20, § 2(Exh. A), 9-14-10; Ord. No. 2021-007, § 2, 1-26-21).

gen.cite: Sec. 285-20, Emergency generators in nonresidential districts [PDF p.1363]
gen.text: (A) Emergency generators and associated fuel tanks which operate with liquid propane or natural gas for fuel are permitted as accessory structures to commercial, industrial, institutional, and other nonresidential uses, as provided in this section. (B) Generators and above-ground fuel tanks are not permitted in a front yard. (C) Generators and fuel tanks shall be set back a minimum of twenty-five (25) feet from street lines and any shared property line with a residentially zoned lot, and fifteen (15) feet from all other property lines. (D) Generators and above-ground fuel tanks must be screened from view from all streets and residentially zoned lots using landscaping, fencing or masonry walls, to a height of at least six (6) inches higher than the top of any portion of the generator and tank. (E) Generators and fuel tanks shall not be located in any easement. (F) Any generator with a noise rating on its specifications sheet exceeding seventy (70) db (decibels) at a distance of twenty-three (23) feet is prohibited. (G) Proposed generators, fuel tanks, or both that cannot be installed in compliance with this section may be proposed as special exception uses. (Ord. No. 2010-20, § 2(Exh. A), 9-14-10; Ord. No. 2016-021, § 3, 10-10-16).

gen.cite: Sec. 215-50(E) and (F), Permitted yard encroachments in the E-1, RS-18000, RS-12000, RS-8000, RS-6000, NBHD-RES, and RD-8000 Districts [PDF p.1273]
gen.text: (E) At-grade air conditioning units, heating units, pool pumps, and related equipment shall not be located in a front yard or within five (5) feet of a side yard lot line. Such devices, and related equipment, may be located in a required rear yard provided a minimum five-foot setback is provided to any property line. Existing air conditioning, heating, and pool equipment that was installed with proper permits, but does not comply with the locational requirements of this section, may be replaced at the same location. Variances from the required yard setbacks for at-grade air conditioning units shall be considered pursuant to Article 620, "Administrative Variances." (F) At-grade generators and fuel tanks may encroach into required yards as provided in section 285-210 (Emergency generator regulations). [Note: the printed cross-reference reads "285-210"; the emergency generator regulations are at sections 285-10 and 285-20.]

equip.cite: Sec. 215-90, Accessory structure setbacks [PDF pp.1275-1276]
equip.text: Certain accessory structures are permitted to encroach into required yards, as follows. All other accessory structures are subject to principal structure setbacks. (A) Accessory buildings and structures in E-1, RS-18000, RS-12000, RS-8000, RS-6000, NBHD-RES, and RD-8000 districts. Accessory buildings and structures are subject to the following requirements: (1) No accessory building or structure shall be located within five (5) feet of a side or rear lot line unless otherwise provided in this code. (2) No accessory building or structure shall be located within a required yard abutting any street line, such as front yards, corner side street yards and through lot rear yards, except as provided in section 215-50 for carports. (3) Any accessory building or structure located closer than ten (10) feet to a principal structure shall be considered attached, and shall comply in all respects with the lot, yard and bulk requirements of this code applicable to the principal structure, and shall not interfere with any part of a lot necessary to comply with parking requirements for the principal use.... (B) Accessory buildings and structures in the RMH District.... (5) At grade air conditioner units, heating units or other mechanical equipment shall not be located in a front yard and may be located in the side or rear yard provided a minimum five foot (5') setback from the side and rear property line is provided.... (C) Accessory buildings and structures in other districts. Accessory structures shall comply with front and side yard requirements for the principal structure to which they are accessory and shall be not closer to any rear property line than ten (10) feet. This subsection does not apply to the CRA form-based zoning districts. (D) [Parking.] Accessory buildings and structures shall not interfere with any part of a lot necessary to comply with parking requirements for the principal use in any zoning district.

equip.cite: Sec. 220-70, Accessory structure height [PDF p.1287]
equip.text: Accessory buildings and structures are subject to the same height limitations as the principal building or structure, provided that within the E-1, RS-18000, RS-12000, RS-8000, RS-6000, RMH, NBHD-RES, and RD-8000 districts, maximum allowable height is ten (10) feet, and up to fourteen (14) feet to the peak of a sloped roof.

equip.cite: Sec. 220-60, Rooftop mechanical equipment [PDF p.1286]
equip.text: (A) New rooftop air conditioning units in residential districts must be located on flat roofs only on the rear one-half (½) of the building, and must be screened from view from adjacent properties. The city may waive this standard as part of site plan approval in the CRA form-based districts if an acceptable design solution effectively hides the equipment from being viewed at street level and in adjacent buildings of the same or lesser height. (B) Property owners are allowed to replace roof air-conditioning units that are not located on the rear one-half (½) of the building, provided the units are painted the same color as the roof or are painted white.

equip.cite: Sec. 275-170(B), Landscape requirements for screening [PDF p.1350]
equip.text: (B) Equipment. Dumpsters, dumpster enclosures, mechanical equipment and electrical transformers shall be screened on at least three (3) sides by landscape material that is a minimum of thirty (30) inches in height.

equip.cite: Sec. 307-30(D) and (E), Screening requirements; treatment of dumpsters, loading areas and mechanical equipment (CRA form-based districts) [PDF p.1435]
equip.text: (D) Utility boxes and machinery, including, but not limited to, backflow devices, electric meters, air conditioning units, and transformer boxes, shall not be visible from public rights-of-way, parks and other public spaces. equip.cite: Sec. 205-14(e)(10), Additional design standards for properties fronting Griffin Road, Stirling Road, Sheridan Street, Bryan Road and Anglers Avenue/Ravenswood Road [PDF p.1255]

gen.cite: Equipment encroachment into required yards — LDR Ch. 26, Art. 7
gen.text: Generators may sit in a required yard. Generators — with A/C units, pool and solar equipment — may encroach up to 4 ft into a required side yard and up to 4 ft into a required rear yard. Where the yard is 5 ft or less wide, the projection cannot exceed half the yard width. Up to 4 ft into a recorded drainage or utility easement is also allowed, but nothing permanent may sit in an easement in use. Screening, for new construction outside the Special Residential Overlay: the equipment must be screened from view at grade from the public right-of-way by 100% landscaping, a landscaping/fence combination, or an architecturally compatible wall or opaque fence panel — screen no more than 6 ft tall, 8 ft long (or the equipment length, whichever is less) and 4 ft wide.
